It lists the calendar texts only for languages without built-in names: not for en.po and nl.po, nor for regions of English and Dutch, such as en_US.po and nl_BE.po, which need not contain them.

The tasks run go run . translations and go run . translations check, which call App.Translations (see translations.go and the translations package). App.TranslationCatalog() returns the same texts as go-translator's *extract.Catalog, for tools of your own. They parse the templates, so they find every text, also on pages nobody visited, and the running site never writes to its catalogues.

Only literal texts can be found. A call such as {{tl localizer .Status}} is reported as a warning, and updating from the POT file would mark its translations obsolete. Name each possible text in a literal call, for example in a {{define}} that is never used:

{{define "status-texts"}}{{tl localizer "open"}}{{tl localizer "full"}}{{tl localizer "cancelled"}}{{end}}

The modules' default components and e-mail use tl too, so the same files translate them.

Dates, times and money

date, time, dateRange, timeRange, weekday and money write in the page's language:

{{date .Start "full"}}             Sunday 25 October 2026 · zondag 25 oktober 2026
{{time .Start}}                    14:00 (2:00 PM in en-US)
{{money .PriceCents "EUR"}}        €45.00 · € 45,00

Times stored in UTC are shown in the site's timezone (Site settings › Timezone). That field lists the time zones by name, each with its current offset from UTC, such as "Europe/Amsterdam (UTC+02:00)". English and Dutch month and day names and date patterns are built in; en writes the day first and en-US the month first, with a 12-hour clock. Money uses the language's separators in every language.

The site's .po files give the names and patterns of other languages, and can replace the built-in ones of English and Dutch. Each is an English name with a context (msgctxt), so the same word can translate differently, such as "May" the month and "May" its short name:

Context msgids
month January … December
month-short Jan … Dec
day Sunday … Saturday
day-short Sun … Sat
time AM and PM
date the patterns of the styles: short, medium, long, full and time 
msgctxt "month"
msgid "October"
msgstr "Oktober"

msgctxt "date"
msgid "long"
msgstr "d. MMMM y"

With these two entries in de.po, {{date .Start}} writes "25. Oktober 2026" on a German page. An entry replaces the built-in name or pattern in every language, English and Dutch included: a month entry for October in nl.po replaces "oktober". A name or pattern without a translation, or with an empty one, falls back to the built-in one, or to English for a language without built-in names; the same msgid without its context does not count. en.po and nl.po therefore need none of these entries, and other languages need all of them. An entry is found as other texts are, so a date pattern in en.po also replaces the American one of en-US unless en_US.po has its own. dateRange keeps its built-in shorter form, such as "25–27 Oct 2026", only for a style whose pattern is not replaced.

task translations adds all of them to the POT file, so they need no template, with core:calendar (frontend.CalendarReference) as their reference; frontend.CalendarTexts() lists them, and frontend.BuiltInCalendar(locale) reports whether a language has built-in ones. Msgids such as date:long, without a context, are no longer read: move their translations to the date context.

In Go code, such as a module's e-mail, app.Frontend.Format(ctx, locale) writes dates with the same names and patterns. It keeps them per language in a frontend.Calendars, which SetTranslations clears. A frontend.Format of your own with a Lookup looks them up for every date, unless its Calendars field points to a frontend.Calendars it can keep them in.

Template functions describes every style and pattern.

The admin language

The admin has one language for everyone, set in Config.AdminLanguage:

app := webthings.New(webthings.Config{
    AdminLanguage: "nl",
})

English (the default) and Dutch are built in: the admin itself and each section, such as pages, media, the site settings and every module, bring their own catalogue. The messages of the admin's forms, such as "This field is required.", come from go-form's catalogue of the admin language; go-form brings English and Dutch. Texts without a translation are shown in English. The admin's pages name their language in <html lang> as a BCP 47 tag, such as pt-BR for AdminLanguage pt_BR.

To change admin texts, or to add a language, put a catalogue in <StateDir>/translations, such as var/translations/nl.po. The admin reads that folder at start when it exists, and never writes to it. A catalogue serves its language whatever the spelling: nl.po, nl_NL.po and nl-NL.po all serve AdminLanguage nl, and de_DE.po serves de. Its translations win over the built-in ones, which fill in the rest, so it can change any admin text. An entry left empty counts as missing and keeps the built-in translation, so updating the file from a POT file in Poedit is safe. Restart the site after changing the file.

The built-in catalogues are in go-webthings: the admin's own in admin/translations/, with its template translations.pot, and those of the sections in the translations/ folder of their package, such as modules/comments/translations/. For a new language, start from them in Poedit. The admin records no texts while it serves, so what editors type, such as titles and file names, never ends up in a catalogue.

Module titles and navigation groups from main.go, such as "News" or .Group("Website"), are texts like any other: they are shown translated when a catalogue has them, and as written otherwise. The group names Content, Website, Visitors, Communication, Shop and Agenda are built in; add others, and module titles, to a catalogue in <StateDir>/translations.

Dates, times and amounts of money in the admin follow the admin language, with times in the site's timezone.

The admin language is independent of the content languages: a Dutch admin edits English content in the English tab. Modules write e-mail for staff, such as a notification about a new form entry, in the admin language (Env.AdminLanguage).

Guides.Title: Templates
Guides.Summary: The public site is rendered from Go templates: a layout around one content template per screen. This guide covers which template gets which data, how module templates are found, and how to write starting points for them.
Guides.Body:
Where templates live

Config.Templates is the folder with the site's templates, usually os.DirFS("templates"). Each theme is a folder in it (see Themes); the paths in this guide are relative to a theme folder such as templates/default/.

layout.gohtml            wraps every screen; gets frontend.View
page.gohtml              a content page; gets frontend.Page
404.gohtml               the "not found" page; gets frontend.NotFound (optional)
500.gohtml               the page for a failing template (optional)
search.gohtml            the search screen; gets frontend.SearchView (optional)
news/list.gohtml         a module screen, by instance key ...
publishing/post.gohtml   ... or by module type
partials/card.gohtml     snippets every template can use
regions/head.gohtml      the page's tags in <head>; gets frontend.View
regions/menu.gohtml      a part of the layout; gets frontend.View (for HTMX)
fragments/results.gohtml a part of a page; gets the page's content (for HTMX)
mail/                    e-mail templates
assets/site.css          CSS, JavaScript and images, served at /theme/

The layout places a region with {{slot "menu"}}, which HTMX navigation updates along with the content, and a template places a fragment with {{requiredSlot "results"}}, {{slot "results"}} or {{deferredSlot "results"}}, which HTMX can ask for on its own. See HTMX.

Each theme is rendered by frontend.Templates, which uses the render package on top of go-partial. The templates are html/template, so output is escaped for its context. Every template gets the same functions: core's, those of the modules in app.Use, the translation functions of Config.Translations, and your own from Config.Funcs (see Template functions).

The layout, content templates, partials, regions, fragments, components and e-mail templates are parsed once and kept, so restart the site after adding or changing one. While you develop, Config.ReloadTemplates reads them again for every request, and Config.Development shows template errors in the browser (see While you develop). ReloadTemplates also gives a changed file of the theme's assets/ or of Config.Assets a new version, and their tags and the import map then carry no integrity (see Themes).

The layout

layout.gohtml wraps every screen. It gets the whole page context, a frontend.View, and places the content template with {{content}}:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="{{.Locale}}">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    {{slot "head"}}
    {{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}}
</head>
<body>
    <a href="{{.Site.HomeURL}}">
        {{with .Site.LogoURL}}<img src="{{.}}" alt="">{{end}}
        {{.Site.Name}}
    </a>

    <nav>
        {{range .Menu}}
            <a href="{{.URL}}" {{if .Active}}aria-current="page"{{end}}>{{.Title}}</a>
        {{end}}
    </nav>

    {{with .Editor}}<a href="{{.EditURL}}">Edit</a>{{end}}

    {{content}}

    <footer>{{.Site.Footer}}</footer>
</body>
</html>

{{slot "head"}} places the tags of the page in <head>. A theme without regions/head.gohtml gets core's: the <title>, the description, robots for a preview, the canonical link, the hreflang links with x-default, the og: tags and twitter:card, the favicon and the apple-touch-icon, {{feedLinks}}, {{apiLink}} and {{structuredData}} (see Search and SEO). For tags of its own, a theme adds regions/head.gohtml, which gets the View, like the layout, and calls core's tags first:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
{{template "webthings/head-tags.gohtml" .}}
<meta name="theme-color" content="#336699">

A head region that does not call webthings/head-tags.gohtml replaces core's tags and writes all of them itself. A layout without {{slot "head"}} gets nothing from core and writes its tags itself.

On a whole page the region's tags sit between two empty <template> markers, with the <title> just before them. An HTMX navigation replaces them with those of the new page, so no tag of the page left stays behind, except after a Back or Forward that htmx restores from its history (see The head region). Static tags, such as the stylesheets, stay in the layout. render.View.HeadRegion names the region placed in <head>; for themes core sets it to "head", and go-partial's exp/head does the work with head.Region.

{{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}} links the stylesheets in the order they must have: go-partial's partial-errors.css first, then the files given, each from the theme's assets/ or else from core, such as webthings.css, and the theme's values stylesheet last, each with its version and integrity (see styles).

Field What it holds
.Site The site in the page's language: Name, Tagline, SEOTitle, SEODescription, Footer, LogoURL, FaviconURL, AppleTouchIconURL, SocialImageURL, Organisation, Email, Phone, Address, HomeURL and Profiles
.Locale The page's language, such as en
.Path The current path with its language prefix, such as /en/news/hello
.Title, .Description The title and description of the page or module item
.Image An image for sharing, when a module screen sets one, such as a post's featured image; .Site.SocialImageURL is the site's default. An image from the media library is made into a 1200 × 630 JPEG, as the social image is
.Menu The published pages below the home page: ID, ElementID (the id for the item's element, see The menu), Path, Title, URL, Active and Children
.Languages Links to the same content in each language where it is published: Locale, URL, Active and Default, set for the site's default language, whose address the head region gives as hreflang="x-default" (see Search and SEO)
.Page The content page on page screens; on module screens, the page the module is placed on; nil elsewhere
.Module The instance key on module screens, such as news; empty elsewhere
.Content The data of the content template
.Preview Set when a signed-in editor previews a revision on the site
.Revision The previewed revision: its Number, Published when it is the published one, and PublishedURL, the address without the preview; nil elsewhere
.Theme The theme's Name and the Values of its settings (see Themes); {{styles}} and {{themeStyle}} link those with css as custom properties
.Editor The edit link for a signed-in editor who may edit what is shown (Name, EditURL); nil for visitors (see Editing and publishing)
.Status The page's status, such as 404 on the not-found page or a status a module screen sets; zero is 200 OK. The response has it, also an HTMX request for the content, a region or a fragment alone

.Site.Footer is the editors' formatted footer text, rendered from Markdown to HTML. It brings its own paragraphs, so place it in a <footer> or <div>, not in a <p>.

The site's images are copies made to measure from the images of the Site settings: .Site.LogoURL is the logo at most 600 pixels wide in the format it was uploaded in, .Site.FaviconURL the favicon as a 32 × 32 PNG, .Site.AppleTouchIconURL the favicon as a 180 × 180 PNG for the home screen of phones, and .Site.SocialImageURL the social image as a 1200 × 630 JPEG for og:image. Each is empty when the settings have no image. See The site's images.

{{feedLinks}} writes a <link rel="alternate"> for each Atom and RSS feed of the page shown, such as the posts of a news page, with absolute addresses, so browsers and feed readers find them. Pages without feeds get nothing. See feedLinks. For a link visitors see, {{feedURL "atom"}} and {{feedURL "rss"}} give the address of the page's feed, or "" (see feedURL).

{{apiLink}} writes a <link rel="alternate" type="application/json"> to the page shown in the content API, for apps, with an absolute address. It writes nothing while the API is off, on the not-found page and in a preview. See apiLink.

{{structuredData}} writes the page's structured data for search engines, schema.org's JSON-LD in one <script type="application/ld+json">: the site, its organisation, the page's trail, the page, and the item of the module's content, such as a post's Article. The not-found page gets nothing. See structuredData and Search and SEO.

For other links into the admin, adminURL gives the address of a named admin route to signed-in editors, and "" to visitors (see Template functions):

{{with adminURL "admin.dashboard"}}<a href="{{.}}">Admin</a>{{end}}

A preview is a page an editor opens from the admin to see a revision before it is published. A banner tells them so:

{{with .Revision}}
    <p class="preview-bar" role="status">
        {{tl localizer "Preview of revision %d" .Number}}
        <a href="{{.PublishedURL}}">{{tl localizer "Show the published version"}}</a>
    </p>
{{end}}

See Editing and publishing.

partial-errors.css, which {{styles}} links first, is go-partial's stylesheet of the box that takes the place of a part of the page that failed, which core serves at /_/partial-errors.css; a layout without {{styles}} links it with {{assetStyle "partial-errors.css"}} (see While you develop and The error box).

task templates -- site writes a complete layout to start from, with {{slot "head"}} and {{styles}}, and a regions/head.gohtml that calls core's tags (see Starting points).

Content templates

A content template gets only its own data, so it stays small and your code editor can check its fields. The layout gets everything else.

Template Data Shown for
page.gohtml frontend.Page Every content page
404.gohtml frontend.NotFound Addresses that do not exist, with status 404
search.gohtml frontend.SearchView /<locale>/search?q=
<key>/<name>.gohtml The module's view Module screens, such as news/post.gohtml

Content templates reach the page context through functions instead of fields, for example {{locale}}, {{theme "accent"}} and {{moduleURL "news"}}.

page.gohtml

page.gohtml shows a page of the page tree. Its frontend.Page has ID, ParentID (empty for the home page), Slug, Path (such as /about/team), Title, Description, Body (the page text as HTML), URL and IsHome:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.Page */}}
<main id="content">
    <h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
    {{with .Description}}<p class="lead">{{.}}</p>{{end}}
    {{.Body}}

    {{if .IsHome}}
        {{range posts "news" 3}}{{template "partials/post-card.gohtml" .}}{{end}}
    {{end}}
</main>

See Pages for the page tree.

404.gohtml

404.gohtml is shown with status 404 for addresses that do not exist. frontend.NotFound has one field, HomeURL, the home page in the current language. The layout's .Title is Not found, translated with the site's translations (the msgid is Not found). Without 404.gohtml, visitors get a plain-text "404 page not found".

search.gohtml

search.gohtml is the search screen at /<locale>/search?q=. frontend.SearchView has the Query, the Results (each with Title, Summary, URL, Module, Type and Score), the screen's URL for the form, and Throttled, set when the visitor searched too often in a short time: the search did not run, Results is empty and the response has status 429, so the template shows a message instead. The layout's .Title is the query, and the links of .Languages keep it. A fragment of search.gohtml, such as results that follow the visitor's typing, comes with the regions out of band, so the title and the language links follow the query; fragments of other pages come alone (see Fragments).

{{if .Throttled}}
    <p role="status">Too many searches in a short time. Wait a moment and try again.</p>
{{else if .Query}}
    {{range .Results}}<h2><a href="{{.URL}}">{{.Title}}</a></h2>{{else}}<p>Nothing found for “{{.Query}}”.</p>{{end}}
{{end}}

A published page with the path /search takes precedence over the screen, and without search.gohtml the address answers 404. See Search and SEO.

Module templates

A module renders its screens with templates named after the instance key: publishing.Module("news", "News") shows its posts with news/list.gohtml and news/post.gohtml. When a theme has no <key>/<name>.gohtml, the module type's <type>/<name>.gohtml is used, so instances can share a design or each have their own:

news/post.gohtml         the news instance
publishing/post.gohtml   blog and every other publishing instance

A theme other than default/ looks for both names in its own folder first, then in default/ (see Themes).

One shared template can still tell instances apart. In the layout .Module is the instance key; some module views carry it too, such as the Key of a list:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/lists.ListView */}}
<main id="content">
    <h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
    {{if eq .Key "faq"}}
        {{range .Entries}}<details><summary>{{.Title}}</summary>{{.Body}}</details>{{end}}
    {{else}}
        {{range .Entries}}<article><h2>{{.Title}}</h2>{{.Body}}</article>{{end}}
    {{end}}
</main>

The README of a module with screens lists its templates and their data, for example Publishing and Events. Module screens have no built-in default: the theme must have them (see Missing templates).

Module views give each image as a copy made for pages, never as the uploaded file: <X>URL is a WebP copy at most 1600 pixels wide, <X>Srcset lists it with narrower copies for a srcset attribute, <X>Width and <X>Height are its size, and <X>OriginalURL is the uploaded file, for a download link. A post has ImageURL, ImageSrcset, ImageWidth, ImageHeight and ImageOriginalURL, a person PhotoURL and the others:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing.Post */}}
<main id="content">
    <h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
    {{if .ImageURL}}
        <img src="{{.ImageURL}}" srcset="{{.ImageSrcset}}" sizes="(min-width: 46rem) 42rem, 100vw"
             width="{{.ImageWidth}}" height="{{.ImageHeight}}" alt="{{alt .ImageURL}}">
    {{end}}
    {{.Body}}
</main>

The gallery's images also have LargeURL, a copy at most 2400 pixels wide for a lightbox. {{image}} and {{srcset}} make copies in other sizes from these URLs; see Image sizes in templates.

The views of modules with a visitor form, such as the comments' ListView and the newsletter's SignupView, carry the form as .Form. A theme renders it with {{form_open .Form}}, its fields with {{form_field .Form "name" nil}}, with their labels and limits in the page's language, and {{form_close}}, or the whole form with {{form_render .Form nil}} (see Template functions). The form returns the visitor to the element whose id is the instance key, so give the element around the form and its result that id; the ids of its fields start with the key, such as guestbook-name. After a post with mistakes, the forms of the comments, newsletter, registrations and submissions modules show the visitor's values again, with the messages at the fields that need a correction, without a change to the template (see A post with mistakes).

Partials

Templates in partials/ can be used in every template, the layout included:

{{range posts "news" 3}}{{template "partials/post-card.gohtml" .}}{{end}}

The name is the path with its extension. Give a partial its own @dot line, like any other template:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing.Post */}}
<article class="card">
    <h3><a href="{{.URL}}">{{.Title}}</a></h3>
    <span class="meta">{{date .Date "medium"}}</span>
</article>

Components can use partials/ too. E-mail templates use mail/partials/ instead.

The @dot line and editor support

The first line of a template names the type of its data:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/events.Event */}}

The line changes nothing at runtime. It is a contract for go-clue, which gives code editors (GoLand, VS Code, Sublime Text, Vim and Neovim) completion, checks of fields and functions, hover and go-to-definition in Go templates. The starting points come with the right line.

go-clue reads .go-clue/config.json in the site's folder. List the go-webthings packages whose functions the templates use, as the starter and the demo do:

{
  "include": ["/"],
  "exclude": ["vendor", "var", "bin"],
  "providers": [
    "github.com/donseba/go-partial",
    "github.com/donseba/go-partial/exp/localization",
    "github.com/donseba/go-translator/v2",
    "github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend",
    "github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing",
    "github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/events"
  ],
  "functionMaps": [
    "github.com/donseba/go-partial/exp/localization.FuncMap"
  ]
}

The page anywhere: @model

@dot names a template's dot, which a partial or a range replaces. @model names a value a template can use however deep it is:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing.Post */}}
{{/* @model View github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
<p>{{.Title}} on {{View.Site.Name}}</p>

Every render offers two values, matched by their type: the page's frontend.View, what the layout gets, and the content of the page, what the content template gets, such as a publishing.Post. The name is yours. A partial can declare the post it is shown with, whatever was passed to it:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/comments.Comment */}}
{{/* @model Post github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing.Post */}}
<p>{{.Name}} on {{Post.Title}}</p>

@model works in the layout, content templates, partials and components. A value the page does not have, such as a publishing.Post on an events page, fails the render with an error that names it. E-mail templates and templates rendered with Frontend.Execute have no page; they use @dot only.

Starting points

App.WriteTemplates(dir, key) writes starting points for templates into dir: the module's own example when it has one, otherwise plain HTML generated from the data, with the @dot line and every field. The starter runs it as a task, writing into templates/default/:

task templates -- agenda
task templates -- news blog
task templates -- site
Key Files written
site layout.gohtml with its head region regions/head.gohtml and its stylesheet assets/site.css, page.gohtml, 404.gohtml, search.gohtml and core's component site/share.gohtml
A module instance key <key>/<name>.gohtml for each screen and component, and mail/<key>/<name>.gohtml for each e-mail

Existing files are never overwritten, and the app does not need to be started. WEBTHINGS_THEME=night task templates -- agenda writes into templates/night/ instead (see Themes).

The layout of site links the theme's assets/site.css with {{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}}, and site also writes that file, frontend.StyleScaffold: a comment saying it comes after webthings.css and before the theme's settings, so the settings' custom properties, such as var(--accent), can be used in it. A file that is there already is never overwritten. A file the theme does not have is a call that finds nothing, which fails every page in development (see Calls that find nothing).

Components and e-mail have defaults, so their copies are optional: delete the ones you keep as they are, and the module's default is used. Module screens need their files.

In your own main.go:

written, err := app.WriteTemplates("templates/default", "agenda")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

for _, file := range written {
    log.Println("wrote", file)
}

Missing templates

When the site starts, every module that can be placed on a page is checked against every theme. A screen that is missing as <key>/<name>.gohtml and as <type>/<name>.gohtml is logged with the command that writes it:

WARN missing template theme=default template=agenda/list.gohtml or=events/list.gohtml generate="task templates -- agenda"

task templates -- agenda is the starter's task, which calls App.WriteTemplates(dir, "agenda") (see Starting points). The site still starts. The check does not cover layout.gohtml, page.gohtml, 404.gohtml or search.gohtml.

Checking the templates at start

When the site starts, it parses every *.gohtml of every theme, in any folder, with the functions its pages render with: core's, those of the modules in app.Use, the translation functions and Config.Funcs (go-partial's Partial.CheckTemplates). Each problem a render would fail with is logged at WARN as template problem, with the themes that render the file and its position: a template that does not parse, a function the site does not have, and a {{template}} that names a template no file of the theme defines. A function of a bundled module names that module; any other unknown name gets the closest one:

WARN template problem themes=default problem="templates/default/page.gohtml:1:22: function \"absUrl\" not defined; did you mean \"absURL\"?"
WARN template problem themes=dark problem="templates/dark/page.gohtml:1:6: function \"pollBox\" not defined: it comes from the polls module; add it to app.Use or remove the call"

With os.DirFS("templates") the position starts with that folder, so your editor opens it; another file system, such as an embedded one, gives it from the theme's folder, such as default/page.gohtml:1:22. A file of default/ that other themes use is logged once, with all of them.

With Config.Development, as task dev sets it, Start fails with every problem at once, with webthings.ErrTemplates:

templates have problems (in development every problem stops the start):
  templates/default/page.gohtml:1:22: function "absUrl" not defined; did you mean "absURL"?

Otherwise Start fails only for a problem every page of the active theme would fail with: a template of its layout, regions/ or partials/ that does not parse or calls a function the site does not have, such as one of a module removed from app.Use. Every other problem only warns, also a {{template}} that names no file, which fails only where it runs:

templates have problems (every page of the active theme default would fail):
  templates/default/layout.gohtml:2:5: function "newsletterForm" not defined: it comes from the newsletter module; add it to app.Use or remove the call

A site with a Renderer of its own has no templates to check.

Calls that find nothing

Some calls run but cannot do what they ask, and would show nothing. Each is logged once at WARN as template mistake, with what there is:

  • an instance key the site has no such module of, such as {{posts "nieuws" 3}};
  • a file that neither the theme's assets/ nor core has, in asset, assetStyle, assetScript or styles;
  • a setting the theme does not declare, such as {{theme "acent"}}.
WARN template mistake problem="posts: no publishing instance \"nieuws\" (known: blog, news)"
WARN template mistake problem="assetStyle: no file \"sitee.css\" in the assets of theme default (closest: site.css, webthings.css, focal-points.css)"
WARN template mistake problem="theme: no setting \"acent\" in theme default (known: accent)"

Outside development the page still renders: posts gives no posts, assetStyle the file's address without a version or integrity, and theme gives "". With Config.Development the page fails with the message, which the error page shows.

When something goes wrong

Situation What the visitor gets
No templates at all A plain-text page saying which templates to add
The screen's template is missing Status 500 with missing_template; the log names the template and theme
404.gohtml is missing A plain-text "404 page not found"
search.gohtml is missing Status 404 at /<locale>/search
An error in the layout or a content template Status 500 with the theme's 500.gohtml, or without one go-partial's plain error page: "Internal Server Error", "Something went wrong. Please try again." and the address. The heading and the sentence are translated into the page's language with the site's translations, and the page's lang is that language; the page never names the template or the error. The error is logged as render page. With Config.Development, a detailed error (see below)
A module's handler or a visitor action that fails, such as a comment that cannot be saved The same, in the page's language or that of the page the form was on, also for an HTMX request (Frontend.Fail); the error is logged as render page. With Config.Development, go-partial's detailed error page with the error
An error in 404.gohtml The theme's 500.gohtml with status 500, or a plain-text "404 page not found" without one; the error is logged as render not found. With Config.Development, a detailed error with status 500

Errors include a function that does not exist, a field the data does not have and a component that fails. One failing part fails the whole page, so visitors never get half a page. The log names the template and the line. A template that does not parse and a function that does not exist are found at start, before a visitor meets them (see Checking the templates at start). An invalid theme.json stops the site at start.

500.gohtml

500.gohtml is the theme's page for a failing template, and for a module's handler or a visitor action that fails (Frontend.Fail), outside development. It renders on its own, without the layout, with status 500, and is never cached; an HTMX request gets it alone too. It gets every template function and the theme's partials/, in the page's language; asset, assetStyle, assetScript, themeStyle and styles give the theme's versioned addresses and integrity as on every page, also after a failing action. @model View names the page's frontend.View, what the layout gets; after a failing action it is the site in the language of the page the form was on, without a page of its own. Its dot is go-partial's errors.Data: its Message is a sentence that tells nothing of the error, "Something went wrong. Please try again.", already translated into the page's language with the site's translations, so {{.Message}} shows it; its Title is the heading, the status text "Internal Server Error", translated the same way; its Lang is the page's language, as View.Locale is; its Error holds the error itself, so leave that out. task translations adds the sentence and the heading to the POT file (see Languages). The demo has one in templates/default/500.gohtml. A minimal one:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-partial/ext/errors.Data */}}
{{/* @model View github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="{{View.Locale}}">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <title>{{View.Site.Name}}</title>
    {{styles "site.css"}}
</head>
<body>
    <h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
    <p>{{.Message}}</p>
    <p><a href="{{View.Site.HomeURL}}">{{tl localizer "Back to the home page"}}</a></p>
</body>
</html>

When 500.gohtml fails itself, go-partial's plain error page answers instead, as for a theme without one, and it never names the template or the error. A theme other than default/ uses the one in default/ when it has none. Without any, the visitor gets go-partial's plain error page, with its heading and sentence in the page's language (see When something goes wrong). That page styles itself with one <style> element. The site's own Content-Security-Policy allows that element by its hash, go-partial's errors.StyleHash() (ext/errors), on every page (see Under a Content-Security-Policy); another policy without 'unsafe-inline' in style-src blocks it unless it has that hash, and the page then shows unstyled. A 500.gohtml that links the theme's stylesheets, like the one above, needs no hash. Under the site's policy, a <style> element or style attribute in 500.gohtml itself is blocked.

While you develop

Config.Development shows a failing template in the browser instead of 500.gohtml or a plain error. The error page replaces the whole response: it says "Template render error" and names the template, the line and the error, with status 500, and is never cached. An HTMX request gets the same error alone, as a box without the layout or regions (see HTMX). The error is still logged. It works on the site and in the admin. In development Start also fails for every problem the check at start finds, and a call that finds nothing fails its page (see Checking the templates at start).

The error page styles itself with the same <style> element as go-partial's plain error page, which the site's own policy allows by its hash (see 500.gohtml). The box has no inline style, only go-partial's classes: go-partial-error, and go-partial-error__title, go-partial-error__message and go-partial-error__details for its heading, sentence and list. go-partial's partial-errors.css styles them. Core serves it at /_/partial-errors.css, and {{styles}} in the layout links it first, as in the layout task templates -- site writes; a layout without {{styles}} links it with {{assetStyle "partial-errors.css"}} (see The error box). Without it the box shows unstyled, as a heading, a paragraph and a list, unless the theme's stylesheet styles the classes. errors.StylesheetFS() holds the same rules as a file.

Config.Development also makes {{debug .}} show a value, such as the dot of a template, so you can see which fields it has:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.Page */}}
<main id="content">
    {{debug .}}
    <h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
</main>

Without Config.Development, {{debug .}} shows nothing, so one that is left behind does no harm. Use Development on your own computer only, like ReloadTemplates: the error page and {{debug .}} show internals to anyone who opens the page.

app := webthings.New(webthings.Config{
    Templates:       os.DirFS("templates"),
    ReloadTemplates: true,
    Development:     true,
})

See Template functions for debug, and Configuration for every setting.

Components

The interactive modules offer components: parts of a page with plain, accessible default markup that any template includes with one function, such as {{commentThread "remarks" .ID}} or {{newsletterForm "letters"}}. Core has one, {{shareBar "" .Title}}.

A theme replaces a component with <key>/<name>.gohtml or <type>/<name>.gohtml, like a module screen (see Themes for a theme other than default/), and core's with site/<name>.gohtml; otherwise the module's default renders. A component is rendered through go-partial as a part of the page, a child of the template that includes it: in the page's language, with the theme's partials/, every template function and the page for @model (see Template functions). A component that fails fails the page. Themes covers their markup and styling; each module's README lists its components, for example Comments.

E-mail templates

Modules write their e-mail from templates too. A theme replaces a module's default with mail/<key>/<name>.gohtml or mail/<type>/<name>.gohtml, found like a module screen (see Themes); templates in mail/partials/ can be used in every e-mail template. A mail template defines subject, text and optionally html. See E-mail.

Your own functions

Config.Funcs adds functions to every template, after core's and the modules'. A function with the name of a core or module function replaces it. The site's translations are not among them: Config.Translations takes the translator frontend.Translations returns, which gives templates tl, tn, ctl and ctn (see Languages):

translations, err := frontend.Translations("translations")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

app := webthings.New(webthings.Config{
    Templates:    os.DirFS("templates"),
    Translations: translations,
    Funcs:        []template.FuncMap{siteFuncs()},
})

A function whose first parameter is a context.Context gets the context of the request being rendered; templates call it without that parameter. In that context, frontend.Locale(ctx) is the page's language, frontend.Request(ctx) the request and frontend.Service(ctx, key) the API of a module instance:

func siteFuncs() template.FuncMap {
    return template.FuncMap{
        "year": func() int {
            return time.Now().Year()
        },
        // {{with featured "news"}}: the newest post with an image.
        "featured": func(ctx context.Context, key string) *publishing.Post {
            news, ok := frontend.Service(ctx, key).(*publishing.Service)
            if !ok {
                return nil
            }

            posts, err := news.Latest(ctx, frontend.Locale(ctx), 10)
            if err != nil {
                return nil
            }

            for _, post := range posts {
                if post.ImageURL != "" {
                    return &post
                }
            }

            return nil
        },
    }
}

In the layout:

{{with featured "news"}}<a href="{{.URL}}"><img src="{{image .ImageURL "1200"}}" alt="">{{.Title}}</a>{{end}}
<p>© {{year}} {{.Site.Name}}</p>

Your functions also work in components and e-mail templates. To give editors their signatures and go-to-definition, mark the function that returns them for go-clue, and give each function that takes a context its signature as templates call it:

// go-clue:funcmap
func siteFuncs() template.FuncMap {
    return template.FuncMap{
        //go-clue:sig func(key string) *github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing.Post
        "featured": featured,
    }
}

There is no need for go-clue's @func in templates: it declares a function for one template, which must still be registered here.

A site or module function named like one of go-partial's, such as url, content, locale, localizer, slot, hasSlot, requiredSlot, deferredSlot, targetHeader, targetValue or targetIs, or with a name starting with _, stops the site at start with render.ErrReserved. Two module types that offer the same function name stop it too, with template function "<name>" is offered by <type> and <type>. Template functions lists go-partial's functions.

HTMX requests

go-partial answers HTMX requests, with the htmx 4 protocol. A request with HX-Request: true aimed at the element with ID content gets only the content template, without the layout, followed by the theme's regions out of band, in the order of their file names, the same on every request, so the same page gives the same bytes and ETag; the starting points wrap their content in <main id="content"> for this. Aimed at a fragment of the theme, it gets only that fragment, when the page has what the fragment declares; on the search screen the regions follow it out of band. Without a target the request gets the whole page, and so does a request for the whole document, such as one with hx-select. Aimed at any other element, or at a fragment the page cannot answer for, it gets the content template with HX-Retarget: #content and HX-Reswap: outerHTML, and for a GET HX-Push-Url, so HTMX replaces the content element and the address follows. HTMX covers regions, fragments and forms.

Rendering one template from Go

app.Frontend.Execute(ctx, name, locale, data) renders one template of the active theme without the layout, for example Execute(ctx, "partials/card", "nl", post). It renders through go-partial like a part of the theme's pages, with partials/ and every template function, in the given language. There is no request, so request and url give nothing, and no page for @model.

Guides.Title: Template functions
Guides.Summary: A reference of the functions go-webthings gives every public template: links, dates and money, images, theme assets, forms, translations, sharing, search, feeds, the content API, structured data, HTMX attributes and debugging. Module functions are listed by module with a link to their documentation.
Guides.Body:
Where functions come from

Templates get functions from seven places. All of them work in the layout and in every content template.

Source Functions
Core, frontend.Funcs moduleURL, searchURL, absURL, adminURL, date, time, dateRange, timeRange, weekday, money, image, srcset, focalClass, objectPosition, alt, theme, asset, assetScript, assetStyle, themeStyle, styles, form_open, form_hidden, form_field, form_errors, form_buttons, form_close, form_render, profiles, share, shareBar, search, feedLinks, feedURL, apiLink, structuredData
go-translator, with the site's translations from frontend.Translations in Config.Translations tl, tn, ctl, ctn
go-partial, which renders the pages content, locale, localizer, request, url, urlIs, urlStarts, urlContains, joinPath, urlPath, basePath, partial, runtime, ctx, oob, oobAttr, oobSwap, slot, hasSlot, requiredSlot, deferredSlot, targetHeader, targetValue, targetIs
go-partial's exp/interactions, for HTMX attributes noBoost, submitAttrs, liveAttrs, revealAttrs, clientAttrs, confirmAttr, asyncAttrs, pollAttrs, onAttrs, streamAttrs, refreshAttrs
Core's renderer, render debug
go-importmap, with Config.ImportMap or Config.Assets importmap, importmap_nonce, importmap_url, importmap_script, importmap_style
The modules in app.Use, and Config.Funcs See Module functions and Your own functions

A function in Config.Funcs replaces a core, module, translation or import map function with the same name, and core and module functions replace go-partial's interaction functions of the same name. A site or module function with a name from the go-partial row, or a name starting with _, stops the start with render.ErrReserved.

Go's own template functions, such as and, or, not, eq, len, index, printf and slice, work as usual; see the text/template documentation.

The signatures below are as templates call them. Many functions take a context.Context first in Go; they get it from the request being rendered, and templates leave it out.

Links and addresses

moduleURL

func moduleURL(key string) string

The address of the page a module instance is placed on, in the current language, or "" when it is on no page.

{{with moduleURL "news"}}<a href="{{.}}">All news</a>{{end}}

searchURL

func searchURL() string

The address of the search screen in the current language, such as /en/search, for a search form. See Search.

<form action="{{searchURL}}" method="get" role="search">
    <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search">
</form>

absURL

func absURL(link string) string

A link made absolute with the site's address: Config.BaseURL, or the address of the request. A relative path is read from the current page, and a path keeps its query and fragment: "" is the current page without its query, "#top" the current page with #top, and "?page=2" the current page with that query. A link with a scheme or a host, such as https://…, mailto:… or //cdn.example.com/…, stays as it is. Use it for canonical and hreflang links and og:image.

<link rel="canonical" href="{{absURL .Path}}">
{{with or .Image .Site.SocialImageURL}}<meta property="og:image" content="{{absURL .}}">{{end}}

adminURL

func adminURL(name string, args ...any) string

The address of a named admin route, for an editor who is signed in to the admin; "" for visitors and for a route the admin does not have. args are the route's parameters as name and value pairs. The admin's own pages are named like admin.dashboard, and a section's like admin.<key>.index and admin.<key>.edit with "id", such as admin.pages.edit or admin.news.edit. The address follows Config.AdminPath, and visitors never get it, so the admin's path stays off public pages. The admin checks rights itself: a link to a screen the editor may not open answers 403. For the admin screen of what the page shows, the layout's .Editor is simpler (see Editing and publishing).

{{with adminURL "admin.dashboard"}}<a href="{{.}}">Admin</a>{{end}}
{{with adminURL "admin.news.edit" "id" .ID}}<a href="{{.}}">Edit</a>{{end}}

request

func request() *http.Request

The request being rendered. Its path is the page's whole path, also on module screens, such as /en/news/hello.

{{if eq (request.URL.Query.Get "view") "map"}}…{{end}}

url

func url() *url.URL

The URL of the request being rendered. Its path is the page's whole path, like .Path in the layout, also on module screens.

{{with url.Query.Get "q"}}<p>You searched for {{.}}</p>{{end}}

urlIs, urlStarts and urlContains

func urlIs(path string) bool
func urlStarts(prefix string) bool
func urlContains(text string) bool

Compare the request's path: urlIs ignores leading and trailing slashes, urlStarts and urlContains compare as written. Like url, they see the page's whole path, also on module screens.

<a href="/en/contact" {{if urlIs "/en/contact"}}aria-current="page"{{end}}>Contact</a>

joinPath and urlPath

func joinPath(parts ...string) string
func urlPath(base string, parts ...string) template.URL

Join path parts with slashes and clean the result, as Go's path.Join does; urlPath returns it as a URL that html/template keeps as it is.

<a href="{{urlPath (moduleURL "news") "archive"}}">Archive</a>

basePath

func basePath() string

go-partial's base path; always "" on a go-webthings site.

Dates, times and money

The date and money functions write in the page's language. Times stored in UTC, such as when a registration was made, are shown in the site's timezone; times in another zone keep it, such as an event in its own timezone, and calendar dates, such as a post's or a document's date, show the same day in every timezone. English and Dutch are built in. The site's translations replace month and day names and patterns in every language, English and Dutch included, by context (msgctxt) and English msgid: January … December in month, Jan … Dec in month-short, Sunday … Saturday in day, Sun … Sat in day-short, AM and PM in time, and the patterns of the styles short, medium, long, full and time in date. What a catalogue does not translate is the built-in name or pattern, or English in a language without built-in ones, so English and Dutch catalogues need not contain these texts (frontend.BuiltInCalendar). frontend.CalendarTexts() lists them, task translations adds them to the POT file, and task translations:check reports them missing only in languages without built-in ones (see Languages). A German de.po:

msgctxt "month"
msgid "October"
msgstr "Oktober"

msgctxt "day"
msgid "Sunday"
msgstr "Sonntag"

msgctxt "date"
msgid "long"
msgstr "d. MMMM y"

With it, {{date .Start}} writes 25. Oktober 2026 on a German page.

date

func date(t time.Time, style ...string) string

The day of t in a style (short, medium, long or full; long when left out) or in a CLDR date pattern. A zero time gives "".

{{date .Date}}                25 October 2026
{{date .Date "short"}}        25/10/2026, in Dutch 25-10-2026
{{date .Date "medium"}}       25 Oct 2026
{{date .Start "full"}}        Sunday 25 October 2026, in Dutch zondag 25 oktober 2026
{{date .Start "EEE d MMM"}}   Sun 25 Oct

Patterns use d dd, M MM MMM MMMM, y yy, E EEEE, H HH, h hh, mm and a; text in single quotes is copied.

time

func time(t time.Time) string

The time of day of t, such as 14:00, or 2:00 PM in en-US.

<time datetime="{{.Start.Format "2006-01-02T15:04"}}">{{time .Start}}</time>

dateRange

func dateRange(start, end time.Time, style ...string) string

The days from start to end, leaving out what they share in the built-in languages, for a style whose pattern the site's translations do not replace. An end on the same day, or a zero end, gives one date.

{{dateRange .Start .End "long"}}   25–27 October 2026

timeRange

func timeRange(start, end time.Time) string

The times of day from start to end; a zero end gives only the start.

{{date .Start "full"}} · {{timeRange .Start .End}}   Sunday 25 October 2026 · 14:00–17:00

weekday

func weekday(day time.Weekday, style ...string) string

The name of a day of the week, or with "short" its abbreviation: Monday and Mon, in Dutch maandag and ma.

{{weekday .Start.Weekday "short"}}

money

func money(amount any, currency string) (string, error)

An amount in minor units (cents) of an ISO 4217 currency, with the language's separators and symbol position. The amount must be an integer; anything else stops the template with an error.

{{money .PriceCents "EUR"}}   €45.00, in Dutch € 45,00, in German 45,00 €

Images

image and srcset make resized copies of images from the media library, focalClass and objectPosition let the browser crop them around their focal point, and alt gives their alt text. Module views already give each image as a copy at most 1600 pixels wide, with its srcset and size, such as a post's .ImageURL, .ImageSrcset, .ImageWidth and .ImageHeight; these functions are for other sizes. Media and images explains the sizes, formats and how the copies are kept.

image

func image(ref string, spec string) string

The address of a resized copy of an image. ref is an image's URL as module views give it, the copy such as .ImageURL or the original such as .ImageOriginalURL, the URL of any other copy, or a media ID; the copy is always made from the original. spec is a size, optionally followed by crop and a format (webp, the default, jpg or png). A crop is cut around the image's focal point, which editors place in the media library. Files that are not images, and unknown specs, give ref as it is, or the file's URL for a media ID.

<img src="{{image .ImageURL "800x600"}}" alt="">        fits inside 800 × 600
<img src="{{image .ImageURL "800"}}" alt="">            800 wide
<img src="{{image .ImageURL "400x400 crop"}}" alt="">   exactly 400 × 400, around the focal point
<img src="{{image .ImageURL "1200 jpg"}}" alt="">       1200 wide, as JPEG

srcset

func srcset(ref string, widths ...int) string

WebP copies of an image in the given widths, for a srcset attribute. ref is as for image. Widths beyond the image's own width are left out, and the image's own width is offered instead. The copies are never cropped; see focalClass. Gives "" for files that are not images.

Module views give the srcset of their own copy, such as .ImageSrcset, which goes up to 1600 pixels. srcset offers other widths, such as larger copies for an image as wide as the screen:

<img src="{{.ImageURL}}" srcset="{{srcset .ImageURL 800 1600 2400}}" sizes="100vw" alt="">

focalClass

func focalClass(ref string, box ...string) string

The class of core's focal-points.css that keeps an image's focal point in view when the browser crops it with object-fit: cover: fp- with the horizontal and the vertical position in percent, each rounded to a multiple of 5, such as fp-35-60. It is the value of objectPosition as a class, with the same ref and box: with the box's proportions, as "3:2" or "720x480", the browser shows about the same part as {{image . "720x480 crop"}}. Files that are not images in the library give fp-50-50, the centre.

The class needs focal-points.css in the layout, such as with {{styles "site.css" "focal-points.css"}}, and object-fit: cover from the theme's stylesheet (see Focal points). It needs no style attribute, so it works under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline'. Use it with srcset, whose copies are not cropped:

<img src="{{image .ImageURL "720x480 crop"}}"
     srcset="{{srcset .ImageURL 360 720 1080}}"
     sizes="(max-width: 700px) 100vw, 360px"
     class="photo {{focalClass .ImageURL "720x480"}}"
     alt="">

.photo { aspect-ratio: 3 / 2; object-fit: cover; }

For a photo of 2000 × 1000 pixels with its focal point 30% from the left and 60% from the top, this writes class="photo fp-0-50": the 3:2 box shows the photo's whole height, and its left edge. Without proportions, {{focalClass .ImageURL}} gives fp-30-60.

objectPosition

func objectPosition(ref string, box ...string) string

A CSS object-position value for an image the browser crops with object-fit: cover, so the crop keeps the image's focal point in view. With the box's proportions, as "4:3" or "800x600", the browser shows the same part as {{image . "800x600 crop"}}. Without them it gives the focal point itself, such as 25% 75%, which stays in view in a box of any shape but is not centred. ref is as for image: a copy's URL, such as .ImageURL, gives the focal point of its image. Files that are not images in the library give 50% 50%.

The value goes in a style attribute:

<img src="{{image .ImageURL "720x480 crop"}}"
     srcset="{{srcset .ImageURL 360 720 1080}}"
     sizes="(max-width: 700px) 100vw, 360px"
     style="aspect-ratio: 3 / 2; object-fit: cover; object-position: {{objectPosition .ImageURL "720x480"}}"
     alt="">

A Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' in style-src blocks a style attribute, so objectPosition is for themes without such a policy; focalClass gives the same position as a class. See A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own.

alt

func alt(ref string) string

The alt text editors wrote for an image in the media library, in the page's language, or "" when there is none. ref is as for image, such as the copy a module view gives.

<img src="{{.ImageURL}}" width="{{.ImageWidth}}" height="{{.ImageHeight}}" alt="{{alt .ImageURL}}">

Theme and assets

theme

func theme(name string) (string, error)

A setting of the active theme from its theme.json, as editors set it in the admin, or its default. A number setting gives the number without its unit, such as 42. In the layout {{.Theme.Values.accent}} is the same. A setting the theme does not declare gives "" and is logged once with the ones it has, such as theme: no setting "acent" in theme default (known: accent); with Config.Development the page fails with that message (see Calls that find nothing). See Themes.

<body data-headings="{{theme "headings"}}">

asset

func asset(file string) (string, error)

The address of a file in the theme's assets/ folder, with a version from the file's content, such as /theme/default/site.css?v=9b2ca0fe143be1a4, so the address changes when the file does. webthings.css, focal-points.css and partial-errors.css come from core when the theme has no file of that name. A file that neither the theme nor core has gives its address without a version, such as /theme/default/logo.svg, and is logged once with the closest names there are; with Config.Development the page fails with that message (see Calls that find nothing). For a stylesheet or script, assetStyle and assetScript write the whole tag with the file's integrity. See Themes.

<link rel="icon" href="{{asset "favicon.svg"}}" type="image/svg+xml">
<img src="{{asset "img/logo.svg"}}" alt="">

assetScript and assetStyle

func assetScript(file string, attrs ...string) (template.HTML, error)
func assetStyle(file string, attrs ...string) (template.HTML, error)

assetScript writes a <script> and assetStyle a <link rel="stylesheet"> for a file of the theme's assets/ folder, at the address asset gives, with the file's Subresource Integrity and crossorigin="anonymous", so the browser refuses a file whose content is not what the page expects. attrs are more attributes as name and value pairs; an empty value writes the name alone, such as defer. webthings.css, focal-points.css and partial-errors.css, go-partial's stylesheet of the box that takes the place of a part of the page that failed (see The error box), come from core, as with asset.

{{assetStyle "webthings.css"}}
{{assetStyle "partial-errors.css"}}
{{assetStyle "site.css"}}
{{assetStyle "print.css" "media" "print"}}
{{assetScript "site.js" "type" "module"}}

This writes:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_/webthings.css?v=1490831917b655ed" integrity="sha384-FJCDGRe2Ve0xKnzX94IslGPK/7R+/RPOOqYddXKEC6t0t5sqBSjqEDR3xxlUwxAh" crossorigin="anonymous">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_/partial-errors.css?v=dbaec249af3f1089" integrity="sha384-267CSa8/EImeIQQLR3XAW5pnK8j7PFJDgO+m1+qHE/V5s/kmZZL2w7DZDOHMixq+" crossorigin="anonymous">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/theme/default/site.css?v=9b2ca0fe143be1a4" integrity="sha384-myyg/hQ74aSgjBBvVME/QXAXEkT4Y9dHbVQ5C0lIyGpldvNLJV2IWc5ElXbqLi06" crossorigin="anonymous">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/theme/default/print.css?v=3308f99567027e50" integrity="sha384-Mwj5lWcCflBkQKUBW+SXpHV5nUa7KmgCgLQbh2/9mXSvcECXSfO4988ugU0PGRw0" crossorigin="anonymous" media="print">
<script src="/theme/default/site.js?v=7e94ac7e9f75c0e9" integrity="sha384-fpSsfp91wOloMeTRBzPOrwMSDH0D6SBhTnFTWERkBorjp/6R2ze6PZCreuu3Lr6S" crossorigin="anonymous" type="module"></script>

With Config.ReloadTemplates the theme's files may change while the site runs, so their tags have no integrity, only the address; core's webthings.css, focal-points.css and partial-errors.css do not change and keep it. A file that neither the theme nor core has gets neither version nor integrity, and is logged once as a template mistake with the closest names there are, such as assetStyle: no file "sitee.css" in the assets of theme default (closest: site.css, webthings.css, focal-points.css); with Config.Development the page fails with that message (see Calls that find nothing). A crossorigin in attrs replaces the default one. The address (src, or rel and href) and integrity cannot be set in attrs; trying, or an odd number of attrs, fails the render.

themeStyle

func themeStyle(attrs ...string) (template.HTML, error)

The <link rel="stylesheet"> of the values stylesheet of the theme being rendered, /theme/<theme>/values.css, with its version, its Subresource Integrity and crossorigin="anonymous". Core makes the stylesheet from the theme's color, select and number settings with css in theme.json: each sets its custom property to the setting's value, a number with its unit, such as 42rem, so the page needs no style attribute for them. A theme without such settings gets nothing. A preview in the admin links the values of the theme it shows. attrs are more attributes, as for assetStyle. Put it after the theme's own stylesheets, whose fallbacks its properties replace; styles links it last by itself. See The values stylesheet.

{{assetStyle "site.css"}}
{{themeStyle}}

With {"name": "accent", "label": "Accent colour", "type": "color", "default": "#b5562f", "css": "--accent"} as the theme's only such setting, while no editor chose another colour, {{themeStyle}} writes:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/theme/default/values.css?v=d00cf169d95b4358" integrity="sha384-0AzxadlbQ1ihbiw8IrDYoOEMNd5euEqG0fwxFnEecsLlTSf4ySWQZt0kpauEw/iI" crossorigin="anonymous">

and the stylesheet is:

:root {
    --accent: #b5562f;
}

styles

func styles(files ...string) (template.HTML, error)

The stylesheet links of the layout's <head>, in the order they must have: go-partial's partial-errors.css first, which styles the box that takes the place of a part of the page that failed (see The error box); then files, in the order given, each linked as assetStyle links it, from the theme's assets/ or, when the theme has no file of that name, from core, such as webthings.css and focal-points.css; last the theme's values stylesheet, as themeStyle links it, whose custom properties replace the fallbacks of the stylesheets before it. A file given twice, or partial-errors.css given, is linked once. Every link has its version and Subresource Integrity, as with assetStyle, and none is a <style> element, so the page works under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline'. A file that neither the theme nor core has is a template mistake, as for assetStyle.

{{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}}

With the theme's assets/site.css and the setting of themeStyle above, this writes:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_/partial-errors.css?v=dbaec249af3f1089" integrity="sha384-267CSa8/EImeIQQLR3XAW5pnK8j7PFJDgO+m1+qHE/V5s/kmZZL2w7DZDOHMixq+" crossorigin="anonymous">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_/webthings.css?v=1490831917b655ed" integrity="sha384-FJCDGRe2Ve0xKnzX94IslGPK/7R+/RPOOqYddXKEC6t0t5sqBSjqEDR3xxlUwxAh" crossorigin="anonymous">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/theme/default/site.css?v=16abe7e5ac5a49fd" integrity="sha384-Fqvn5axaSf3U7wTN3et5Jw2dbuNKYHeVtkP0rNIwSkeqN2zpT/WT3q2vIPKFoa/L" crossorigin="anonymous">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/theme/default/values.css?v=d00cf169d95b4358" integrity="sha384-0AzxadlbQ1ihbiw8IrDYoOEMNd5euEqG0fwxFnEecsLlTSf4ySWQZt0kpauEw/iI" crossorigin="anonymous">

The layout task templates -- site writes uses it, and so do the starter's and the demo's.

importmap

func importmap() (template.HTML, error)
func importmap_nonce(nonce string) (template.HTML, error)
func importmap_url(file string) string
func importmap_script(file string, attrs ...string) (template.HTML, error)
func importmap_style(file string, attrs ...string) (template.HTML, error)

go-importmap's functions, only with Config.ImportMap or Config.Assets. importmap writes the import map for the layout's <head>: a <script type="importmap"> that names each package's file by its versioned address, with its integrity. Core adds go-partial's browser clients to it, partial-flash, partial-sse and partial-interactions, with their integrity, unless the site maps such a name itself; a client's file among the site's own files, such as a partial-flash.js, is used instead of core's copy. importmap_url is the versioned address of one of its files, by the file's path in the folder given to importmap.FromFS, such as /assets/vendor/htmx/htmx.esm.min.js?v=9481657c08f4d363 for vendor/htmx/htmx.esm.min.js. With Config.Assets, importmap_url is the versioned address of a file in that folder, such as /assets/site.css?v=9b2ca0fe143be1a4 for site.css, and importmap maps only go-partial's clients (see Themes). See HTMX.

{{importmap}}
<link rel="modulepreload" href="{{importmap_url "vendor/htmx/htmx.esm.min.js"}}">

importmap_style writes a <link rel="stylesheet"> and importmap_script a <script> for a file at its versioned address, with attrs as name and value pairs, for a file the page loads itself rather than through the import map. Both carry the file's integrity and crossorigin="anonymous", so the browser refuses a file whose content is not what the page expects. Files that may change while the site runs get no integrity, here or in the import map: those of Config.Assets with Config.ReloadTemplates, and those of a Config.ImportMap made with go-importmap's assets.Reload; the import map then has no integrity at all, not for go-partial's clients either. The files of importmap.FromFS do not change and keep it, also with ReloadTemplates.

{{importmap_style "site.css"}}
{{importmap_script "site.js" "type" "module"}}

With Config.Assets this writes:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/site.css?v=9b2ca0fe143be1a4" integrity="sha384-myyg/hQ74aSgjBBvVME/QXAXEkT4Y9dHbVQ5C0lIyGpldvNLJV2IWc5ElXbqLi06" crossorigin="anonymous">
<script src="/assets/site.js?v=beecfec8eef56dc6" integrity="sha384-vuz+yO71bcb30P4dMUNzy6/D2y+6d/n0KcOnt5clJtTBxEDoKAqGay0stFlC8Dpr" crossorigin="anonymous" type="module"></script>

The import map is an inline script, so a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' in script-src blocks it unless the policy allows it by its hash or by a nonce. The site's own policy, report only or enforced under Site settings › Security, has the hash of the page's import map, so the site needs nothing more: {{importmap}} writes exactly the map that was hashed, also while the map's files reload, and a page the output cache serves again carries the hash it was made with. Do not change the map's text after it is rendered. A policy sent from elsewhere, such as the proxy or a handler around the app, needs the hash too. go-importmap's ImportMap.ScriptHash() gives the hash of what {{importmap}} writes, with its quotes, such as 'sha256-…'. Core gives the map in Config.ImportMap its addresses and go-partial's clients when the site starts, so take the hash after App.Start. The hash changes only when the map does, so it suits pages the output cache keeps. While the map's files reload (assets.Reload), RenderWithHash gives the import map and its hash from the same moment. importmap_nonce writes what importmap writes with a nonce attribute, such as <script type="importmap" nonce="…"> (go-importmap's WithNonce), and importmap_script takes "nonce" among its attrs. A nonce must differ for every response, so it suits only a site that sends its own policy with nonces, on pages that are never cached; core's policy has no nonces. See go-importmap's Content-Security-Policy and A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own.

Forms

Visitor forms post to a module's action, which returns the visitor to the form's page with a result (see Visitor forms). The form_* functions are go-form's, for the forms modules offer: the Form of a module's view, such as the comments' ListView, is a go-form form.RenderModel of the struct the module's action reads, and the functions render its fields with the limits of its tags, such as required and maxlength, in the page's language. A module makes it with frontend.VisitorForm: the form posts to the module's action with a spam trap and the page to return to, the element whose id is the instance key, such as /en/guestbook#remarks. The ids of its fields start with that key, such as remarks-name, so the forms of two instances on one page keep ids of their own.

form_field

func form_field(model any, name string, errs form.FieldErrors) (template.HTML, error)

One field of a form: its label, its input, select or textarea with the limits of its tags, its description and its errors. name is the field's key in the form, the value of its name tag, such as "name" for the comments' Name; the Go field name fails the render with the names the form has, form: no field "Name" (fields: subject, parent, name, email, body). errs are the errors to show at the field. Templates pass nil for a module's form: after a post with mistakes, the form itself brings the visitor's values and the messages for its fields (see A post with mistakes). Errors passed in errs take the place of those messages.

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/comments.ListView */}}
{{form_open .Form}}
    {{form_field .Form "subject" nil}}
    {{form_field .Form "name" nil}}
    {{form_field .Form "email" nil}}
    {{form_field .Form "body" nil}}
    <button type="submit">{{tl localizer "Send"}}</button>
{{form_close}}

Outside a module's view, a module function can give the model, such as {{form_field (commentInput "remarks" .ID) "name" nil}} for the comments on a post (see Comments), or {{form_open (submitInput "tips")}} for a proposal (see Submissions).

form_open, form_buttons and form_close

func form_open(model any, attrs ...any) (template.HTML, error)
func form_buttons(model any) (template.HTML, error)
func form_close() (template.HTML, error)

The parts of a form around its fields. form_open writes the <form> tag with the model's action and method, followed by the hidden fields: the spam trap and, for a module's form, the page to return to, a field named back. form_buttons writes the submit button, and a cancel link when the model has one; form_close writes </form>. Hidden fields of the model, such as the comments' subject, are fields like the others: place them with form_field.

{{form_open .Form}}
    {{form_field .Form "subject" nil}}
    {{form_field .Form "name" nil}}
    {{form_field .Form "body" nil}}
    {{form_buttons .Form}}
{{form_close}}

attrs are more attributes of the form tag: name and value pairs, or a template.HTMLAttr such as the attributes submitAttrs writes. A class adds to the form theme's class. action, method and enctype come from the model, and giving them fails the render; a pair cannot set an event handler such as onsubmit.

{{form_open .Form "class" "comment-form" (submitAttrs runtime .Action "target" "#remarks" "swap" "outerHTML")}}

This writes <form action="/_/remarks/post" method="POST" class="wt-form comment-form" hx-post="/_/remarks/post" hx-swap="outerHTML" hx-target="#remarks">, then the hidden fields.

form_hidden

func form_hidden(model any) (template.HTML, error)

Only the hidden fields form_open writes after the tag: the spam trap and the page to return to, for a template that writes the <form> tag itself.

<form method="post" action="{{.Action}}" class="comment-form">
    {{form_hidden .Form}}
    {{form_field .Form "subject" nil}}
    {{form_field .Form "name" nil}}
    {{form_field .Form "body" nil}}
    <button type="submit">{{tl localizer "Send"}}</button>
</form>

For the comments remarks on the home page, form_hidden writes:

<input type="text" name="website" value="" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" class="form-honeypot">
<input type="hidden" name="back" value="/en/#remarks">

The spam trap has the class form-honeypot and no style attribute; see The hidden fields.

form_render

func form_render(model any, errs form.FieldErrors) (template.HTML, error)

The whole form: what form_open writes, the page to return to included, every field in the order of the struct, hidden ones included, the buttons and </form>.

{{form_render .Form nil}}

form_errors

func form_errors(errs form.FieldErrors, name string) []string

The messages errs holds for the field name, for a field a template writes itself, such as the errors of Frontend.BindForm (env.Frontend.BindForm) in the view of a module of the site's own.

{{range form_errors .Errors "email"}}<p class="wt-form__error">{{.}}</p>{{end}}

Texts and the form theme

Labels, descriptions and placeholders from the tags are translated with the site's translations. go-form's own texts, such as the "(required)" that screen readers announce after the label of a required field, use the site's entry when it has one; otherwise they show in go-form's own catalogue of the page's language, such as Dutch, also without a .po file, and in English for a language go-form has no catalogue for. When a theme or a module's default template uses form_open, form_field or form_render, task translations also finds the texts of the modules' forms, their option labels and submit texts included (see Languages).

The fields render with go-form's markup and the classes of webthings.css: wt-form, wt-form__field, wt-form__label, wt-form__input, wt-form__help, wt-form__error, wt-form__fieldset for a group of radio buttons or checkboxes, wt-form__options and wt-form__option for radio buttons and checkboxes, wt-form__row and wt-button, and form-honeypot for the spam trap, which webthings.css hides without a style attribute, so it stays hidden under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline'. A group of radio buttons (form:"radios") or checkboxes (form:"multicheckbox") is a fieldset with wt-form__field and wt-form__fieldset, its label the legend, with wt-form__label; its radio buttons or checkboxes are in wt-form__options, each in a wt-form__option, and a single checkbox is in a wt-form__option too. A poll's options are such a group: {{form_field .Form "option" nil}} writes them, with the question as their legend (see Polls). Config.FormTheme names another go-form theme, such as one with the classes of the site's own stylesheet, whose Honeypot names the class that hides the spam trap; see Themes and Configuration.

Translations

tl, tn, ctl and ctn are go-translator's functions. The translator frontend.Translations returns, which the site sets as Config.Translations, gives them the site's translations; without it they show every text as written. Their first argument is always localizer, the page's language. A language without a .po file of its own uses the one of its base language, or of a regional variant: nl_BE uses nl.po, and nl uses nl_NL.po, never another language. Languages covers the .po files.

tl

func tl(loc translator.Localizer, key string, args ...any) string

The translation of key in the page's language; args fill in %s and %d as fmt does. A text without a translation is shown as written.

{{tl localizer "Read more"}}
{{tl localizer "Comments (%d)" .Count}}

tn

func tn(loc translator.Localizer, singular, plural string, n int, args ...any) string

The singular or plural form for n, as the language counts it; pass the number again in args to show it.

{{tn localizer "%d comment" "%d comments" .Count .Count}}

ctl and ctn

func ctl(loc translator.Localizer, context, key string, args ...any) string
func ctn(loc translator.Localizer, context, singular, plural string, n int, args ...any) string

tl and tn with a context, for one English text that needs different translations.

<button>{{ctl localizer "button" "Close"}}</button>

All four show a text without a translation as written. tn and ctn then take the singular when n is 1 and the plural otherwise.

locale and localizer

func locale() string
func localizer() localization.Localizer

locale is the page's language, such as nl; localizer passes it to the translation functions.

<p lang="{{locale}}">{{tl localizer "Opening hours"}}</p>

Social media

The site's profiles are filled in under Site settings, Social media profiles. Labels are the networks' names, translated with the site's translations: the msgid is the name, such as Facebook or E-mail. task translations finds these names itself.

profiles

func profiles() []frontend.Profile

The site's social media profiles, each with Network (such as instagram), Label and URL. The layout has them as .Site.Profiles too.

{{range profiles}}<a href="{{.URL}}" rel="me" class="profile-{{.Network}}">{{.Label}}</a>{{end}}

share

func share(page, title string) []frontend.ShareLink

Links that share a page on Facebook, X, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, e-mail and Bluesky, each with Network (such as facebook), Label and URL. page is "" for the current page, a path such as /en/news/hello, or an absolute URL; paths become absolute with Config.BaseURL or the address of the request.

{{range share "" .Title}}<a href="{{.URL}}" class="share-{{.Network}}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">{{.Label}}</a>{{end}}

shareBar

func shareBar(page, title string) (template.HTML, error)

The same links rendered with core's share component, site/share.gohtml (see Themes).

{{shareBar "" .Title}}

Search

search

func search(query string, limit int) []frontend.SearchResult

Published pages and module content in the current language that contain every word of query, best first, each with Title, Summary, URL, Module, Type and Score. A limit of 0 or less gives at most 20 results, and never more than 100. See Search and SEO.

{{range search "glaze" 5}}<a href="{{.URL}}">{{.Title}}</a>{{end}}

searchURL is under Links and addresses.

Feeds

feedLinks

func feedLinks() template.HTML

A <link rel="alternate"> for each Atom and RSS feed of the page shown, for <head>, so browsers and feed readers find them. Core's head tags have it; a theme that writes its own tags puts it in regions/head.gohtml or the layout's <head>. The feeds are those of the module on the page: those it offers on every page of it, such as a news page's posts, and those it offers on the page shown, such as a category's posts on the category's page. Each feed gets an Atom link and then an RSS link, with the feed's title as readers see it, the title and the site's name, translated with the site's translations (the msgid is %[1]s from %[2]s), and an absolute address, with Config.BaseURL or the address of the request. Pages without feeds, such as content pages, get nothing, and so do error pages, such as the 404 a news page answers for a category that does not exist, and e-mail templates. See Themes.

<head>
    {{feedLinks}}
</head>

On the page of the category "Ceramics" of a news page, on the site "Atelier", this writes:

<link rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml" title="News from Atelier" href="https://example.com/en/news/feed.atom">
<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml" title="News from Atelier" href="https://example.com/en/news/feed.rss">
<link rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml" title="Ceramics from Atelier" href="https://example.com/en/news/category/ceramics/feed.atom">
<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml" title="Ceramics from Atelier" href="https://example.com/en/news/category/ceramics/feed.rss">

For a link visitors see, use feedURL.

feedURL

func feedURL(format string, name ...string) string

The address of a feed of the page shown in format, "atom" or "rss", for a link visitors see: the feed the module offers on the page shown, such as a category's posts on the category's page, or else the one it offers on every page of it, such as a news page's posts. A name picks the feed with that name instead, such as "feed" and "category-feed", the names of the publishing module's feeds. The address is a path, such as /en/news/feed.atom. Pages without feeds, an unknown format and a name the page has no feed of give "", and so do e-mail templates. In Go, Frontend.FeedURL(r, format, name...) gives the same. On an error page, such as the 404 a module answers for a category that does not exist, feedURL gives "" too. See Themes.

{{with feedURL "atom"}}
    <a href="{{.}}" type="application/atom+xml"{{noBoost runtime}}>Atom</a>
    <a href="{{feedURL "rss"}}" type="application/rss+xml"{{noBoost runtime}}>RSS</a>
{{end}}

On a news page this writes:

<a href="/en/news/feed.atom" type="application/atom+xml" hx-boost="false">Atom</a>
<a href="/en/news/feed.rss" type="application/rss+xml" hx-boost="false">RSS</a>

and on the page of its category "Ceramics":

<a href="/en/news/category/ceramics/feed.atom" type="application/atom+xml" hx-boost="false">Atom</a>
<a href="/en/news/category/ceramics/feed.rss" type="application/rss+xml" hx-boost="false">RSS</a>

A post's page has no feed of its own, so it gets the news page's. {{feedURL "atom" "feed"}} gives /en/news/feed.atom on all three. The module's README gives the names and addresses of its feeds, for example Publishing.

Content API

apiLink

func apiLink() template.HTML

A <link rel="alternate" type="application/json"> to the page shown in the content API, for <head>, so apps find its content. Core's head tags have it; a theme that writes its own tags puts it in regions/head.gohtml or the layout's <head>.
