A page links to /api/v1/pages/<id>?locale=<locale>, and an address below a module's page, such as a post's or a category's, to /api/v1/pages/resolve?path=<address>. The address is absolute, with Config.BaseURL or the address of the request. It writes nothing while the API is off, on an error page, such as the not-found page or the 404 a module answers for a post that does not exist, and in a preview of a revision, which the API never shows. In Go, Frontend.APILink(r) gives the address, or "" while the API is off and for a request on no page. See Search and SEO.

<head>
    {{apiLink}}
</head>

On the page /en/about, with Config.BaseURL set to https://example.com, this writes:

<link rel="alternate" type="application/json" href="https://example.com/api/v1/pages/01a116da-5fe0-72a3-9751-056f4b932fa7?locale=en">

and on the post /en/news/open-studio:

<link rel="alternate" type="application/json" href="https://example.com/api/v1/pages/resolve?path=%2Fen%2Fnews%2Fopen-studio">

Structured data

structuredData

func structuredData() (template.HTML, error)

The page's structured data for search engines, for <head>, where core's head tags write it last, or a theme's own tags in regions/head.gohtml or the layout's <head>: one <script type="application/ld+json"> with schema.org's @context and an @graph of the site's WebSite and Organization, the page's BreadcrumbList and WebPage, and the items of the module whose content the page shows, such as a post's Article, an event's Event or the ItemList of a news page's posts. Every address is absolute, with Config.BaseURL or the address of the request, and empty values are left out. html/template escapes <, > and & in the JSON, so no text in it can end the script. The not-found page, module screens with a status of 400 or more and the theme's 500.gohtml get nothing, and so do e-mail templates. 500.gohtml gets nothing for every failing page: a page whose template fails, and a module's handler or a visitor action that fails (Frontend.Fail). See Search and SEO.

<head>
    {{structuredData}}
</head>

On the home page of the site "Atelier Noord", with an e-mail address and an Instagram profile in the site settings, this writes:

<script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@id":"https://example.com/en/#website","@type":"WebSite","inLanguage":"en","name":"Atelier Noord","potentialAction":{"@type":"SearchAction","query-input":"required name=search_term_string","target":{"@type":"EntryPoint","urlTemplate":"https://example.com/en/search?q={search_term_string}"}},"publisher":{"@id":"https://example.com/#organization"},"url":"https://example.com/en/"},{"@id":"https://example.com/#organization","@type":"Organization","email":"hello@example.com","name":"Atelier Noord","sameAs":["https://www.instagram.com/ateliernoord"],"url":"https://example.com/en/"},{"@id":"https://example.com/en/","@type":"WebPage","inLanguage":"en","isPartOf":{"@id":"https://example.com/en/#website"},"name":"Home","url":"https://example.com/en/"}]}</script>

The home page has no BreadcrumbList, and the SearchAction is there because the theme has search.gohtml. A module adds its items with frontend.Content.StructuredData, and a list page its ItemList with frontend.ItemList(name, urls...); see Structured data for modules.

Layout and composition

content

func content() template.HTML

The content template, rendered with its data. Used once, in layout.gohtml.

<body>{{content}}</body>

template

Go's own template action includes a template from partials/ with the data you give it. The name is the path with its extension.

{{range posts "news" 3}}{{template "partials/post-card.gohtml" .}}{{end}}

partial and runtime

func partial(runtime *partial.Runtime, path string, args ...any) template.HTML
func runtime() *partial.Runtime

Render a template file of the theme through go-partial, with one value or key and value pairs as its data. Prefer template, which go-clue understands better. Each partial call renders the file on its own, which costs several times more than template, and key and value pairs arrive as an untyped map. For a part that HTMX asks for on its own by its ID, use a fragment of the theme, placed with requiredSlot, instead. The file can use @model values like any other template (see Templates).

{{partial runtime "partials/notice.gohtml" "Text" "Closed on Monday"}}

ctx

func ctx() *partial.RenderContext

go-partial's render context. Templates rarely need it.

oob, oobAttr and oobSwap

func oob() bool
func oobAttr(values ...string) template.HTMLAttr
func oobSwap(swap ...string) template.HTMLAttr

go-partial's helpers for HTMX out-of-band swaps, used in the theme's regions. When a region goes along with an HTMX navigation, oob is true and oobAttr writes hx-swap-oob="true", or the value given; on a whole page, and in other templates, oob is false and oobAttr writes nothing. oobSwap writes the attribute in every response, with the swap given, such as hx-swap-oob="beforeend", or hx-swap-oob="true" without one. See HTMX.

<nav id="menu" {{oobAttr}}>…</nav>

slot, requiredSlot and hasSlot

func slot(name string) template.HTML
func requiredSlot(name string) (template.HTML, error)
func hasSlot(name string) bool

go-partial's named slots, which hold the theme's regions and fragments: {{slot "menu"}} places regions/menu.gohtml in the layout, {{slot "head"}} places the tags of the page in the layout's <head>, regions/head.gohtml or core's head region for a theme without one (see The head region), {{slot "comments"}} places fragments/comments.gohtml with the page's content as its dot, and hasSlot "menu" reports whether the theme has it. An HTMX request aimed at a fragment's ID gets only the fragment. A fragment of search.gohtml, such as the results of a live search, comes with the regions out of band, so the <title> of the head region and the language links follow the query (render.View.FragmentRegions); fragments of other pages come alone. A name without a region or fragment gives "" and false. requiredSlot places a region or fragment like slot, but fails the render for a name without one, with slot "<name>" is not set, so a missing fragment does not go unnoticed. See Regions and Fragments in HTMX.

<header>{{slot "menu"}}</header>

<main id="content">
    <h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
    {{requiredSlot "comments"}}
</main>

deferredSlot

func deferredSlot(name string, mode ...string) (template.HTML, error)

A fragment that loads after the page. On a whole page it writes an empty element with the fragment's ID that asks the page's own address for the fragment: as soon as the page has loaded, or with "reveal" once the element scrolls into view. The page itself does not render the fragment, so a part that takes long to compute does not hold the page up. A name without a fragment writes nothing, and a region's name fails the render: a region goes out of band and cannot be deferred. A visitor form in such a fragment does not show a post with mistakes again, since the request for the page takes the kept post first; place it with slot or requiredSlot. See HTMX.

<aside>{{deferredSlot "popular" "reveal"}}</aside>

targetHeader, targetValue and targetIs

func targetHeader() string
func targetValue() string
func targetIs(ids ...string) bool

go-partial's helpers for the element an HTMX request is aimed at. targetValue is its ID, such as comments for HX-Target: section#comments, and "" for a whole page; targetIs reports whether it is one of ids; targetHeader is the header's name, HX-Target. See HTMX.

{{if targetIs "comments"}}<p role="status">Updated.</p>{{end}}

HTMX attributes

go-partial's exp/interactions writes htmx's attributes for an element of the template's own, so a theme does not spell them out. Each function takes runtime first, and its attributes start with a space, so it can follow the element's other attributes directly. Options come as name and value pairs: "target" and "swap" say where the answer goes and how (innerHTML when left out), "select" picks a part of the answer, "include", "pushURL" and "replaceURL" become hx-include, hx-push-url and hx-replace-url, and a name starting with hx-, data- or aria- is written as it is. Without a "target", the element itself is the target. Wrong arguments, such as an odd number of them, write a data-partial-error attribute with the error. See HTMX.

noBoost

func noBoost(runtime *partial.Runtime) template.HTMLAttr

hx-boost="false", for a link or form in a boosted body that must load a whole page, such as a link to the admin or to another language.

<a href="{{.URL}}" hreflang="{{.Locale}}"{{noBoost runtime}}>{{.Locale}}</a>

submitAttrs

func submitAttrs(runtime *partial.Runtime, endpoint string, params ...any) template.HTMLAttr

The attributes of a form that posts to endpoint with htmx and swaps the answer into its target: hx-post, hx-target and hx-swap. "method" picks another method, such as "put". Keep method and action on the form, so it works without JavaScript too.

<form method="post" action="{{commentURL "remarks"}}"{{submitAttrs runtime (commentURL "remarks") "target" "#remarks" "swap" "outerHTML"}}>

This writes hx-post="/_/remarks/post" hx-swap="outerHTML" hx-target="#remarks".

liveAttrs

func liveAttrs(runtime *partial.Runtime, endpoint string, params ...any) template.HTMLAttr

The attributes of a field that asks for endpoint while the visitor types, such as a search field: hx-get, hx-target, hx-swap and hx-trigger="input changed delay:300ms, search". "delay" changes the pause, and "include" sends other fields along, such as "closest form".

<input type="search" name="q" value="{{.Query}}"{{liveAttrs runtime .URL "target" "#results" "swap" "outerHTML" "replaceURL" "true"}}>

revealAttrs

func revealAttrs(runtime *partial.Runtime, endpoint string, params ...any) template.HTMLAttr

The attributes of an element that asks for endpoint once it scrolls into view, and swaps the answer into itself: hx-get, hx-target="this", hx-swap and hx-trigger="revealed". With the page's own address and a fragment's ID, the page answers with the fragment alone; deferredSlot writes such an element for a fragment of the theme (see HTMX).

{{/* @model View github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
<section id="popular"{{revealAttrs runtime View.Path "swap" "outerHTML"}}></section>

Other interaction functions

confirmAttr writes hx-confirm, and clientAttrs a confirmation, boosting, target and swap for a link or form; with "inherit" "true" they hold for every element inside, such as the body's for the whole page, where "disableWhileRequest" disables elements while a request runs and "keepOnServerError" "true" keeps the page as it is on a 5xx answer (see HTMX). With "reloadOnError" "true", a link or GET form that gets a 5xx answer, or none, loads as a whole page, and after a POST the server's error page replaces the page; this needs go-partial's browser client partial-interactions.js (see HTMX). asyncAttrs, pollAttrs, onAttrs, streamAttrs and refreshAttrs load an element's content when the page loads, at an interval, on an event, from a stream or on a click. go-partial's functions that write an element of their own, such as poll and reveal, are not among the template functions. go-partial documents them.

Debugging

debug

func debug(value any) template.HTML

A box that shows value, such as a template's dot, with its fields as indented JSON, or in Go syntax when it cannot be JSON. It works only with Config.Development; otherwise it shows nothing, so one that is left behind does no harm. A debug function of your own in Config.Funcs replaces it, also in development. See Templates.

{{debug .}}         the template's dot
{{debug .Site}}     in the layout: the site's name, address and more

The box is go-partial's, styled by one <style> element in it. In development the site's own Content-Security-Policy (see A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own) allows that element by its hash, go-partial's debug.StyleHash() (ext/debug). Another policy without 'unsafe-inline' in style-src blocks it unless it has that hash; the value then shows unstyled.

Module functions

Every module in app.Use adds its functions to every template; their first argument is the instance key. A module's functions exist only when the site uses it. Their signatures, data and examples are in the module's documentation, also at https://modules.gowebthings.com.

Module Functions
Banners banners, banner
Comments comments, commentCount, commentURL, commentResult, commentsClosed, commentThread, commentForm, commentInput
Directory directoryEntries, directoryEntry, directoryCategories
Documents documents, documentsIn
Events events
Gallery albums, album
Lists entries
Newsletter newsletter, newsletterURL, newsletterResult, newsletterForm
People people, peopleIn, person
Polls poll, polls, pollURL, pollBox
Publishing posts
Registrations registration, registerURL, registrationResult, registrationCode, registrationForm
Stats pageViews, popular
Submissions submitURL, submitResult, submitInput
Testimonials testimonials

Forms and Redirects add no functions.

{{range posts "news" 3}}<a href="{{.URL}}">{{.Title}}</a>{{end}}
{{range events "agenda" 5}}{{date .Start "full"}}: {{.Title}}{{end}}
{{commentThread "remarks" .ID}}

Components and e-mail

Components render through go-partial as parts of the page, children of the template that includes them, with the page's request and language. They get every function on this page, go-partial's included, and the same render stages as the page, so debug works there with Config.Development. A component that fails fails the page. content fails in a component; slot and requiredSlot place the page's fragments, as in the template that includes the component.

Every part of an e-mail renders through go-partial too, the subject and text as plain text, with every function on this page and the same render stages, but without a request or a page: request and url give nothing, urlIs is false, content and requiredSlot fail, and slot and deferredSlot write nothing. Without the site's translations, tl, tn, ctl and ctn still work in every part and show the text as written.

An e-mail has no visitor's page: adminURL gives "", and moduleURL, searchURL, asset and image give paths without the site's address. absURL makes a path absolute only with Config.BaseURL. See E-mail.

Guides.Title: Themes
Guides.Summary: A theme is one design of the site: a folder of templates and assets. Editors choose the active theme in the admin, preview it and change its settings, such as colours. Theme checklist lists what a theme needs.
Guides.Body:
Theme folders

Every folder in templates/ that has a layout.gohtml or a theme.json is a theme. default/ is the base: another theme only holds what differs from it, and finds the templates, partials, regions, fragments, components, e-mail templates and assets it lacks in default/. A colour variant can be a single stylesheet:

templates/
  default/
    layout.gohtml
    page.gohtml
    news/post.gohtml
    partials/post-card.gohtml
    regions/head.gohtml
    regions/menu.gohtml
    fragments/comments.gohtml
    assets/site.css
    assets/variant.css
    theme.json
  night/
    assets/variant.css      replaces default's variant.css
    theme.json              the night theme's title and settings

Folder names are lowercase letters, digits, - and _. Other folders are ignored.

A site with layout.gohtml directly in templates/ has a single theme, default, made of the whole folder; its subfolders are then not themes.

For a module screen, a component and an e-mail template, a theme's own files come before those of default/, and within each folder the instance-key file wins over the type file: with default/news/post.gohtml and night/publishing/post.gohtml, the night theme shows news posts with night/publishing/post.gohtml, and with default/remarks/form.gohtml and night/comments/form.gohtml, the remarks form with night/comments/form.gohtml.

The starter has a second, complete theme next to default/: editorial/, with its own layout, regions, fragments and module screens, so it needs nothing from default/. Its module screens are in the type's folders: editorial/publishing/list.gohtml and editorial/publishing/post.gohtml show the posts of both news and blog, where default/ has news/ and blog/, and events/ and registrations/ serve agenda and signup the same way.

Themes are read when the site starts. Restart it after adding a theme or changing a theme.json, also with Config.ReloadTemplates.

theme.json

theme.json is optional. It gives the theme a title and description for the admin, and declares settings that editors change there:

{
  "title": "Atelier",
  "description": "Warm paper tones, clay accents and serif headings.",
  "settings": [
    {"name": "accent", "label": {"en": "Accent colour", "nl": "Accentkleur"}, "type": "color", "default": "#b5562f", "css": "--accent"},
    {"name": "headings", "label": "Headings", "type": "select", "options": ["serif", "sans"], "default": "serif"},
    {"name": "notice", "label": "Notice", "type": "text"},
    {"name": "measure", "label": "Text width", "type": "number", "min": 32, "max": 52, "step": 1, "unit": "rem", "default": "42", "css": "--measure"}
  ]
}

Without a title, the folder name is used. A csp object names the addresses of other sites that the theme's pages load from, such as a font host, for the site's Content-Security-Policy (see Outside sources).

"screenshot": "screenshot.png" names a picture of the theme: a PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or GIF image in the theme's assets/ folder, by its path there, such as screenshot.png or img/preview.jpg. The admin's theme cards show it, in the Theme section and in the Theme step of Getting started; while one theme has a picture, the others get a placeholder of the same size with their title. A path that does not stay inside assets/, such as /shot.png, ../shot.png or ./shot.png, another kind of file and a file that does not exist stop the site at start with an error that names the theme, such as theme default: screenshot "notes.txt": use a PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or GIF image.

Each setting has these fields:

Field Meaning
name How templates read the setting: lowercase letters, digits, - and _
label What editors see: one text, or an object of language codes shown in the admin's language
type color, text, select or number
options The choices of a select
min, max The lowest and highest value of a number, both allowed; a number needs both
step The difference between the values of a number, counted exactly from min, such as 0.5; 0, or left out, allows any value between min and max. "step": 0.1 allows 0.3, and "min": 0.25 with "step": 0.5 allows 0.75 but not 1
unit The CSS unit of a number, which the values stylesheet writes after it: px, rem, em, ch, ex, %, vw, vh, vmin, vmax, s, ms, deg or turn, or none, such as for a line height
default The value until an editor chooses one; for a number, the number alone, such as "42"
css For a color, select or number: the custom property, such as --accent, that the theme's values stylesheet sets to the value (see Settings)
Type Admin field Accepted values
color A colour picker A colour like #1a2b3c, stored in lowercase
text A text field Up to 500 characters
select A list One of options
number A number field with min, max and step, and the unit after the label, such as "Text width (rem)" A number from min to max on a step, stored as the number alone, such as 42

A theme does not inherit settings from default/: each theme.json declares its own, even when they have the same names. A theme.json that is not valid JSON, or a setting with an invalid name, an unknown type, a select without options, a number without min and max, with min above max, a negative step or an unknown unit, a default that does not fit or a css that is not allowed (see Settings), or a csp directive or source that is not allowed (see Outside sources), stops the site at start with an error that names the theme.

Settings

The layout reads the active theme's settings as {{.Theme.Values.accent}}, and {{theme "accent"}} works in every template, including components and e-mail. Each declared setting has a value: the editor's choice or the default. A number gives the number alone, without its unit: {{theme "measure"}} is 42. A stored value that no longer fits its setting, such as a colour after the setting became a select, or a number outside a new range, gives the default. A name the theme does not declare gives "", and {{theme}} logs it once with the names the theme has, such as theme: no setting "acent" in theme default (known: accent); with Config.Development the page fails with that message (see Calls that find nothing). .Theme.Name is the theme's folder name.

A setting reaches the stylesheet in one of two ways, a custom property or a data attribute. Neither needs a style attribute or a <style> element, so the page works under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' for styles (see Under a Content-Security-Policy).

The values stylesheet

A color, select or number setting with css becomes a custom property of the theme's values stylesheet, which core serves at /theme/<theme>/values.css. {{themeStyle}} writes its <link>, with a version and its integrity like assetStyle (see Template functions). It must come after the theme's own stylesheets, so its properties replace their fallbacks; {{styles}} links it last by itself:

{{styles "site.css"}}

A layout without {{styles}} writes {{assetStyle "site.css"}} and then {{themeStyle}}.

/* site.css */
:root { --accent: #b5562f; --measure: 42rem; }

a { color: var(--accent); }
main { max-width: var(--measure); }

With the theme.json above, the values stylesheet is:

:root {
    --accent: #b5562f;
    --measure: 42rem;
}

A number goes in with its unit, so "unit": "rem" and the value 42 give --measure: 42rem;, and a number without a unit, such as a line height of 1.5, gives --leading: 1.5;.

css is the name of a custom property: --, a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and -. Two settings of a theme cannot set the same one, and a text setting cannot have css. A select with css may only have options of letters, digits, spaces and #, ., ,, % and -, such as serif, 1.25rem or #fff, so no option can end the rule. The site does not start with anything else. Each value is checked again before it goes into the stylesheet: a colour must be like #1a2b3c, a select's value one of its options, and a number between min and max on a step. A stored value that does not fit gives the default, and a setting without a value, such as a colour without a default that no editor chose, is left out. A theme without such settings has no values stylesheet: {{themeStyle}} writes nothing and the address answers 404.

The stylesheet follows the saved values: a changed value gives it a new version, so its address changes and pages link the new one. The address with the current version is sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, any other with Cache-Control: no-cache, and every response has an ETag. A preview in the admin links the values stylesheet of the theme it shows, with that theme's saved values. values.css is a reserved name below /theme/<theme>/: a theme's own assets/values.css is not served there, so a stylesheet of the theme needs another name. The layout task templates -- site writes links it with {{styles}}, after its stylesheets.

Data attributes

A setting with a few fixed designs can be an attribute of <html> instead, with a rule for each option in the stylesheet:

<html lang="{{.Locale}}" data-headings="{{.Theme.Values.headings}}">

[data-headings="sans"] h1, [data-headings="sans"] h2 { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }

The demo's two themes and the starter's default/ have a colour picker for their accent, with "css": "--accent", and link it with {{styles}}; the demo writes its headings, serif or sans, as data-headings. The starter's editorial/ keeps a choice of four accents, vermilion, ink, forest and plum, written as data-accent: each is a designed pair of a light and a dark shade whose contrast with the page's background passes WCAG AA in both modes, which a free colour could not promise. It writes the typeface of its text, serif or sans, as data-text. The width of its column of text is a number, measure, from 32 to 52 rem in steps of 1 and 42 by default, with "css": "--measure", which its layout links with {{styles}}.

Choosing a theme in the admin

The admin's Theme section lists the themes with their title, description and picture (see theme.json), and marks the active one. It needs the same rights as Site settings, and is hidden when the site has no themes. Without the edit right there, it has no Use this theme and shows the settings read-only, with a note.

  • Settings shows a theme's settings. Each theme keeps its own values, so a theme can be set up before it is used. A value equal to the default is not stored, so a new default in theme.json still applies. A value that does not fit its type, such as a text over 500 characters, shows its message at the field, and nothing is saved.
  • Preview opens the home page in that theme, with its saved settings, in a new tab. /admin/theme/preview/<theme>?path=/en/about previews another page; /admin is the default admin path (see Admin path). Links in the preview lead to the public site in the active theme.
  • Use this theme makes it the active theme. It asks first, "Use this theme on the website? Visitors see it right away.", since the website changes at once.

Until an editor chooses one, and when the chosen theme no longer exists, the site uses the first theme: default, then the others by name.

Assets

Files in a theme's assets/ folder are served below /theme/:

Address Serves
/theme/<theme>/<file> The file from that theme, or from default/ when the theme lacks it
/theme/<theme>/values.css The theme's values stylesheet, made by core from its settings (see The values stylesheet)
/theme/<file> The file from the active theme

{{asset "site.css"}} is the address of a file in the theme being rendered, with a version from the file's content, such as /theme/default/site.css?v=9b2ca0fe143be1a4. The version changes when the file does, so an address with the current version is sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; any other address, such as one without a version or with an old one, is sent with Cache-Control: no-cache. Every response has an ETag, so a browser checks a file again cheaply. Subfolders work: {{asset "img/logo.svg"}}. Files and folders whose name starts with a dot are not served.

The versions are worked out once per theme, so restart the site after changing an asset; until then its address keeps the old version. Config.ReloadTemplates looks at the folder again for every request and gives a changed file a new version, for development.

{{assetStyle "site.css"}} and {{assetScript "site.js"}} write the <link rel="stylesheet"> or <script> tag of a file at that address, with the file's integrity and crossorigin="anonymous", so the browser refuses a file whose content is not what the page expects; more attributes follow as name and value pairs. With Config.ReloadTemplates the theme's files get no integrity, since they may change while the site runs; core's webthings.css, focal-points.css and partial-errors.css keep it (see Template functions).

{{assetStyle "site.css"}}
{{assetStyle "variant.css"}}
{{assetScript "site.js" "defer" ""}}

{{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}} writes the stylesheet links of <head> in the order they must have: go-partial's partial-errors.css first (see The error box), then the files given, each once and in that order, as assetStyle links them, and the theme's values stylesheet last (see The values stylesheet). A file comes from the theme's assets/, or from core when the theme has none of that name, such as webthings.css and focal-points.css. None of them is a <style> element, so the page works under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' (see Template functions).

A file that neither the theme nor core has gives its address without a version or integrity, and asset, assetStyle, assetScript and styles log it once with the closest names there are, such as assetStyle: no file "sitee.css" in the assets of theme default (closest: site.css, webthings.css, focal-points.css); with Config.Development the page fails with that message (see Calls that find nothing).

Config.Assets is one more folder, shared by all themes and served at /assets/ with versions and ETags like a theme's assets: {{importmap_url "site.css"}} is the address of a file with its version, such as /assets/site.css?v=9b2ca0fe143be1a4, {{importmap_style "site.css"}} and {{importmap_script "site.js"}} write its <link> or <script> tag with its integrity (see Template functions), and a plain /assets/site.css is sent with Cache-Control: no-cache. Core adds go-partial's browser clients to the folder, so {{importmap}} maps partial-flash, partial-sse and partial-interactions for the theme's scripts; a file of the same name in the folder replaces core's. The folder's versions are worked out when the site starts; with Config.ReloadTemplates a changed file gets a new version, like a theme's, and neither the tags nor the import map carry integrity (see Configuration). Config.ImportMap serves the files of a go-importmap import map there instead, the same way, with go-partial's clients added to its map with their integrity; a client's file among the map's own files is used instead of core's. The demo and the starter vendor htmx this way (see HTMX). A site sets one of the two; with both, it does not start.

Feeds

Modules can offer Atom and RSS feeds, such as the posts of a news page at /en/news/feed.atom and /en/news/feed.rss. {{feedLinks}} in <head> lets browsers and feed readers find them. Core's head tags have it, so a layout that places {{slot "head"}} links the feeds without more (see The head region); a head region that replaces core's tags, or a layout without the slot, writes {{feedLinks}} itself.

{{feedLinks}} writes a <link rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml"> and a <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml"> for each feed of the page shown, with absolute addresses, and nothing on pages without feeds or on error pages, also a module's 404 (see Template functions). The starter's and the demo's themes get it from core's head tags. A module offers feeds with Parts.Feeds; see Feeds for modules.

{{feedLinks}} is for browsers and feed readers. A link visitors see takes the feed's address from {{feedURL "atom"}} or {{feedURL "rss"}} (see Template functions): the feed of the page shown, such as /en/news/category/updates/feed.atom on a category's page, or else the module's, such as /en/news/feed.atom, and "" on a page without feeds and on an error page. In a body that HTMX boosts, give the link {{noBoost runtime}}, so the browser opens the feed instead of swapping it into the page. The starter's editorial theme has such links below its lists of posts and events:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing.ListView */}}
{{with feedURL "atom"}}
    <a href="{{.}}" type="application/atom+xml"{{noBoost runtime}}>Atom</a>
    <a href="{{feedURL "rss"}}" type="application/rss+xml"{{noBoost runtime}}>RSS</a>
{{end}}

Regions and fragments

A theme that uses HTMX has two more folders:

Folder Holds
regions/ Parts of the layout that change from page to page, such as regions/menu.gohtml or regions/head.gohtml with the tags of the page in <head>. The layout places one with {{slot "menu"}}; it gets the page, a frontend.View, and follows every HTMX navigation out of band, in the order of the file names.
fragments/ Parts of a page that HTMX asks for on their own, such as fragments/comments.gohtml. A template places one with {{requiredSlot "comments"}} or {{slot "comments"}}, or after the page with {{deferredSlot "comments"}}; it gets the page's content, and a request aimed at #comments gets only the fragment.

A region's outer element carries its name as id and {{oobAttr}}, except the head region's; a fragment's carries its name as id. Both can use the theme's partials/. HTMX covers them.

The head region

The layout places the tags of the page in <head> with {{slot "head"}}. A theme without regions/head.gohtml gets core's head region, the tags of webthings/head-tags.gohtml:

  • the <title>, the description, and <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> in a preview;
  • the canonical link, and the hreflang links with x-default;
  • og:title, og:description, og:type, og:url, og:site_name, og:locale, og:image and twitter:card;
  • the favicon and the apple-touch-icon;
  • {{feedLinks}}, {{apiLink}} and {{structuredData}}.

Static tags, such as <meta charset>, the stylesheets and scripts, stay in the layout:

<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    {{slot "head"}}
    {{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}}
</head>

Language.Default marks the site's default language among .Languages. With more than one language, core's tags give that language's address as hreflang="x-default", for visitors whose language the site does not have (see Search and SEO). A page with status 400 or above, such as the not-found page, gets no canonical link, alternates, og:url or structured data.

{{structuredData}} writes what the page is about for search engines: one <script type="application/ld+json"> with the site, its organisation, the page's trail, the page, and the module's item for the content shown, such as a post's Article, an event's Event or the ItemList of a news page's posts (see Search and SEO). Like the other tags of the region, it changes with every HTMX navigation. {{apiLink}} writes a <link rel="alternate" type="application/json"> to the page shown in the content API, for apps: /api/v1/pages/<id>?locale=<locale> for a page, and /api/v1/pages/resolve?path=<address> below a module's page, such as for a post, with absolute addresses. It writes nothing while the API is off, on the not-found page and in a preview (see Template functions).

For tags of its own, a theme adds regions/head.gohtml and calls core's tags in it. It gets the View, like the layout, and needs no id and no {{oobAttr}}. The head region task templates -- site writes (App.WriteTemplates(dir, "site")) is such a file, with the theme's own tags as a comment to fill in, such as:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
{{template "webthings/head-tags.gohtml" .}}
<meta name="theme-color" content="#336699">

A head region that does not call webthings/head-tags.gohtml replaces core's tags: it writes the <title> and the other tags itself, with {{feedLinks}}, {{apiLink}} and {{structuredData}} where it wants them. A layout without {{slot "head"}} gets nothing from core and writes its tags in <head> itself.

An HTMX navigation replaces the region's tags with those of the new page, so none of the page left stays behind; a Back or Forward that htmx restores from its history is the exception (see The head region). A site without HTMX uses the region the same way; it renders in place on every page. The starter's and the demo's themes use core's head region. Search and SEO covers the tags.

Components

The interactive modules render components: parts of a page that any template includes with one function. Their default markup is plain, accessible HTML with stable class names in BEM style, and texts through tl, so the site's translations apply. It has no style attributes and no <style> elements, so it works under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' for styles.

Component Function Default markup
Comment thread {{commentThread "remarks" .ID}} wt-comments, wt-comment, wt-comment__body, wt-comment--staff
Comment form {{commentForm "remarks" .ID}} wt-comment-form
Poll {{pollBox "survey" "colour"}} wt-poll, wt-poll__question, wt-poll__results, wt-poll__result, wt-poll__bar
Newsletter signup {{newsletterForm "letters"}} wt-newsletter, wt-newsletter__title, wt-newsletter__note
Event sign-up {{registrationForm "signup" .ID}} wt-registration, wt-registration__facts
Share links (core) {{shareBar "" .Title}} wt-share, wt-share__list, wt-share__link

Forms share wt-form, wt-form__field, wt-form__label, wt-form__input and wt-button, and a group of radio buttons or checkboxes is a fieldset with wt-form__field and wt-form__fieldset, its question a legend with wt-form__label; radio buttons and checkboxes, such as the options of a poll, are in wt-form__options with a wt-form__option for each, and a single checkbox has a wt-form__option too; messages use wt-notice, small print wt-meta, and wt-visually-hidden hides text from sight but not from screen readers. A poll's result bar is a <meter class="wt-poll__bar"> with the percentage as its value, and the percentage is also written as text, in wt-poll__percent. webthings.css fills the bar with --wt-accent whatever region its value is in, so a theme's own poll markup with low, high or optimum on the meter gets the accent too, not the browser's red or yellow. The module READMEs describe the components, for example Comments and Polls.

Replacing a component

A theme replaces a component with a template of its own, found like a module screen (see Theme folders):

Component Theme file
Comments <key>/thread.gohtml and <key>/form.gohtml, or comments/thread.gohtml and comments/form.gohtml
Polls <key>/box.gohtml, or polls/box.gohtml
Newsletter <key>/form.gohtml, or newsletter/form.gohtml
Registrations <key>/form.gohtml, or registrations/form.gohtml
Share links site/share.gohtml

Without one, the module's default renders. Start from the default: task templates -- remarks writes remarks/thread.gohtml and remarks/form.gohtml (with the instance's other templates), and task templates -- site writes site/share.gohtml. Move a copy to the type's folder, such as comments/, to use it for every instance.

A component template gets the component's data, can use the theme's partials/ and every template function, go-partial's included (see Template functions). Like the other templates, components are read once per theme: restart the site after changing one, or set Config.ReloadTemplates while you develop (see Templates).

Forms

Fields a template renders with form_field and the other form_* functions (see Template functions) have go-form's markup with the classes of webthings.css, from the go-form theme frontend.FormTheme: wt-form, wt-form__field, wt-form__label, wt-form__input, wt-form__help, wt-form__error, wt-form__fieldset for a group of radio buttons or checkboxes, wt-form__options and wt-form__option for radio buttons and checkboxes, wt-form__row and wt-button. A group of radio buttons (form:"radios") or checkboxes (form:"multicheckbox") renders as a fieldset, with the field's classes and wt-form__fieldset, and its label as the legend, with the label's classes; webthings.css takes away the browser's border and padding of the fieldset and lays out the legend like a label. The "(required)" after the label of a required field is for screen readers only: a span with the class sr-only, which webthings.css hides inside wt-form__field.

form_open also writes the spam trap, a text field named website that people do not see and many bots fill in (see The hidden fields). frontend.FormTheme gives it the class form-honeypot, which webthings.css hides, so the field needs no style attribute and the form works under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline'. The admin's form theme and stylesheet do the same.

Config.FormTheme names another go-form theme: one of go-form's own, bootstrap, tailwind, tailwindv4 or plain, or one the site registers with the classes of its own stylesheet before it starts, with go-form's github.com/donseba/go-form/v2/templates, as the demo does:

// go-form's markup with the classes of the theme's site.css.
if _, err := templates.RegisterClassTheme("atelier", templates.ThemeClasses{
    Wrapper:     templates.StyleOption{Class: "field"},
    Description: templates.StyleOption{Class: "help"},
    Error:       templates.StyleOption{Class: "error"},
    Button:      templates.StyleOption{Class: "button"},
    // The spam trap, hidden by site.css.
    Honeypot: templates.StyleOption{Class: templates.HoneypotClass},
}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

app := webthings.New(webthings.Config{
    Templates: os.DirFS("templates"),
    FormTheme: "atelier",
})

Such a theme's stylesheet hides .sr-only itself. It also takes away the border and padding of the fieldset of a group of radio buttons or checkboxes and styles its legend like a label, as the demo's site.css does with fieldset.field and .field legend. ThemeClasses.Fieldset and Legend give the fieldset and the legend classes of their own, on top of those of Wrapper and Label. A name go-form does not know fails every page with a form.

ThemeClasses.Honeypot names the class of the spam trap, which the theme's stylesheet hides; the field then has no style attribute. The demo uses templates.HoneypotClass, form-honeypot, with a rule for it in its site.css. Without Honeypot, go-form gives the field the class form-honeypot and an inline style that hides it, which a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' blocks; a rule for .form-honeypot, such as the one in webthings.css, still hides it then. go-form's bootstrap theme hides the field with the class visually-hidden, and tailwind and tailwindv4 with sr-only.

The base stylesheet

Core has one optional stylesheet that lays out the default components: spacing, forms, lists and poll bars. Include it in the layout before your own stylesheet:

{{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}}

Core serves it at /_/webthings.css, with a version, its integrity and caching like a theme's assets. A theme with its own assets/webthings.css gets that file from {{styles "webthings.css"}}, {{assetStyle "webthings.css"}} and {{asset "webthings.css"}} instead. Every rule is wrapped in :where(), so it has no specificity and any rule of the theme wins; only the rules that hide sr-only text in forms and the spam trap, form-honeypot, have the weight of one class. Leave it out to style the wt-* classes yourself.

The stylesheet takes its colours and spacing from custom properties a theme sets:

Property Default Used for
--wt-accent #2b59c3 Buttons, badges, focus outlines, poll bars and the edge of notices
--wt-accent-text #ffffff Text on buttons and badges
--wt-border rgb(0 0 0 / 0.18) Borders of fields, boxes and share links
--wt-muted rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6) Small print and help texts
--wt-surface rgb(0 0 0 / 0.035) The background of notices
--wt-bar rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08) The track of poll bars
--wt-radius 0.375rem Corner radius
--wt-gap 1rem Spacing between parts
--wt-field-width 32rem The maximum width of forms
--wt-error #b42318 The errors of form fields 
:root {
    --wt-accent: #b5562f;
    --wt-radius: 0;
    --wt-gap: 1.25rem;
}

A theme setting feeds them (see Settings). The starter's default/ sets --wt-accent: var(--accent) in its site.css, and the values stylesheet, which {{styles}} links last, sets --accent to the colour chosen in the admin. Its editorial theme does the same through its data attribute:

:root {
    --accent: #b93c0b;
    --wt-accent: var(--accent);
}

:root[data-accent="forest"] { --accent: #2f6b3a; }

Focal points

Core serves a second optional stylesheet, focal-points.css, at /_/focal-points.css: one class for each position of an image's focal point in steps of 5%, from .fp-0-0 to .fp-100-100, the horizontal position first, each setting object-position. {{focalClass}} gives an image the class of its focal point, so a photo the browser crops with object-fit: cover keeps it in view without a style attribute (see Crops in the browser). Include it in the layout:

{{styles "site.css" "focal-points.css"}}

It has a version, its integrity and caching like webthings.css, and a theme with its own assets/focal-points.css gets that file instead. Each rule has the weight of one class, so a rule of the theme that sets object-position with more weight, such as .card > img, wins over it. The demo's layout includes it for the photos of its cards.

The error box

Core serves a third optional stylesheet, go-partial's partial-errors.css, at /_/partial-errors.css. It styles the box that takes the place of a part of the page that failed, such as the answer to an HTMX request whose template fails in development (see While you develop). The box has go-partial's classes, go-partial-error, go-partial-error__title, go-partial-error__message and go-partial-error__details, and no inline style, so a Content-Security-Policy does not block it; without the stylesheet it shows as a plain heading, paragraph and list. {{styles}} links it first, so a layout with {{styles}} needs nothing more; a layout without it includes it with:

{{assetStyle "partial-errors.css"}}

It has a version, its integrity and caching like webthings.css, and a theme with its own assets/partial-errors.css gets that file instead. The layout task templates -- site writes links it with {{styles}}, and so do the starter's and the demo's.

Under a Content-Security-Policy

The site can send a Content-Security-Policy that lets browsers run only the scripts and styles the site serves itself. Administrators turn it on under Site settings › Security, unless Config.ContentSecurityPolicy sets it: the card then shows that mode, which cannot be changed there. Report only blocks nothing and logs what the policy would block, enforce blocks it (see A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own). The policy has no 'unsafe-inline' and no 'unsafe-eval'. Core's own inline code is allowed by its hash in every page's policy: the import map that {{importmap}} writes, the <style> element of go-partial's plain error page, and in development that of the {{debug}} box. Anything else inline is blocked, so a theme for such a site has:

  • no style attribute, also not one with {{objectPosition}}: {{focalClass}} gives an image its focal point as a class (see Focal points), and settings reach the stylesheet without one (see Settings);
  • no <style> element and no inline <script>. A data block, such as <script type="application/json"> or the application/ld+json of {{structuredData}}, does not run, so the policy does not block it;
  • no event handler attribute, such as onclick, and none of what htmx runs as JavaScript: hx-on* attributes, trigger filters, and js: or javascript: values in hx-vals, hx-headers or hx-confirm (see HTMX).

The starting points, the modules' default templates and the starter's and the demo's themes keep to these rules. A <style> or <script> element a theme cannot do without needs its hash in csp (see Outside sources).

Outside sources

A theme that loads files from another site, such as fonts from a font host, names those addresses in its theme.json, by directive:

{
  "title": "Atelier",
  "csp": {
    "font-src": ["https://fonts.example.com"],
    "style-src": ["https://fonts.example.com"]
  }
}

The policy of the theme's pages, and of its preview in the admin, then allows them besides the site's own files while the policy is on (report only or enforce); with the policy off the preview sends only the admin's frame-ancestors 'none': here font-src 'self' https://fonts.example.com, and https://fonts.example.com in style-src. The sources under Site settings › Security and in Config.ContentSecuritySources apply in every theme.

The directives are connect-src, font-src, form-action, frame-src, img-src, manifest-src, media-src, script-src, style-src and worker-src, in lowercase. Each source is one of:

  • an address with the scheme http, https, ws or wss, such as https://www.youtube-nocookie.com, https://*.example.com/embed/ or wss://live.example.com:8443;
  • 'self';
  • the scheme https:, wss:, data: or blob:, except in script-src;
  • the hash of one inline script or style, such as 'sha256-…', in script-src and style-src only.

Anything else, such as 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', *, a nonce, 'strict-dynamic' or another directive such as default-src, stops the site at start:

theme default: csp script-src ['unsafe-inline']: invalid_csp_source

site.CheckCSPSources does the check, the same as for the sources under Site settings › Security. frontend.Theme.CSP holds a theme's sources, and Frontend.ThemeCSP returns those of the theme a request renders in: the active theme, or the one the admin previews.

Starting points for a theme

The starter's task templates writes into the theme named by WEBTHINGS_THEME, default when it is unset:

WEBTHINGS_THEME=night task templates -- remarks

A copy in a theme replaces the one in default/ for that theme, also when the copy is a plain starting point. Delete the copies you do not change. See Templates.

Guides.Title: Theme checklist
Guides.Summary: What a theme needs, in one list. Core does much of the work: it writes the tags in <head>, links the stylesheets in their order, and checks every template when the site starts. Each item links to the guide that explains it. The starter's templates/default/ is a small complete theme to compare with.
Guides.Body:
Files

File Needed Without it
layout.gohtml In default/; another theme uses that one unless it has its own A folder without layout.gohtml or theme.json is not a theme, and a site without any theme answers with a plain-text page that names the templates to add
page.gohtml Yes Every content page answers with status 500 and missing_template
<key>/<name>.gohtml or <type>/<name>.gohtml For each screen of each module placed on a page That screen answers with status 500; the start logs missing template with the task templates -- <key> that writes it
404.gohtml Recommended A plain-text "404 page not found"
500.gohtml Recommended go-partial's plain error page, in the page's language
search.gohtml When the site has a search form /<locale>/search answers 404
theme.json Optional The folder name as the title, and no settings
regions/head.gohtml Optional Core's head tags

Components and e-mail templates have defaults: copy one only to change it. A module screen with a visitor form gives the element around the form the instance key as its id, such as <section id="{{.Key}}">, so the form returns the visitor there (see Module templates). A theme other than default/ holds only what differs from default/ (see Theme folders). task templates -- site writes the layout, its head region, assets/site.css, page.gohtml, 404.gohtml and search.gohtml, and task templates -- <key> a module's screens (see Starting points and When something goes wrong).

The layout

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="{{.Locale}}">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    {{slot "head"}}
    {{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}}
</head>
<body>
    {{content}}
</body>
</html>
  • <html lang="{{.Locale}}"> gives the page's language.
  • <meta charset> and the viewport stay in the layout: core's head tags do not write them.
  • {{slot "head"}} places core's head tags: the title, the description, the canonical and hreflang links, the sharing tags, the icons, the feeds, the link to the content API and the structured data. For tags of your own, add regions/head.gohtml and call {{template "webthings/head-tags.gohtml" .}} first; a head region without that call replaces core's tags (see The head region).
  • {{styles}} links partial-errors.css first, then the files given in their order, and the values stylesheet of the theme's settings last. Leave out webthings.css to style the wt-* classes yourself, and add focal-points.css when the theme uses {{focalClass}} (see styles).
  • {{content}} places the content template.
  • Around it, the menu from .Menu, the language links from .Languages, the edit link from .Editor and the preview banner from .Revision (see The layout).

With HTMX navigation

  • Every content template, 404.gohtml, search.gohtml and the module screens included, wraps its content in <main id="content"> (see Navigation that swaps only the content).
  • A region's outer element carries the region's name as id and {{oobAttr}}, and is written on every page, empty when there is nothing to show. The head region needs neither (see Regions).
  • The language links and the links to the admin have {{noBoost runtime}}, so they load a whole page.
  • htmx 4 is loaded, for example with the import map (see Loading htmx).

Under a Content-Security-Policy

  • No style attribute: {{focalClass}} gives an image its focal point as a class, and a setting reaches the stylesheet with css or as a data attribute (see Settings).
  • No <style> element and no inline <script>. A data block, such as <script type="application/json">, is fine.
  • No event handler attribute, such as onclick, and no hx-on* attribute, trigger filter or js: value (see Under a Content-Security-Policy).
  • Files from another site, such as fonts, are named in theme.json under csp (see Outside sources).

Regions and fragments follow the same rules: what htmx swaps into the page runs under the page's policy. See Under a Content-Security-Policy.

Check it

  • Run the site with task dev. Templates are read again on every request, the start fails with every template problem at once, and a call that finds nothing, such as {{theme "acent"}}, fails its page (see While you work on the templates and Checking the templates at start).
  • Restart the site after adding a theme or changing a theme.json, also with task dev.
  • Open each kind of page once: the home page, a content page, every module screen, an address that does not exist and the search.
  • Choose Report only, block nothing under Site settings › Security, use the site, and read the log: each content security policy violation names what the theme must change (see A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own).

Guides.Title: HTMX
Guides.Summary: With HTMX, a theme swaps only the part of a page that changes: a link replaces the content while the menu and the title follow, and a form updates only its own box. Every address still answers with a whole page, so the site keeps working without JavaScript.
Guides.Body:
How it fits together

The public site answers HTMX requests with the htmx 4 protocol. A theme offers HTMX three kinds of parts:

Part Lives in Its dot HTMX gets it
The content <main id="content"> around each content template The content template's data For a request aimed at #content, such as a boosted link
A region regions/<name>.gohtml, placed by the layout with {{slot "<name>"}} The page, a frontend.View Out of band, with every response that swaps the content
A fragment fragments/<name>.gohtml, placed with {{requiredSlot "<name>"}}, {{slot "<name>"}} or {{deferredSlot "<name>"}} The page's content, View.Content Alone, for a request aimed at #<name>; on the search screen with the regions out of band

frontend.Templates reads both folders, and render decides what a request gets. A theme other than default/ finds the regions and fragments it lacks in default/, and replaces one with a file of the same name. The folders are read once and kept, or for every request with Config.ReloadTemplates. The demo uses everything in this guide; the starter's editorial theme uses its navigation, regions, fragments and forms.

A theme writes the hx-* attributes itself, or has go-partial write them, as the demo does: {{noBoost runtime}} for a link that loads a whole page, {{submitAttrs runtime …}} for a form that swaps in its answer, {{liveAttrs runtime …}} for a field that asks while the visitor types, and {{deferredSlot "<name>" "reveal"}} for a fragment that loads once it scrolls into view (see Template functions). Theme templates have go-partial's attribute functions: those whose names end in Attrs, noBoost and confirmAttr. Its functions that write an element of their own, such as poll and reveal, are not there.

For go-clue to know slot, requiredSlot, deferredSlot, hasSlot and the attribute functions such as noBoost, list github.com/donseba/go-partial/exp/slots and github.com/donseba/go-partial/exp/interactions in the providers of .go-clue/config.json, and github.com/donseba/go-partial/exp/slots.FuncMap and github.com/donseba/go-partial/exp/interactions.AttrsFuncMap in its functionMaps; github.com/donseba/go-importmap.FuncMap adds the importmap functions (see Templates).

Loading htmx

Any way of loading htmx 4 works, such as a copy in the theme's assets with {{assetScript "htmx.min.js" "defer" ""}}, which writes its <script> tag with the file's integrity (see Template functions).

The demo and the starter vendor it with go-importmap instead: its importmap command downloads front-end packages into the site's folder, with their licences and a lock file, and the site embeds them and serves them with an import map, so a module script can import "htmx" and the site needs no network at run time. go-webthings depends on go-importmap, so go mod tidy adds it to the site's go.mod. importmap.json lists the packages:

{
  "provider": "cdnjs",
  "packages": [
    {
      "name": "htmx",
      "version": "4.0.0",
      "require": [{"file": "htmx.esm.min.js", "as": "htmx"}],
      "license": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/htmx.org@4.0.0/LICENSE"
    }
  ]
}

importmap vendor downloads them into assets/vendor/: htmx/htmx.esm.min.js, htmx/LICENSE and importmap.lock.json, which lists each file with its source and SHA-384 integrity. The demo and the starter run it with go generate (their task vendor) and embed the folder:

//go:generate go run github.com/donseba/go-importmap/cmd/importmap vendor -config importmap.json -out assets/vendor

//go:embed assets
var assetFiles embed.FS

// importMap is the import map of the vendored packages.
func importMap() (*importmap.ImportMap, error) {
    files, err := fs.Sub(assetFiles, "assets")
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    return importmap.FromFS(files, "vendor/"+importmap.LockFile)
}

The site needs no copy of go-partial's browser clients. When the site starts, core adds them to its import map under the names scripts import them by, at /assets/ with a version: partial-interactions, which clientAttrs needs for "reloadOnError" and "submitConfirm", partial-flash and partial-sse. A name the site maps itself keeps the site's mapping. With Config.Assets the clients are among the site's files, and a file of the same name in that folder replaces core's. An import map of the site's own in Config.ImportMap, such as this one, gets core's copies, unless a client's file is among its own files, such as a partial-flash.js in the folder given to importmap.FromFS: that file is used instead. Either way the clients carry their integrity, like the site's other files. A site with neither has no import map.

Commit assets/vendor/, so building the site needs no network either. Run importmap vendor again after changing importmap.json. FromFS checks every vendored file against the lock and returns an error when one does not match, so the demo does not start with a changed file; go run github.com/donseba/go-importmap/cmd/importmap verify -out assets/vendor checks the same without starting the site, for CI.

Config.ImportMap takes the import map:

imports, err := importMap()
if err != nil {
    return err
}

app := webthings.New(webthings.Config{
    Templates: os.DirFS("templates"),
    ImportMap: imports,
})

The site serves the embedded files at /assets/, with a version from each file's content in its address and an ETag, like a theme's assets (see Themes), and templates get {{importmap}}, {{importmap_nonce}}, {{importmap_url}}, {{importmap_script}} and {{importmap_style}} (see Template functions). Config.Assets is served at /assets/ too: a site that sets both does not start. In the layout's <head> the import map comes before the theme's script, and site.js starts with import "htmx";:

{{importmap}}
{{assetScript "site.js" "type" "module"}}

{{importmap}} writes the import map with each file's versioned address and its integrity, the vendored files' and go-partial's clients', so the browser refuses a file whose content is not what the page expects:

<script type="importmap">
{
  "imports": {
    "htmx": "/assets/vendor/htmx/htmx.esm.min.js?v=9481657c08f4d363",
    "partial-flash": "/assets/partial-flash.js?v=60e5df53e40a18e9",
    "partial-interactions": "/assets/partial-interactions.js?v=d8a76b4a43a6496e",
    "partial-sse": "/assets/partial-sse.js?v=a0f0d65652166f47"
  },
  "integrity": {
    "/assets/partial-flash.js?v=60e5df53e40a18e9": "sha384-YOXfU+QKGOm1S7l6qDXMeljvUGkE517dLGoJyACRoi2wEyVWHbaw/qnZUZ2z4JUk",
    "/assets/partial-interactions.js?v=d8a76b4a43a6496e": "sha384-2KdrSkOmSW69IuWFe06CoM5FD1wB6V6JJbV/XyUCaRBGsQsGkCMQpKcrngHBXwYm",
    "/assets/partial-sse.js?v=a0f0d65652166f47": "sha384-oPDWVlIWb0djQk9kQhJlRDZoj/pHABnjUmz7vwjcGt5axvSWK8TUsJxfZ/pRAsTY",
    "/assets/vendor/htmx/htmx.esm.min.js?v=9481657c08f4d363": "sha384-lIFlfAj002Phzxvrea858KMM3/dXelBFF5rq+Oh5lChznUWuVI0mabAEUnsRa/2W"
  }
}
</script>

Navigation that swaps only the content

Every content template wraps its content in <main id="content">, as the starting points do. Boosting the body makes links and forms swap only that element; htmx 4 passes an attribute on to the elements inside only with :inherited:

<body hx-boost:inherited="target:#content swap:'outerHTML showTarget:body'">

go-partial's clientAttrs writes the same attribute, as the demo's layout does. It quotes the swap, so its scroll modifier stays part of it:

<body{{clientAttrs runtime "inherit" "true" "boost" "on" "target" "#content" "swap" "outerHTML showTarget:body"}}>

A request aimed at #content gets the content template without the layout, followed by every region out of band, in the order of their file names, such as editor, head, languages and then menu. The order is the same on every request, so the same page gives the same bytes and the same ETag. The render package sends the regions of a View's Regions first, in the order listed, and then those of its RegionFiles by file name; core's head region, for a theme without regions/head.gohtml, is in Regions, so it comes first. A request that needs the whole document, such as one with hx-select or htmx's history restore, gets the whole page. Give links that must load a whole page {{noBoost runtime}}, which writes hx-boost="false": the language links, since the layout's lang changes with them, and links to the admin:

{{with adminURL "admin.dashboard"}}<a href="{{.}}"{{noBoost runtime}}>Admin</a>{{end}}

Responses vary by HX-Request, HX-Boosted, HX-Target, HX-Request-Type and HX-History-Restore-Request, and by go-partial's own X-Select and X-Action, so a cache keeps whole pages and parts apart; a navigation that gets the menu region out of band also varies by HX-Current-URL (see The menu). While compression is on (Site settings › Performance, on by default), they also vary by Accept-Encoding, so a cache keeps the gzipped and the plain version apart. The site's own output cache does the same: it keeps the whole page and the HTMX navigation of one address side by side, and a navigation from another page, with another HX-Current-URL, as an answer of its own (see The output cache and The output cache for modules).

When a template fails, an HTMX request gets status 500, as a whole page does: the theme's 500.gohtml alone, or go-partial's plain error page without one, in the page's language, or with Config.Development the "Template render error" box alone; the page and the box are never cached and come without the layout or regions (see Templates). htmx 4 swaps it into the target, unless the theme stops swaps for server errors as the demo does (see Forms with HTMX).

Regions

A region is a part of the layout that changes from page to page, such as the menu with the current page marked. Its dot is the page, like the layout's, and its outer element carries the region's name as id and {{oobAttr}}:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
<nav class="menu" id="menu" {{oobAttr}}>
    {{range .Menu}}
        <a id="{{.ElementID}}" href="{{.URL}}" {{if .Active}}aria-current="page"{{end}}>{{.Title}}</a>
    {{end}}
</nav>

The layout places it with {{slot "menu"}}, and {{hasSlot "menu"}} reports whether the theme has it. On a whole page {{oobAttr}} writes nothing; along with the content of a navigation it writes hx-swap-oob="true", and HTMX swaps the element with the same ID.

Write the outer element on every page, empty when there is nothing to show: HTMX can only swap an element that is already on the page. The demo's regions/editor.gohtml is always a <div id="editor" {{oobAttr}}>, with the edit link inside only for editors.

The menu

Each item of .Menu has an ElementID, menu- and the page's ID. When the items of regions/menu.gohtml carry it as their id, as above, a navigation gets only the items whose Active changes, each with hx-swap-oob="true", instead of the whole menu. Going from /en/about/team to /en/work, with regions/title.gohtml, a region that holds only the <title> (see The head region), which comes after the menu by its file name:

<main id="content">…</main><a hx-swap-oob="true" id="menu-01a1…" href="/en/about" >About</a><a hx-swap-oob="true" id="menu-01a1…" href="/en/work" aria-current="page">Work</a><title>Work · My site</title>

The items of the pages below, .Children, change too, such as Team here; a region that shows them with their ElementID gets them along, and an item the region does not show is left out.

The items that change follow from the page the visitor comes from, which htmx sends as HX-Current-URL, so such a response varies by HX-Current-URL. That address counts as this site's also behind a trusted proxy that names the visitor's host in X-Forwarded-Host (Config.TrustedProxies, go-router's middleware.SameOrigin). The whole menu goes, as on any other request, when the items have no ElementID, when the request has no HX-Current-URL, and when that address is of another site, of another language or of no page, such as one the not-found page answered. Pages added, moved or renamed show in the menu with the next whole page, so a region with these IDs shows nothing else that changes from page to page.

The menu is chosen this way, and the response varies by HX-Current-URL, only when the menu region goes out of band: for a navigation, or a fragment of the search screen (see Fragments), to a theme with regions/menu.gohtml, not for a fragment alone or a request for the whole document (HX-Request-Type: full).

The head region

The tags of the page in <head> change from page to page too: the <title>, the description, the canonical and hreflang links, the feed links, the link to the content API, the structured data and the tags for sharing. A region named head holds them, and the layout places it in its <head> with {{slot "head"}}. A theme without regions/head.gohtml gets core's, with all of these tags (see The head region in Themes). A theme's own regions/head.gohtml adds to core's tags by calling them first:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
{{template "webthings/head-tags.gohtml" .}}
<meta name="theme-color" content="#336699">

This region needs no id and no {{oobAttr}}. <head> has no element that could wrap it, and the number of its tags changes from page to page, such as the feed links a news page has and a content page does not. On a whole page the region's tags sit between two empty <template> markers, with the <title> just before them:

<title>News · My site</title><template data-partial-head="head"></template>
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/en/news">
…
<template data-partial-head-end="head"></template>

Along with the content of a navigation, the region sends its <title> and two out-of-band swaps: one deletes the tags between the markers, the other adds the tags of the new page before the end marker. The tags of the page left, such as its feed links, alternates or description, are removed rather than kept, and none is doubled. So is its <script type="application/ld+json"> from {{structuredData}}: after a navigation from a post to the home page, <head> holds one such script, without the post's Article. htmx sets the document's title from the <title>. This works with htmx 4 without the head-support extension. Static tags, such as <meta charset>, stylesheets and scripts, stay in the layout outside the region and are never touched. The whole region goes with every navigation and adds nothing to the response's Vary header. go-partial's exp/head does the work (see Templates).

A Back or Forward in the browser is the exception. htmx 4, which the demo, the starter's editorial theme and the admin load, then asks for the page again, with the header HX-History-Restore-Request, and the site answers with the whole page, its head region included. htmx takes only the <title> from that answer and leaves the rest of <head> as it was, so the head keeps the region's tags of the page left, such as its canonical link and feed links, until the next navigation or a reload. The content and the title are those of the page returned to.

A layout without {{slot "head"}} gets no head region from core: it writes these tags itself, and a navigation leaves them as they are. A region with only the <title>, such as regions/title.gohtml placed with {{slot "title"}}, still works: htmx 4 sets the document's title from a <title> in a response and leaves the element out of the swap.

Fragments

A fragment is a part of a page that HTMX can ask for on its own, such as search results that follow the visitor's typing. The demo's fragments/results.gohtml is a <div id="results"> with the results of its frontend.SearchView; search.gohtml places it with {{requiredSlot "results"}}, below a search field that asks for it:

<input type="search" name="q" value="{{.Query}}" aria-label="Search"
    {{liveAttrs runtime .URL "target" "#results" "swap" "outerHTML" "replaceURL" "true"}}>

liveAttrs writes hx-get with the address, hx-target, hx-swap, hx-trigger="input changed delay:300ms, search" and, for "replaceURL" "true", hx-replace-url="true", so the address bar shows the query.

A request for a fragment of search.gohtml, such as the one aimed at #results, gets the fragment without the layout, followed by the regions out of band, as a navigation does. The search screen's title is the query and its language links keep it, so the tab's title, the head region's tags and the language links follow what the visitor types. A request for a fragment of any other page gets only the fragment, without the layout or the regions. Core sets render.View.FragmentRegions for the search screen only. On a whole page the fragment renders where it is placed. Its dot is the page's content, View.Content, also when the layout places it, so a fragment in the layout names the page with @model (see Templates). Its outer element carries the fragment's name as id. {{slot "results"}} places it as well. With a name the theme has no fragment for, {{requiredSlot}} fails the render with slot "results" is not set, and {{slot}} writes nothing.

Each request of the search field is a search, and a visitor may run 30 a minute. Beyond that the search does not run: the screen answers with status 429 and SearchView.Throttled set, without results, and htmx 4 swaps that answer in like any other, so a fragment that shows a message for .Throttled keeps the results box in place (see Templates and Search and SEO):

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.SearchView */}}
<div id="results">
    {{if .Throttled}}
        <p role="status">Too many searches in a short time. Wait a moment and try again.</p>
    {{else}}
        {{range .Results}}<a href="{{.URL}}">{{.Title}}</a>{{else}}<p>Nothing found.</p>{{end}}
    {{end}}
</div>

Alone or as a navigation

A fragment answers alone, or on the search screen with the regions, only on a page that has what it declares: data of its @dot type, and a value for every @model among the page and its content. A fragment that declares neither answers on every page. On any other page the request is a navigation: it gets the page's content with HX-Retarget: #content and HX-Reswap: outerHTML, and for a GET HX-Push-Url, so HTMX replaces the content and the address bar follows. A request aimed at an element that is neither the content, a region nor a fragment gets the same. Each answer has the page's status, such as 422 for a page that shows a form's errors, also a fragment or region alone.

The demo's sign-up box of a workshop, fragments/signup.gohtml, named after the registrations instance signup, declares the workshop and posts with hx-target="#signup"; form_open adds the attributes of submitAttrs to the form tag:

{{/* @model Event github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/events.Event */}}
{{with registration "signup" Event.ID}}
    <section class="booking" id="signup">
        {{form_open .Form (submitAttrs runtime .Action "target" "#signup" "swap" "outerHTML")}}
            …
        {{form_close}}
    </section>
{{end}}

When the workshop is full or a field is wrong, the registrations module returns to the workshop, which answers with the box alone and its message; for a wrong field, the form shows the visitor's values again with the messages at their fields (see A post with mistakes). A successful sign-up goes to the visitor's booking page instead. That page has no workshop, so it answers as a navigation: the visitor lands on the booking page and the address bar follows.

A fragment that loads later

A part that takes long to compute can follow the page. The demo's journal places its fragment fragments/popular.gohtml with deferredSlot, which writes an empty element that asks for the fragment once it scrolls into view:

<aside class="sidebar">
    {{deferredSlot "popular" "reveal"}}
</aside>

On a whole page this writes <div id="popular" hx-get="/en/journal" hx-swap="outerHTML" hx-target="this" hx-trigger="revealed" aria-busy="true"></div>, with the page's address. Without "reveal", {{deferredSlot "popular"}} asks with hx-trigger="load", as soon as the page has loaded. The fragment declares no @dot or @model, so every page answers the request with the fragment alone, and only that request counts the most read pages. A name the theme has no fragment for writes nothing. revealAttrs with "swap" "outerHTML" writes the same request attributes on an element of the template's own (see Template functions).

A visitor form in such a fragment does not show a post with mistakes again: the request for the page takes the kept post before the fragment's own request comes. Place a form with {{slot}} or {{requiredSlot}} instead (see A post with mistakes).

Forms with HTMX

Visitor forms post to the module's actions at /_/<key>/…, which answer with a 303 back to the page the form is on, the result in the query (see Visitor forms). A module's form returns the visitor to the element whose id is the instance key, such as #remarks, and its fields' ids start with that key, such as remarks-name. With HTMX, the browser follows the redirect with the same HX-Target, so a form aimed at its fragment gets the fragment back with the result. The comments under a post, in a fragment named after the instance key, fragments/remarks.gohtml:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing.Post */}}
<section id="remarks">
    {{range comments "remarks" .ID}}
        <p><strong>{{.Name}}</strong> {{.HTML}}</p>
    {{end}}

    {{if eq (commentResult "remarks") "sent"}}<p role="status">Thank you for your comment.</p>{{end}}

    {{with commentInput "remarks" .ID}}
        {{form_open . (submitAttrs runtime (commentURL "remarks") "target" "#remarks" "swap" "outerHTML")}}
            {{form_field . "subject" nil}}
            {{form_field . "name" nil}}
            {{form_field . "body" nil}}
            <button type="submit">Send</button>
        {{form_close}}
    {{end}}
</section>

commentInput is the form of the comments on the post. form_open writes the form tag with the spam trap and the page to return to, and adds what submitAttrs writes: hx-post with the address, hx-target and hx-swap. Posting replaces the comments, now with the new one and the message, and the address stays. Without JavaScript the form posts the usual way and returns to #remarks. Comments lists the fields and results.

A poll has no fixed ID, since a page can show several: its Anchor, <key>-<ID>, is the id of its element and the place its form returns to. The form picks its own poll out of the page with hx-select, which makes htmx ask for the whole page:

{{form_open .Form (submitAttrs runtime .Action "target" (printf "#%s" .Anchor) "select" (printf "#%s" .Anchor) "swap" "outerHTML")}}

A form in a boosted body without an hx-target of its own is a navigation: it swaps in the content of the page it returns to. The forms module's forms post to their own page and work this way, also when they show errors with status 422: htmx 4 swaps every response except 204 and 304. To keep a server error from replacing the page, the demo's layout sets hx-status:5xx:inherited="swap:none push:false" on its body, with "keepOnServerError" "true" among the clientAttrs above. With "reloadOnError" "true" as well, a link that gets a 5xx answer, or none, loads as a whole page, and so does a GET form; a POST is never sent twice: the server's error page replaces the page. A visitor action that fails, such as a comment that cannot be saved, answers an HTMX post as it answers a plain one, with status 500 and the whole error page: the theme's 500.gohtml, or go-partial's plain error page without one, in the language of the form's page (Frontend.Fail; see Templates). reloadOnError needs go-partial's browser client partial-interactions.js, which core adds to the site's import map (see Loading htmx); the demo loads it with import "partial-interactions"; in site.js. The starter's editorial theme sets keepOnServerError and reloadOnError on its body too, and loads the client the same way.

Under a Content-Security-Policy

htmx 4 works under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval', such as the one the site sends itself when an administrator turns it on under Site settings › Security (see A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own), as long as the theme leaves out what htmx runs as JavaScript, which only 'unsafe-eval' allows:

  • hx-on* attributes, such as hx-on:click;
  • trigger filters, such as hx-trigger="click[ctrlKey]";
  • js: and javascript: values, such as in hx-vals, hx-headers and hx-confirm. Plain JSON in hx-vals and hx-headers, and a plain question in hx-confirm, are fine.

The starting points, the demo and the starter use none of them, and go-partial writes none of them itself. htmx 4 adds the styles of its indicators as a constructable stylesheet rather than a <style> element, which such a policy does not block, and go-partial's browser clients are files the site serves at /assets/, which 'self' covers. Three things need care:

  • The import map is an inline script. The site's own policy allows it by its hash on every page; a policy sent from elsewhere, such as the proxy, needs that hash too (see importmap).
  • Content that htmx swaps into the page runs under the page's policy, not under that of the response. A style attribute in a fragment or region is blocked, and an inline <style> or <script> in it applies only when the page's policy has its hash. Style swapped content with classes, and keep inline scripts out of fragments. The box that answers an HTMX request whose template fails in development has go-partial's classes only, and partial-errors.css, which {{styles}} links first, styles them (see The error box).
