  • With reloadOnError, a failed POST writes the server's error page into the page, under the page's policy. A theme's 500.gohtml without inline style shows as it is. go-partial's plain error page, which a theme without one shows, styles itself with a <style> element. The site's own policy has the hash of that element, go-partial's errors.StyleHash() (ext/errors), on every page, so the error page is styled; under another policy it is styled only when the page's style-src has that hash.

go-partial's README covers its own output under such a policy in Content-Security-Policy; see also Under a Content-Security-Policy in Themes.

A complete example

A news site with the menu, the tags in <head> and comments under each post has regions/menu.gohtml from Regions, core's head region, fragments/remarks.gohtml from Forms with HTMX, import "htmx"; in assets/site.js, and this layout:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="{{.Locale}}">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    {{slot "head"}}
    {{styles "site.css"}}
    {{importmap}}
    {{assetScript "site.js" "type" "module"}}
</head>
<body hx-boost:inherited="target:#content swap:'outerHTML showTarget:body'">
    <header>
        <a href="{{.Site.HomeURL}}">{{.Site.Name}}</a>
        {{slot "menu"}}
    </header>

    {{content}}
</body>
</html>

news/post.gohtml places the comments; page.gohtml and the other content templates also wrap their content in <main id="content">:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing.Post */}}
<main id="content">
    <h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
    {{.Body}}

    {{requiredSlot "remarks"}}
</main>

What the browser asks and gets:

GET  /en/news/hello                 the whole page
GET  /en/news/hello                 HX-Target: main#content
                                    HX-Current-URL: https://example.com/en/
     → <main id="content">, then the <title>, the head region's two swaps and, with hx-swap-oob, the menu items that change
POST /_/remarks/post                HX-Target: section#remarks
     → 303 See Other to /en/news/hello?remarks=sent#remarks
GET  /en/news/hello?remarks=sent    HX-Target: section#remarks
     → <section id="remarks"> alone, with the new comment

Guides.Title: Media and images
Guides.Summary: Editors keep images and files in one media library, and pages and modules refer to them by ID. Templates show the images in the sizes the design needs, without editors uploading several copies.
Guides.Body:
The media library

Media in the admin (/admin/media) lists every uploaded file, newest first, with its type, size and, for images, its dimensions, 48 files per page with Previous and Next. Its search finds files by file name, title and alternative text in every language. Upload one file at a time; the upload opens the file's own page. Trash shows the deleted files. The admin is at /admin unless Config.AdminPath moves it; see Admin path.

A file's page shows:

  • a preview and an Open file link;
  • for images, the Focal point that crops keep in view, with crop previews (see The focal point);
  • Use in content: the Markdown that places the file in a text, for the editor's Markdown view (see Images and files in text);
  • a tab per site language with a Title and an Alternative text;
  • Move to trash, for editors with the delete right. It moves the file to the trash: it leaves the library and the website, and can be restored. See The trash.

Who may do what follows the Media row of the permission matrix: read opens the library and the text editor's image button, create uploads, edit changes titles, alternative texts and focal points, delete moves files to the trash and restores them or deletes them for good. Without create, the library has no upload form. Without edit, a file's page shows its texts read-only, with a note, and no focal point. See Accounts and permissions.

Choosing an existing file in a form, such as a post's Image, a person's Photo or the site's logo under Site settings, needs no Media rights: the dropdown lists the library's files by name.

Accepted files

The type is recognised from the file's content, not its name. A file is stored as <id>.<extension>, and its original name is kept for downloads.

Files Recognised by
JPEG, PNG and GIF images content
PDF and plain UTF-8 text content
ZIP, Word, Excel and PowerPoint (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx), OpenDocument (.odt, .ods, .odp) ZIP content and the extension
CSV text content and the .csv extension

Other files are refused, including WebP and video, and the upload form lists the accepted types. SVG files are always refused, also without an XML declaration and whatever their name. Every file may be up to 10 MB, images up to 40 megapixels, and names up to 255 characters.

In the admin, the upload form first checks the file's extension or the type the browser names, and its size: no file, a file of another type or one over 10 MB is refused at the field. The library then checks the content, and a file it refuses, such as an SVG named logo.txt, gets a message with the reason.

Titles and alternative text

Titles and alternative texts are written per language. The language tab is marked complete when an image has an alternative text, or another file a title.

The gallery module gives its templates both, in the page's language (.Title and .Alt of each image). Other modules give an image without its texts, such as a post's .ImageURL. {{alt .ImageURL}} gives the alternative text from the library in the page's language, or nothing when there is none:

{{with .ImageURL}}<img src="{{.}}" alt="{{alt .}}">{{end}}

Write alt="" for a decorative image.

A changed alternative text shows at once on the server that saved it. Other servers of the site show it within a minute, and in texts within two: each keeps the library's details and its rendered texts in memory for a minute.

The focal point

An image's focal point is the part that matters most, such as a face. Every crop keeps it as near its centre as the image allows, so a point near a corner stays near that corner. New images have it in the centre. Copies that are not cropped show the whole image and do not use it.

On the image's page, click or drag in the preview to place the marker, or select the marker and move it with the arrow keys, 1% at a time or 10% with Shift. Previews show the 1:1, 4:3, 16:9 and 3:4 crops while it moves. Save focal point stores it. Without JavaScript the marker does not show: type the point in From the left (%) and From the top (%); a value that is not a number from 0 to 100 is refused at its field, and the stored point stays. Saving needs the edit right.

The point is placed on the image as browsers show it: a photo the camera stored on its side is upright. Templates crop around it with {{image}}, {{focalClass}} and {{objectPosition}}; see Image sizes in templates.

Files in use

Content records which files it uses: files placed in texts, files chosen in fields such as a post's Image, and the logo, favicon and social image of the site settings. A file in use cannot be deleted; the library says "This file is used by content, perhaps in the trash, and cannot be deleted."

Pages, posts and events keep their history, and every revision counts. A file that an older revision used stays in use, so that revision can still be restored. Content in the trash keeps its files in use too, so it can be restored with them. A file is free only once the page, post or other item that used it is deleted for good from the trash. The library does not list where a file is used.

Images and files in text

Texts are stored as Markdown. In the text editor, the Image from the media library button lists the library's images, newest first and searchable by file name, title and alternative text in every language, ignoring case and accents (see Editing and publishing). It inserts the chosen image as ![alt](media:<id>), with the alternative text typed in its dialog or none. Other files are placed in the editor's Markdown view, written with media: and their ID, exactly as Use in content shows it:

![Our workshop in the old harbour](media:0199b1c2-7d4e-7a51-9c3f-2e8d4b6a1f07)

Read the [annual report](media:0199b1c2-8a10-7c22-8d5e-41f0c3b9e2a6).

The snippet for an image uses the alternative text of the language you are editing; the snippet for another file links its name. When the page is shown, media:<id> becomes the file's URL. Write the reference in this exact form, so the file is recorded as in use.

JPEG and PNG images in a text are shown as module views show them (see Image sizes in templates): as WebP copies at most 1600 pixels wide, with a srcset of copies 480, 800, 1200 and 1600 pixels wide and sizes="100vw". As in {{srcset}}, widths beyond the image's own are left out, and the image's own width is offered instead. GIFs are shown as uploaded, so an animation keeps moving. Every image gets width and height attributes with the size it is shown in, so the browser keeps its place before it loads. An image written without alternative text, such as ![](media:…), gets the library's alternative text in the page's language:

<img src="/media/v/<signature>/<id>_1600x0.webp" alt="Our workshop in the old harbour" srcset="… 480w, … 800w, … 1200w, … 1600w" sizes="100vw" width="1600" height="1067">

Newsletter mails show the images of their text as JPEG or PNG copies at most 1200 pixels wide instead, which every mail program shows (see What sends e-mail). So do the entries of the feeds of the publishing and events modules, with absolute addresses (see Search and SEO).

Image sizes in templates

Module views give each image as a copy made for pages, never as the uploaded file, which can be many megabytes. The fields are named after the image, such as a post's ImageURL or a person's PhotoURL:

Field What it holds
<X>URL A WebP copy at most 1600 pixels wide, never larger than the image
<X>Srcset <X>URL and the copies 480, 800 and 1200 pixels wide that are narrower, for a srcset attribute
<X>Width, <X>Height The size of <X>URL in pixels, for the width and height attributes
<X>OriginalURL The uploaded file, for a download link 
{{if .ImageURL}}
    <img src="{{.ImageURL}}"
         srcset="{{.ImageSrcset}}"
         sizes="(min-width: 60rem) 50vw, 100vw"
         width="{{.ImageWidth}}" height="{{.ImageHeight}}"
         alt="{{alt .ImageURL}}">
{{end}}

A GIF keeps its own URL, so an animation keeps moving, and its <X>Srcset is empty. The gallery's images have URL, Srcset, Width, Height and OriginalURL in the same way, and LargeURL, a copy at most 2400 pixels wide for the image on its own, such as in a lightbox (see Gallery).

{{image}} makes a copy in another size. It takes a URL a module view gives, the copy or the original, or an asset ID, and a size:

{{with .ImageURL}}<img src="{{image . "800x600"}}" alt="">{{end}}
Size Result
"800x600" fits inside 800 × 600 pixels
"800" 800 pixels wide
"x600" 600 pixels high
"800x600 crop" exactly 800 × 600, cut around the focal point
"800 jpg", "400x400 crop png" the same, as JPEG or PNG

The default format is WebP; jpg (or jpeg) and png can follow the size. An image is never made larger than it is: a size beyond the original gives the original's size, and a crop larger than the image cuts the largest part with the requested proportions. A side may be at most 4000 pixels.

For files that are not images, and for sizes it cannot read, which it also reports in the log, {{image}} returns the URL it was given, or the file's URL for an asset ID. A URL that does not come from the media library is returned as it is.

{{srcset}} lists WebP copies in widths of your own for a srcset attribute:

{{with .ImageURL}}
    <img src="{{image . "800"}}"
         srcset="{{srcset . 400 800 1600}}"
         sizes="(min-width: 60rem) 50vw, 100vw"
         alt="{{$.Title}}">
{{end}}

Widths beyond the image's own width are left out, and the image's own width is offered instead, so a small image is never offered as a large one. {{srcset}} is empty for files that are not images.

Crops in the browser

{{srcset}} copies are never cropped. To show them in a box with fixed proportions, the browser crops them with object-fit: cover. {{focalClass}} with the box's proportions, as "3:2" or "720x480", gives the image a class that places it so the browser shows about the same part as the crop copy:

{{with .ImageURL}}
    <img src="{{image . "720x480 crop"}}"
         srcset="{{srcset . 360 720 1080}}"
         sizes="(max-width: 700px) 100vw, 360px"
         class="photo {{focalClass . "720x480"}}"
         alt="">
{{end}}

.photo { aspect-ratio: 3 / 2; object-fit: cover; }

The classes are in focal-points.css, which core serves at /_/focal-points.css and the layout includes with {{styles "site.css" "focal-points.css"}}, or with {{assetStyle "focal-points.css"}} in a layout without styles, with a version and its integrity (see styles). It has one class for each position in steps of 5%, from .fp-0-0 to .fp-100-100, the horizontal position first, each setting object-position; {{focalClass}} rounds both positions to the nearest step, such as fp-35-60. A theme with its own assets/focal-points.css gets that file instead (see Focal points). A class needs no style attribute, so it works under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline', such as the site's own (see A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own).

{{objectPosition}} gives the same position unrounded, such as 35.2% 60%, for a style attribute: style="object-position: {{objectPosition . "720x480"}}". Such a policy blocks that attribute, so it is for sites without one.

Without proportions, both give the focal point itself, such as fp-25-75 or 25% 75%: it stays in view in a box of any shape, but not centred. Files that are not images in the library give fp-50-50 and 50% 50%.

The site's images

The logo, favicon and social image of the Site settings reach the layout as copies too (see The layout):

Field What it holds
.Site.LogoURL The logo at most 600 pixels wide, never enlarged, in the format it was uploaded in: a PNG stays a lossless PNG and a JPEG a JPEG, since WebP would blur its sharp edges. A PNG no wider than 600 pixels and a GIF keep their own address
.Site.FaviconURL The favicon as a 32 × 32 PNG, for <link rel="icon">
.Site.AppleTouchIconURL The favicon as a 180 × 180 PNG, for <link rel="apple-touch-icon">: the icon phones put on their home screen
.Site.SocialImageURL The social image as a 1200 × 630 JPEG, for og:image, or smaller with those proportions when the image is

The two icons and the social image are cut around the focal point. An image a module screen gives for sharing, the layout's .Image, such as a post's featured image, is made like the social image; an address outside the library stays as it is.

How the copies are made

Rendering a page only writes the URLs of copies. After an upload of a JPEG or PNG, the site makes the copies pages show by default in the background, one image at a time: the WebP copy at most 1600 pixels wide, then the narrower ones of its srcset. A 3000 pixels wide photo gets the copies 1600, 1200, 800 and 480 pixels wide, a 1000 pixels wide one 1000, 800 and 480, so the first visitor of a page with a new image does not wait for them. Every other copy, such as those of {{image}} and {{srcset}}, crops, the gallery's LargeURL, the site's images and the copies for e-mail, is made on its first request; so are the default copies of an upload while 1024 others still wait, as in a large import. A request for a copy that is being made waits for it rather than making it again. Each copy is kept in the media storage next to the original, so later requests only read it. Its URL names the image, size and format, and for a crop the focal point:

/media/v/<signature>/<id>_800x600.webp
/media/v/<signature>/<id>_400x400c.png
/media/v/<signature>/<id>_400x400c-250-750.png

A crop around the centre ends in c. Around another point, the point follows in thousandths of the width and height: here 25% from the left and 75% from the top.

The URLs are signed with a key from the site settings, so only sizes and focal points the templates ask for can be made, and every server of the site makes the same URLs. Because a URL never changes its content, copies are sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable. An image in the trash and its copies are not served; deleting it for good deletes its copies too.

Moving the focal point gives crops new URLs and deletes the crops made around other points. Copies that are not cropped keep their URLs. An old crop URL still gives the old crop, made again when asked for. Other servers of the site use a new point within a minute.

Resizing follows a JPEG's EXIF orientation and uses the Catmull-Rom filter. The width and height the library keeps are those of the upright image too, as browsers show it, and {{srcset}} uses that width. WebP copies have quality 80 and JPEG copies quality 85; JPEG has no transparency, so transparent parts become white. An animated GIF gives its first frame.

File URLs and downloads

Module views give other files, and the uploaded originals of images (<X>OriginalURL), as plain URLs, such as /media/0199b1c2-7d4e-7a51-9c3f-2e8d4b6a1f07.jpg, and core serves them below /media/. Images are shown in the browser. Other files, PDFs included, are sent as downloads with their original file name. Files are cached for an hour, with an ETag, and range requests work.

Files and copies are sent with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so a browser never takes a file for another type than it has, and Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, as the site's pages are. The site's framing setting does not apply to them: they have no X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors.

For a list of downloads with a counter, by category and year, use the documents module.

In Go, app.Media.URL(ctx, id) returns a file's URL, or "" for an unknown ID; module code uses env.Frontend.MediaURL(ctx, id). Images that pages show come from Image instead (see From Go).

Storage

Uploads and their resized copies are kept in StateDir/media (var/media in the starter). Back it up together with the database. Config.Storage names another place:

app := webthings.New(webthings.Config{
    Storage: store,
})

A storage implements media.Storage (media.go):

type Storage interface {
    Put(ctx context.Context, key string, reader io.Reader, size int64) error
    Open(ctx context.Context, key string) (io.ReadCloser, error)
    Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
    URL(key string) string
}
  • Keys are file names such as <id>.jpg and <id>_800x0.webp.
  • Open returns an error wrapping fs.ErrNotExist for a missing key; copies are made when it does. To serve originals at /media/, the reader must also be an io.Seeker.
  • Delete of a missing key should succeed, as it does for the built-in storage.
  • URL is the public address of a key, such as one on a CDN, or "" when the site serves the file itself at /media/. The built-in storage, media.NewFilesystem(dir, ""), returns "". Copies are always served at /media/v/ by the site itself, whatever the storage.
  • A storage with a Close() error method is closed when the app closes.

The s3 package of go-webthings-contrib (github.com/donseba/go-webthings-contrib/s3) keeps the files in an S3-compatible store, such as AWS S3, DigitalOcean Spaces or MinIO. With its public URL set, pages link to the store or its CDN directly; without it, the site serves the files at /media/ and the bucket can stay private.

When URL gives an absolute http or https address, such as the store's public URL, the site's Content-Security-Policy allows its origin, the scheme and host, in img-src and media-src, so pages show the files from there under the policy: img-src 'self' data: https://media.example.com. The origin is read once, at Start. A path on the site, such as that of media.NewFilesystem(dir, "/files"), needs nothing. See A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own.

From Go

Seed data and imports use the same service as the admin, once the app has started:

file, err := os.Open("seed/harbour.jpg")
if err != nil {
    return err
}

defer file.Close()

asset, err := app.Media.Upload(ctx, "harbour.jpg", file)
if err != nil {
    return err
}

err = app.Media.SaveTranslation(ctx, asset.ID, media.Translation{
    Locale:  "en",
    Title:   "The old harbour",
    AltText: "Fishing boats in the old harbour at sunset",
})

app.Media.Image(ctx, asset.ID, media.ImageWidth) gives an image as module views give it: a media.Image with URL, a WebP copy at most that many pixels wide and never larger than the image, Srcset, OriginalURL, and Width and Height, the size of URL. A GIF and an address outside the library, such as a theme's SVG, keep their own URL; an unknown asset gives an empty Image. It only builds URLs: the copies are made after the upload or on their first request (see How the copies are made), and app.Media.WaitPrepared(ctx) waits until those of the images uploaded so far are stored, for tests and tools. media.ImageWidth (1600) is the width of module views and texts, media.LargeImageWidth (2400) that of the gallery's LargeURL, and media.ImageWidths (480, 800, 1200 and 1600) are the widths Srcset offers below URL. Module code uses env.Frontend.Image(ctx, id), which is Image with media.ImageWidth; see The public handler.

For e-mail, env.Frontend.MailImage(ctx, id) gives a copy at most media.MailImageWidth (1200) pixels wide, never enlarged, as a JPEG, or as a PNG for a PNG with transparency, since not every mail program shows WebP; a GIF keeps its own address. Its URL is a path on the site, which mail needs absolute. env.Frontend.AbsoluteMarkdown(r, source) renders a text for a feed entry this way: its images as MailImage gives them, with their size, and every address of the site absolute, relative links leading from the address of r, such as the feed's, as a feed reader resolves them (see Feeds for modules). env.Frontend.MarkdownOptions(ctx, locale, base, true) gives the options to render a text of your own this way, such as a mailing, with base as the address its relative links lead from. env.Frontend.AltText(ctx, id, locale) gives the library's alternative text in a language the code chooses, such as a mailing's; app.Media.AltText does the same.

Texts are rendered with markdown.Render(source, markdown.Options{Media: …, Images: …}). Media gives the URL of a file, and Images a markdown.Image for an image of the library: its URL, Srcset with Sizes, Alt, used when the Markdown gives none, and Width and Height, which become the width and height attributes; a zero size leaves them out. Base makes the site's own addresses absolute, for readers away from the site, such as a feed or an e-mail. It is the absolute address the text's relative links lead from, such as https://example.com/en/: every link or image address without a scheme is resolved from it as a browser resolves it, also one that Media or Images gives. With that Base, /en/about and about both become https://example.com/en/about, ../x becomes https://example.com/x, ?page=2 becomes https://example.com/en/?page=2, and //cdn.example.com/… gets the scheme, https://cdn.example.com/…. Every address of an image's srcset is resolved the same way; its descriptors, such as 480w, stay as they are. Addresses with a scheme, such as https://… and mailto:…, and a fragment alone, such as #top, stay as they are. An empty Base, or one that is not an absolute address, such as /en/, changes nothing. markdown.AbsoluteSrcset(base, srcset) does the same for a srcset outside Markdown: with the Base above, /a.webp 480w, b.webp 800w becomes https://example.com/a.webp 480w, https://example.com/en/b.webp 800w. markdown.PlainMedia(source, options) resolves the references for readers of the Markdown itself, such as the text part of an e-mail: an image becomes a link, [alt](address), and a link to a file gets the file's address. With Base, it resolves the addresses of links, images and reference definitions the same way, except in code spans and code blocks.

app.Media.VariantURL(ctx, asset.ID, media.Variant{Width: 800, Height: 600, Crop: true}) gives the URL of a resized copy, as {{image}} does. A crop is cut around the image's focal point; Focus names another point and needs Crop.

Image, VariantURL, Srcset, AltText, Resizable, FocalPoint, ObjectPosition and PositionClass take an asset ID, the URL of a file or the URL of one of its copies, so the URLs a view gives work as well as the ID. app.Media.Resizable(ctx, ref) reports whether copies keep what the file shows: true for JPEG and PNG, false for a GIF, which may be animated, and for other files.

The addresses come from the library's two routes, which the app mounts at /media: media.asset serves the files and media.variant the resized copies. (*media.Service).RegisterRoutes(routes) registers them on a go-router; the app does so at start. A media.Service of your own, made with media.New, needs it too: before, VariantURL returns an error, and URL gives "" for files its storage leaves to the site.

app.Media.SetFocalPoint(ctx, asset.ID, media.FocalPoint{X: 0.3, Y: 0.4}) sets the focal point, in fractions of the upright width and height from the top left. It returns media.ErrInvalid for files that are not images and for points outside the image. app.Media.FocalPoint(ctx, asset.ID) reads it, app.Media.ObjectPosition(ctx, asset.ID, "4:3") gives what {{objectPosition}} gives, and app.Media.PositionClass(ctx, asset.ID, "4:3") what {{focalClass}} gives. For a point and an image size of your own, media.FocalPoint's ObjectPosition(width, height, box) and PositionClass(width, height, box) do the same, with the box's proportions as an image.Point, or a zero one for a box of any shape.

app.Media.Version() changes whenever a file changes in this process: its texts, its focal point, or whether it is in the library. A cache of what is made from files, such as rendered texts, compares it to know it is out of date. Changes on other servers do not change it.

Next steps

  • Templates shows which data each template gets.
  • Template functions lists image, srcset, focalClass, objectPosition, alt and the other functions.
  • Using modules covers the modules that show images, such as the gallery.

Guides.Title: Search and SEO
Guides.Summary: The site search finds published pages and module content in the visitor's language. WebThings also serves sitemap.xml and robots.txt, and writes the tags in <head> for titles, descriptions, links between languages, links to feeds and to the content API, sharing and structured data, or gives a theme's own head region what it needs for them.
Guides.Body:
The search screen

/<locale>/search?q=…, such as /en/search?q=glaze, searches the published content of that language and renders search.gohtml in the layout. Write a starting point with:

task templates -- site

The template gets a frontend.SearchView:

Field Meaning
Query The search as typed, trimmed to at most 200 characters.
Results At most 20 results, best first.
URL The search screen in this language, for the form's action.
Throttled Set when the visitor searched too often in a short time: the search did not run and Results is empty.

Each result is a frontend.SearchResult:

Field Meaning
Title The page's or item's title.
Summary About 200 characters of plain text around the first match.
URL The address of the page or item.
Module The module instance key, such as news; empty for pages.
Type The module type, such as publishing, or page.
Score How well it matches; results are sorted by it. 
{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.SearchView */}}
<main id="content">
    <form action="{{.URL}}" method="get" role="search">
        <input type="search" name="q" value="{{.Query}}" aria-label="{{tl localizer "Search"}}">
        <button>{{tl localizer "Search"}}</button>
    </form>

    {{if .Throttled}}
        <p>{{tl localizer "Too many searches in a short time. Wait a moment and try again."}}</p>
    {{else if .Query}}
        {{range .Results}}
            <article class="result-{{.Type}}">
                <h2><a href="{{.URL}}">{{.Title}}</a></h2>
                {{with .Summary}}<p>{{.}}</p>{{end}}
            </article>
        {{else}}
            <p>{{tl localizer "Nothing found for “%s”." .Query}}</p>
        {{end}}
    {{end}}
</main>

A search form in the layout points to {{searchURL}}, the search screen in the current language:

<form action="{{searchURL}}" method="get" role="search">
    <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="{{tl localizer "Search"}}">
</form>
  • The layout's .Title is the query, and the language switch leads to the same search in the other languages.
  • A site without search.gohtml answers "not found" at /search.
  • A published page with the slug search directly below the home page takes the address instead of the search screen.

Each visitor may run 30 searches a minute on the screen (frontend.DefaultSearchThrottle). A search beyond that does not run: the visitor gets the search screen with status 429, without results and with .Throttled set, so the template can say why, as above. htmx 4 swaps that answer into a live search like any other; see HTMX. The screen without a query and the search function do not count. Visitors are told apart by IP address, so list a reverse proxy in Config.TrustedProxies (see Visitor forms). The counts are kept in memory: a restart clears them, and each server counts its own. app.Frontend.SetSearchThrottle(limit, window) sets another limit; a limit of 0 turns it off.

How matching works

A result must contain every word of the query, in its title or its text. Case and accents are ignored in every script, so "ecole" finds "École". Words also match inside longer words: "pot" finds "pottery".

A word in the title counts 10 and a word in the text 1; a query of several words that appears whole in the title gets 5 more. Title matches therefore come first. Results with the same score are sorted by title.

There is no special syntax: quotes and operators are plain characters. Only the first 10 different words of a query count.

The search runs in Go over the published content, so it behaves the same on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. It reads all published content for every search, which suits sites up to a few thousand items. The plain text of each published page revision is kept in memory, so a page's Markdown is turned into searchable text once, not for every search.

What is searched

  • Pages: the title, description and content of every published page in the language, including the own text of pages that hold a module.
  • Modules: the publishing, events, gallery, lists, people, directory and documents modules add their published content. Their READMEs list the fields they search.

A module's content is only found while its instance is placed on a page, because a result needs an address. A module that fails is logged and left out, so it cannot break the search. Your own module joins with Parts.Search and frontend.ParseQuery; see Writing a module.

The same search works in any template, in the current language:

{{range search "workshop" 3}}
    <a href="{{.URL}}">{{.Title}}</a>
{{end}}

sitemap.xml

/sitemap.xml lists every published page in every enabled language, each with links to the same page in all the languages it has. A page in more than one language also links to its address in the default language as x-default, for visitors whose language the site does not have; a page without a translation in the default language has none. Below a module page it adds the module's own addresses, such as each post and category of a news instance. The publishing, events, gallery, people and directory modules add their items, and the documents module its category pages. Feeds, such as a news page's feed.atom and feed.rss, are not in it. On a site whose default language is Dutch:

<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/nl/over-ons</loc>
  <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="nl" href="https://example.com/nl/over-ons"></xhtml:link>
  <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/en/about"></xhtml:link>
  <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/nl/over-ons"></xhtml:link>
</url>
<url>
  <loc>https://example.com/nl/nieuws/open-atelier</loc>
</url>

The addresses start with Config.BaseURL. Without it, each request's own address is used: https when the request came over TLS, and its Host header. X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host, or else the proto= and host= of Forwarded, count only from proxies listed in Config.TrustedProxies. Set BaseURL in production; see Configuration.

The sitemap is built again as soon as what visitors see changes on the same server, so a page or item published there, in the admin or from Go, is in the next sitemap at once, also while the output cache keeps the sitemap like a page. Otherwise it is built at most once every 10 seconds. A change made by another server shows up once this server reads the published pages again (Config.CacheTTL, 30 seconds by default), in a sitemap at most 10 seconds later, plus the output cache's time, 1 minute by default. It lists at most 50,000 addresses, the most a sitemap file may hold; beyond that, the last ones are left out and a warning is logged. A module that fails is logged and left out, so it cannot break the sitemap.

robots.txt

/robots.txt allows everything and points to the sitemap:

User-agent: *
Allow: /
Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml

It does not name the admin, so an admin path of your own stays private (see Admin path). Admin pages are sent with X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow instead, which keeps them out of search results also when other sites link to them.

Both files are served by WebThings itself; a site cannot replace them with a page.

The head region

The tags of this guide, for the title, the description, robots, the canonical and hreflang links, the feeds, the content API, sharing and structured data, are the head region, which the layout places in its <head> with {{slot "head"}}. A theme without regions/head.gohtml gets core's. On /en/about, a page with a description, on a site in English and Dutch with Config.BaseURL set to https://example.com, core writes this, here without its empty lines and with the JSON-LD shortened:

<title>About · My site</title><template data-partial-head="head"></template>
<meta name="description" content="Who we are">
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/en/about">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/en/about">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="nl" href="https://example.com/nl/over-ons">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/en/about">
<meta property="og:title" content="About">
<meta property="og:description" content="Who we are">
<meta property="og:type" content="website">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://example.com/en/about">
<meta property="og:site_name" content="My site">
<meta property="og:locale" content="en">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary">
<script type="application/ld+json">…</script>
<template data-partial-head-end="head"></template>

A tag without a value is left out, such as the description of a page without one; the favicon, the apple-touch-icon, og:image, the feed links and the link to the content API follow when the site has them. og:type is article on a screen whose first structured data item is an Article, such as a post, and website elsewhere.

A theme adds tags of its own in regions/head.gohtml, after core's tags; a head region that does not call them replaces them, and gets the same View as the layout to write its own:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.View */}}
{{template "webthings/head-tags.gohtml" .}}
<meta name="theme-color" content="#336699">

A layout without {{slot "head"}} gets nothing from core. An HTMX navigation replaces the region's tags with those of the new page, so the description, alternates, feed links and structured data of the page left do not stay behind. A Back or Forward that htmx restores from its history is the exception (see HTMX). task templates -- site writes a head region that calls core's tags (see Themes).

Titles and descriptions

The layout and its regions get a title, a description and an image for the current screen:

Screen .Title .Description .Image
Page the page's title the page's Summary empty
Module list set by the module, usually the page's title set by the module set by the module
Module item, such as a post the item's title set by the module, such as a post's excerpt set by the module, such as a featured image
Search the query empty empty
Not found "Not found", translated with the site's tl empty empty

The site settings add texts per language: .Site.Name (Site title), .Site.Tagline (Tagline), .Site.SEOTitle (SEO title) and .Site.SEODescription (SEO description). Core's head tags use them:

  • The <title> is the screen's title and the site's name, such as About · My site, or the site's name alone on a screen without a title. On the home page the SEO title, when there is one, is the whole <title> and the og:title; no other page shows it.
  • og:title is the screen's title, or else the site's name.
  • The description, also as og:description, is the screen's own, or else the SEO description, or else the tagline. Without any of them the page has none.

A theme whose head region replaces core's tags decides itself. For example, the SEO title on the home page and the SEO description where a screen has no description of its own:

{{if and .Page .Page.IsHome .Site.SEOTitle}}
    <title>{{.Site.SEOTitle}}</title>
{{else}}
    <title>{{if .Title}}{{.Title}} · {{end}}{{.Site.Name}}</title>
{{end}}

{{with or .Description .Site.SEODescription}}<meta name="description" content="{{.}}">{{end}}

.Image is the image the module gives in frontend.Content.Image, such as a post's featured image, as a 1200 × 630 JPEG cut around the image's focal point: the size social networks and chat apps expect. An image too small for that gives a smaller copy with the same proportions. .Site.SocialImageURL is the Social image of the site settings, made the same way, for screens without an image of their own. Both are paths such as /media/v/…, whatever the storage; an address outside the media library is used as it is. Social networks need a full address. {{absURL}} makes one with Config.BaseURL, or with the request's address like sitemap.xml. An address with a scheme or a host, such as https://… or //cdn.example.com/…, stays as it is:

{{with or .Image .Site.SocialImageURL}}<meta property="og:image" content="{{absURL .}}">{{end}}

Core's head tags write this og:image, with <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">; a screen without either image gets summary.

The Favicon of the site settings gives two copies, both cut square around the focal point: .Site.FaviconURL, a 32 × 32 PNG for the browser's tab, and .Site.AppleTouchIconURL, a 180 × 180 PNG for the icon phones put on their home screen. Core's head tags link both:

{{with .Site.FaviconURL}}<link rel="icon" href="{{.}}" sizes="32x32">{{end}}
{{with .Site.AppleTouchIconURL}}<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="{{.}}">{{end}}

.Site.LogoURL is a copy of the Logo at most 600 pixels wide, never enlarged, in the format it was uploaded in, since WebP would blur its sharp edges: a JPEG gives a JPEG and a PNG a PNG. A PNG at most 600 pixels wide, and a GIF of any size, keep their own address. A theme's own logo, such as an SVG in its assets, is not a setting: link it with {{asset "logo.svg"}}. Each copy is made on its first request, not while the page renders; see The site's images and How the copies are made.

Canonical and alternate links

Every page has one address: other spellings, such as a trailing slash, redirect to it (see Pages). .Path in the layout and its regions is that address with its language prefix and without query string, so a canonical link is:

<link rel="canonical" href="{{absURL .Path}}">

.Languages gives the same content in each language where it is published, including the current one, for hreflang links. Their URL is a path; search engines want full addresses:

{{range .Languages}}<link rel="alternate" hreflang="{{.Locale}}" href="{{absURL .URL}}">{{end}}
{{if gt (len .Languages) 1}}{{range .Languages}}{{if .Default}}<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="{{absURL .URL}}">{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}

The second line names the address in the default language, the one with .Default set, as x-default, for visitors whose language the site does not have. It writes nothing when the content is in one language only, or not in the default language. Core's head tags have the canonical link and both lines. A page with status 400 or above, such as the not-found page or a module's 404, has none of them and no og:url: it has no address of its own to give.

On a module's screen below its page, such as a post, the links lead to the translations of the content shown when the module gives them in frontend.Content.Alternates, as the publishing, events, gallery, people and directory modules do for their items. A screen whose module gives none links to the module's page in the other languages, and to itself in its own language, so its hreflang link for the current language and its canonical link are the same address. On the screen /en/ticker/topic/harbour of a ticker module without alternates, on a site whose default language is English:

<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/en/ticker/topic/harbour">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/en/ticker/topic/harbour"><link rel="alternate" hreflang="nl" href="https://example.com/nl/tikker">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/en/ticker/topic/harbour">

sitemap.xml carries the alternates of every page with full addresses. Languages explains which languages are listed on which screen.

Feeds

Modules can offer Atom and RSS feeds, such as the posts of a news page at /en/news/feed.atom and /en/news/feed.rss. {{feedLinks}}, which core's head tags have, makes them discoverable: it writes a <link rel="alternate"> for each feed of the page shown, with absolute addresses, and nothing on pages without feeds or on error pages (see Template functions):

{{feedLinks}}

A link visitors see takes the feed's address from {{feedURL "atom"}} or {{feedURL "rss"}} (see Feeds in Themes). sitemap.xml never lists feeds. An entry of a feed has an ID that stays the same when its address changes: a tag: URI on the site's host, such as tag:example.com,2026-10-01:news/<post ID> for a post of the news instance created that day. The host is that of Config.BaseURL, or else of the request, so set BaseURL for IDs that do not change with the address a reader used. A module offers feeds with Parts.Feeds; see Feeds for modules.

A link to the content API

While the content API is on, {{apiLink}} in the head region links each page to its content as JSON, for apps: a <link rel="alternate" type="application/json"> to /api/v1/pages/<id>?locale=<locale> for a page, and to /api/v1/pages/resolve?path=<address> below a module's page, such as for a post, with an absolute address (see Template functions):

{{apiLink}}

It writes nothing while the API is off, on an error page, such as the not-found page or a module's 404 for a post that does not exist, and in a preview, which the API never shows. Core's head tags have it after {{feedLinks}}.

Structured data

{{structuredData}}, the last of core's head tags, tells search engines what a page is about, as schema.org items in JSON-LD. It writes one <script type="application/ld+json"> with @context and an @graph of the page's items (see Template functions):

{{structuredData}}
Item What it holds
WebSite The site in the page's language: the Site title as name, the SEO description, the home page as url, the language as inLanguage and the organisation as publisher. When the theme has search.gohtml, a SearchAction leads to the search screen, such as https://example.com/en/search?q={search_term_string}.
Organization The organisation behind the site, from the site settings: the Organisation as name, or the Site title when it is empty, the Logo at most 600 pixels wide (.Site.LogoURL), the Email, Phone and Address, and the social media profiles as sameAs.
BreadcrumbList The page's place in the page tree, from the home page down to the page, and to the module's screen below it, such as a post. The home page has none, and neither do screens outside the page tree, such as the search screen.
WebPage The page itself, at its canonical address: its title, description and image (.Title, .Description and .Image), its language, the site and the trail. The search screen is a SearchResultsPage.
The module's items What a module's screen shows, such as a post's Article; see below.

The items name each other by @id. The organisation's @id is the same on every page and in every language, such as https://example.com/#organization, so an article names it as its author and an event as its organiser. The site is always an Organization, never a LocalBusiness: the site settings hold the address as free text and no opening hours, and not every organisation with an address is a business that receives visitors. A directory entry with opening hours is a LocalBusiness.

The modules add an item for the content a screen shows:

Module Screen Item
Publishing a post Article: the title as headline, the excerpt as description, the featured image as a 1200 × 630 JPEG, the post's date as datePublished, when the revision shown was saved as dateModified, the language, the categories as articleSection, and the organisation as author and publisher
Events an event Event: the title, summary and image, startDate and endDate in the event's own timezone, such as 2026-11-07T14:00:00+01:00, or the day alone for an all-day event, eventStatus EventScheduled, the Location and Address as a Place, the language, and the organisation as organizer
Registrations with ForEvents an event of that agenda an Offer in the event's offers while visitors can register (InStock) or every place is taken (SoldOut): the adult price, the currency, the event's page as url and the time registration closes as validThrough
People a person Person: the name, the role as jobTitle, the photo, e-mail address and phone number, the website and LinkedIn address as sameAs, and the organisation as worksFor
Directory an entry LocalBusiness when the entry has opening hours, Place when it has a street, a city or a position, Organization otherwise, with its address, position and contact details
Publishing, Events, People, Directory and Gallery a list: the posts of a news page or a category, the upcoming or past events, the people, the entries of a directory, also when searched or filtered, or of a category's page, and the albums ItemList: the page's title as name, or the category's on a category's page, the number of items as numberOfItems, and a ListItem for each item, with its position and the address of its page as url, in the order the page shows them. A list without items has none

The module's first item is the page's main entity: its mainEntityOfPage is the page's address. The other modules add no item, also on their lists. A module of your own adds items with frontend.Content.StructuredData, and adds to the items of other modules, as registrations does, with Parts.StructuredData; see Structured data for modules.

Every address in it is absolute, with Config.BaseURL or the request's address, as {{absURL}} makes it. Empty values are left out, so a page without a description has no description and a site without a logo an Organization without logo. The not-found page, a module's screen with a status of 400 or more, and the theme's error page, 500.gohtml, have no structured data. That holds for every failing page: a page whose template fails, and a module's handler or a visitor action that fails (Frontend.Fail). html/template escapes <, > and & in the JSON, so text such as a title with </script> cannot end the script.

On the post /en/news/a-new-kiln, with Config.BaseURL set to https://example.com, it writes this on one line; here it is laid out, with the media paths shortened:

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@graph": [
    {
      "@id": "https://example.com/en/#website",
      "@type": "WebSite",
      "description": "Ceramics studio in Amsterdam Noord",
      "inLanguage": "en",
      "name": "Atelier Noord",
      "potentialAction": {
        "@type": "SearchAction",
        "query-input": "required name=search_term_string",
        "target": {"@type": "EntryPoint", "urlTemplate": "https://example.com/en/search?q={search_term_string}"}
      },
      "publisher": {"@id": "https://example.com/#organization"},
      "url": "https://example.com/en/"
    },
    {
      "@id": "https://example.com/#organization",
      "@type": "Organization",
      "address": "NDSM-Plein 28, Amsterdam",
      "email": "hello@example.com",
      "logo": "https://example.com/media/v/…_600x0.png",
      "name": "Atelier Noord",
      "sameAs": ["https://www.instagram.com/ateliernoord"],
      "telephone": "+31 20 123 4567",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/"
    },
    {
      "@id": "https://example.com/en/news/a-new-kiln#breadcrumb",
      "@type": "BreadcrumbList",
      "itemListElement": [
        {"@type": "ListItem", "item": "https://example.com/en/", "name": "Home", "position": 1},
        {"@type": "ListItem", "item": "https://example.com/en/news", "name": "News", "position": 2},
        {"@type": "ListItem", "item": "https://example.com/en/news/a-new-kiln", "name": "A new kiln", "position": 3}
      ]
    },
    {
      "@id": "https://example.com/en/news/a-new-kiln",
      "@type": "WebPage",
      "breadcrumb": {"@id": "https://example.com/en/news/a-new-kiln#breadcrumb"},
      "description": "The kiln arrived.",
      "image": "https://example.com/media/v/…_1200x630c.jpg",
      "inLanguage": "en",
      "isPartOf": {"@id": "https://example.com/en/#website"},
      "name": "A new kiln",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/news/a-new-kiln"
    },
    {
      "@type": "Article",
      "articleSection": ["Studio"],
      "author": {"@id": "https://example.com/#organization"},
      "dateModified": "2026-10-07T09:54:26Z",
      "datePublished": "2026-10-01",
      "description": "The kiln arrived.",
      "headline": "A new kiln",
      "image": "https://example.com/media/v/…_1200x630c.jpg",
      "inLanguage": "en",
      "mainEntityOfPage": {"@id": "https://example.com/en/news/a-new-kiln"},
      "publisher": {"@id": "https://example.com/#organization"},
      "url": "https://example.com/en/news/a-new-kiln"
    }
  ]
}

Keeping pages out of search engines

  • Previews of revisions, a page's address with ?revision=<id>, are never indexed or cached. Only signed-in editors see them, and they are sent with X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow and Cache-Control: private, no-store, without an ETag. The View's .Preview is set there too, and core's head tags then write <meta name="robots" content="noindex">; a head region that replaces core's tags writes it with {{if .Preview}}<meta name="robots" content="noindex">{{end}}. See Editing and publishing.
  • The search screen is sent with X-Robots-Tag: noindex: its results are endless variations of the site's content.
  • Admin pages are sent with X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow; robots.txt does not name the admin.

There is no per-page "noindex" setting. A head region can add the meta tag for chosen paths, such as {{if eq .Path "/en/thanks"}}<meta name="robots" content="noindex">{{end}}.

Guides.Title: Content API
Guides.Summary: The content API serves the site's published content as JSON at /api/v1/, for apps and other frontends that show it.
Guides.Body:
Turn it on

The API is off by default. Config.API, an api.Config of package api, turns it on:

// in the Config:
API: api.Config{Enabled: true},
Field Default What it does
Enabled false Serves the API at /api/v1/
AllowedOrigins none: no CORS headers The sites whose pages may read the API in the browser; see Browsers on other sites
RateLimit 300 How many requests one client may make per RateWindow; negative turns the limit off; see Rate limit
RateWindow a minute The time RateLimit counts in

While the API is off, /api/v1/ is an address of the site like any other, which has no page there: it gets the site's 404 page. While it is on, /api/v1 is one of the app's own addresses (App.CorePaths()), so no language can have the code api and no top-level page the slug api. Set Config.BaseURL, so the addresses in the answers do not depend on the address a client used.

Endpoints

Core serves the site, its search and its pages:

Endpoint Route name Answers with
GET /api/v1/site api.site The site in one language: its name, tagline and description, the languages, the menu and the module instances that have endpoints
GET /api/v1/site/search?q=harbour api.search The matches of the site search, best first, as a list; without q, none
GET /api/v1/pages api.pages The published page tree: the home page with the pages below it
GET /api/v1/pages/resolve?path=/en/about api.resolve The page at an address of the site, as the site finds it
GET /api/v1/pages/{id} api.page A page by its ID
GET /api/v1/<key>/… api.<key>.<name> The endpoints of a module instance

The route names build the addresses in Go: app.Frontend.Route("api.page", "id", id) is /api/v1/pages/<id>, and app.Frontend.Route("api.news.post", "id", id) is /api/v1/news/posts/<id>. The answers link to each other, so a client can also follow their api_url and api_base fields from /api/v1/site.

These bundled modules have endpoints below /api/v1/<key>/: their published items as a list, and each item by its ID:

Module Endpoints
Publishing /posts, newest first, also of one category with ?category=<slug>; /posts/{id}; /categories
Events /events, the upcoming and running events, soonest first, or the past ones with ?past=true; /events/{id}
Gallery /albums, in the editors' order; /albums/{id}, with its images
Lists /entries, in the editors' order; /entries/{id}
People /people, in the editors' order, also of one group with ?group=<name>; /people/{id}
Testimonials /testimonials, in the editors' order; /testimonials/{id}
Directory /entries, by name, also of one category with ?category=<slug>; /entries/{id}; /categories
Documents /documents, newest first, also of one category with ?category=<slug>; /documents/{id}; /categories

The lists of Publishing, Events, Gallery, People and Directory also take ?slug=<slug>, for the item at an address below the instance's page (see Pages and addresses). A ?category= that names no published category is answered with 404 not_found, as the site's page of such a category is. Lists, Testimonials and Documents, whose items have no page of their own, give each item whole in their lists; Publishing, Events, Gallery, People and Directory give an item's text only at /{id}. The modules' READMEs describe their fields. The other bundled modules have no endpoints. A module of your own adds endpoints with Parts.API; see The content API for modules.

Languages

Every endpoint answers in one language: that of its locale parameter, such as ?locale=nl, or the site's default language without it. /pages/resolve takes the language from the address instead. A locale the site does not offer is answered with 404 unknown_locale, and at /pages/resolve an address without one of the site's languages with 404 not_found. Content that is not published in the language asked for, such as a page without a Dutch translation, is answered with 404 not_found.

/site lists the languages with the site's address and api_url in each, and a page lists its alternates, the page in the other languages it is published in. GET /api/v1/site, abridged to two pages of the menu and two modules:

{
  "name": "Test site",
  "tagline": "",
  "description": "",
  "locale": "en",
  "default_locale": "en",
  "url": "https://example.com/en/",
  "logo": null,
  "languages": [
    {
      "locale": "en",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/",
      "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/site?locale=en",
      "default": true
    },
    {
      "locale": "nl",
      "url": "https://example.com/nl/",
      "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/site?locale=nl",
      "default": false
    }
  ],
  "menu": [
    {
      "id": "01a115cb-afc4-795c-95cc-9c19bc764806",
      "title": "About",
      "path": "/about",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/about",
      "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/pages/01a115cb-afc4-795c-95cc-9c19bc764806?locale=en",
      "module": null,
      "children": [
        {
          "id": "01a115cb-b00a-767a-9b00-358490a550c7",
          "title": "Team",
          "path": "/about/team",
          "url": "https://example.com/en/about/team",
          "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/pages/01a115cb-b00a-767a-9b00-358490a550c7?locale=en",
          "module": null,
          "children": []
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "01a115cb-b03c-77a9-b00f-912918ca4ebc",
      "title": "News",
      "path": "/news",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/news",
      "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/pages/01a115cb-b03c-77a9-b00f-912918ca4ebc?locale=en",
      "module": {
        "key": "news",
        "title": "News",
        "type": "publishing",
        "url": "https://example.com/en/news",
        "api_base": "https://example.com/api/v1/news"
      },
      "children": []
    }
  ],
  "modules": [
    {
      "key": "news",
      "title": "News",
      "type": "publishing",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/news",
      "api_base": "https://example.com/api/v1/news"
    },
    {
      "key": "agenda",
      "title": "Agenda",
      "type": "events",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/agenda",
      "api_base": "https://example.com/api/v1/agenda"
    }
  ]
}

menu holds the pages below the home page, as the site's menu shows them; /pages gives the same tree with the home page at the top. A page with a module instance names it in module. modules lists the instances with endpoints; url is the page an instance is on, null while it is on none.

Pages and addresses

/pages/resolve finds the published page at an address of the site, as the site does. GET /api/v1/pages/resolve?path=/en/about, with the long srcset shortened:

{
  "id": "01a115cb-afc4-795c-95cc-9c19bc764806",
  "locale": "en",
  "title": "About",
  "description": "Who we are",
  "slug": "about",
  "path": "/about",
  "url": "https://example.com/en/about",
  "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/pages/01a115cb-afc4-795c-95cc-9c19bc764806?locale=en",
  "parent_id": "01a115cb-af90-727a-acc1-8df00267c0cc",
  "is_home": false,
  "body_html": "\u003cp\u003eRead the \u003ca href=\"https://example.com/en/news\"\u003enews\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp\u003e\u003cimg src=\"https://example.com/media/v/wlN_-0Ps0_NzcXkN/01a115cb-afb9-7d37-a62d-7512dda0e551_1600x0.webp\" alt=\"The harbour\" srcset=\"https://example.com/media/v/hJrpW0UZS6JpKfmT/01a115cb-afb9-7d37-a62d-7512dda0e551_480x0.webp 480w, …\" sizes=\"100vw\" width=\"1600\" height=\"900\"\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-07T09:57:12.791656Z",
  "alternates": [
    {
      "locale": "nl",
      "url": "https://example.com/nl/over-ons",
      "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/pages/01a115cb-afc4-795c-95cc-9c19bc764806?locale=nl"
    }
  ],
  "breadcrumbs": [
    {
      "id": "01a115cb-af90-727a-acc1-8df00267c0cc",
      "title": "Home",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/",
      "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/pages/01a115cb-af90-727a-acc1-8df00267c0cc?locale=en"
    },
    {
      "id": "01a115cb-afc4-795c-95cc-9c19bc764806",
      "title": "About",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/about",
      "api_url": "https://example.com/api/v1/pages/01a115cb-afc4-795c-95cc-9c19bc764806?locale=en"
    }
  ],
  "module": null
}

path is the page's address without the language, / for the home page, whose slug is empty and is_home true. parent_id is null for the home page. updated_at is when the published revision was saved. breadcrumbs lead from the home page to the page, both included. /pages/{id} answers with the same page by its ID, in the language of ?locale=.

An address below a page with a module instance, such as a post at /en/news/hello-harbour, resolves to that page, with the rest of the address in module.path:

  "module": {
    "key": "news",
    "title": "News",
    "type": "publishing",
    "url": "https://example.com/en/news",
    "api_base": "https://example.com/api/v1/news",
    "path": "/hello-harbour"
  }

module.path is / for the page itself and is left out of every other answer. The instance's endpoints, below api_base, give its content: GET /api/v1/news/posts?slug=hello-harbour lists the post with that slug. An address without a published page is answered with 404 not_found.

Core's head tags point each page of the site to its answer here with {{apiLink}}: a <link rel="alternate" type="application/json"> to /pages/{id} for a page, and to /pages/resolve for an address below a module's page, such as a post's. Frontend.APILink(r) gives the same address in Go.

Responses

The answers follow the same rules everywhere:

  • Names are in snake_case, such as api_url and body_html.
  • Times are in RFC 3339, such as "2026-10-07T09:57:12.791656Z". Times the site records, such as updated_at, are in UTC; an event's start and end carry the offset of its timezone, such as "2027-06-12T14:30:00+02:00".
  • Addresses are absolute, on Config.BaseURL or else the address of the request: url is the content on the site, api_url the same content in the API.
  • A field without a value is null, such as the image of content without one or the url of content whose instance is on no page. Text without a value is "" and an empty list []. Two fields are left out instead: module.path outside /pages/resolve, and the text of a module's item with a page of its own, such as a post's body_html or an album's description_html, which only the item's own endpoint gives, when the item has text.
  • Editors write text in Markdown. The API gives it as HTML in body_html, or in a field named after the text, such as description_html and bio_html, as the site shows it: in the language of the answer, with every address of the site absolute and images with their srcset, sizes, width, height and alt text. Relative links lead from the home page of that language, such as https://example.com/en/.
  • Images of the media library are objects, as the site shows them:
Field
url A WebP copy at most 1600 pixels wide, never wider than the upload
srcset The smaller copies, for an img tag's srcset
width, height The size of url
alt The alt text in the language of the answer, as editors wrote it in the media library
original_url The uploaded file

JSON writes <, > and & in text as \u003c, \u003e and \u0026, as the examples show; a JSON parser reads them as the characters. Answers of 1 KiB or more are compressed for clients that accept gzip, as pages are (Site settings › Performance).

Lists

A list is one page of the items, newest or best first as the endpoint says:

Field
items The items of this page
total How many items there are in all
limit How many items a page holds: the limit parameter, 20 by default, at most 100
offset Where the page starts: the offset parameter, 0 by default
next The absolute address of the next page, with the same parameters; null on the last page

A limit or offset that is not a whole number, or is out of range, is the default or the nearest value allowed, so paging never fails. GET /api/v1/site/search?q=harbour&limit=1:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "title": "Harbour fair",
      "summary": "Games and food",
      "url": "https://example.com/en/agenda/harbour-fair",
      "type": "events",
      "module": "agenda"
    }
  ],
  "total": 4,
  "limit": 1,
  "offset": 0,
  "next": "https://example.com/api/v1/site/search?limit=1\u0026offset=1\u0026q=harbour"
}

A search result's type is page or the module type, such as publishing, and module the instance key, null for a page. The search finds at most 100 matches, as the site search does in the visitor's language, but without its limit of 30 searches a minute: the API's rate limit applies instead.

Errors

An error is an object with the HTTP status, a code that stays the same and a message for people:

{
  "error": {
    "status": 404,
    "code": "unknown_locale",
    "message": "Not Found"
  }
}
Code Status When
not_found 404 No published content at the address or in the language asked for, an address without an endpoint, or another method than GET or HEAD
unknown_locale 404 The site does not offer the language of ?locale=
rate_limited 429 The client made more requests than the rate limit allows
internal_error 500 The server failed; the log has the details

The message is the status text, translated with the site's translations (Config.Translations) into the language of the answer. Errors are sent with Cache-Control: no-cache and without an ETag. The API answers no 400 or 405: a wrong method is not found, and paging parameters are corrected (see Lists).

What the API shows

The API shows what visitors see on the site, nothing else: only published content, never a draft, a scheduled revision or a preview, also not to signed-in editors. Every answer is the same for everyone, so the API needs no session and the output cache can keep its answers. The modules show what their pages show, and no data of visitors: Registrations, Submissions, Forms, Comments, Polls and Newsletter have no endpoints, so sign-ups, proposals, form entries, comments, votes and subscribers never appear.

Caching

The API's answers go through the output cache as pages do: they are kept per address and query, and every change visitors see, such as a post that is published, has them made again. Searches with a query are not kept. Unlike pages, answers to signed-in editors are kept and served from the cache too, since they are the same.

Answers with status 200 have a weak ETag. A client that sends it again in If-None-Match gets 304 Not Modified without a body while the answer has not changed. Their Cache-Control is that of pages, Browsers and caches keep pages for in Site settings › Performance: no-cache by default, so clients ask every time, or public, max-age=… with a time, with stale-while-revalidate=… when that is set too. Searches with a query and errors are always no-cache. See Deployment.

A single page, post, event, album, list entry, person or testimonial also has a Last-Modified: /pages/{id}, /pages/resolve, /<publishing>/posts/{id}, /<events>/events/{id}, /<gallery>/albums/{id}, /<lists>/entries/{id}, /<people>/people/{id} and /<testimonials>/testimonials/{id}. It is the latest change of the item and of what the answer shows of other content: the pages above a page, the page a module instance is on, a post's categories, the media files in the text and the item's images, such as a featured image, a photo or an album's images, with their alt texts and focal points, and when an event ended, once it is past. A client that sends it in If-Modified-Since gets 304 Not Modified while none of them changed, also from the output cache. An answer that shows something without a date gets none, such as a post in a category that was deleted, an item whose image was deleted, an instance on no page or a page below one that is not published, and so does a date ahead of the server's clock. Lists, the page tree, /site and the categories have none either, since an item that leaves a list leaves no newer date behind, and neither does a single directory entry or document: its category counts the published items in it, which another item changes. Their ETag answers If-None-Match. Changes to the site settings, such as the languages offered, do not move the date; the ETag covers them.

Rate limit

Each client, known by its address, may make RateLimit requests per RateWindow: 300 a minute unless the configuration says otherwise. Answers from the output cache count too. More requests in the window are answered with 429 rate_limited and Retry-After, the length of the window in seconds, until earlier requests leave the window:

API: api.Config{
    Enabled:    true,
    RateLimit:  60,
    RateWindow: 10 * time.Second,
},

A negative RateLimit turns the limit off. Each process counts in its own memory, so with several servers a client may make RateLimit requests on each. Behind a reverse proxy, list it in Config.TrustedProxies: otherwise every client has the proxy's address and they share one limit.

Browsers on other sites

Without AllowedOrigins, the API sends no CORS headers: the site's own pages, apps and servers read it, the pages of other sites in a browser cannot. AllowedOrigins names the sites whose pages may:

API: api.Config{
    Enabled:        true,
    AllowedOrigins: []string{"https://app.example.com", "*.example.org"},
},

An entry is an origin, such as https://app.example.com; * allows every site, and *.example.org the subdomains of example.org, over HTTP and HTTPS, but not example.org itself. Then:

  • A request from an allowed origin gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin, with that origin or *, and Access-Control-Expose-Headers: ETag, Last-Modified, Retry-After, so scripts can read those headers.
  • A request from another origin is answered with 403 without a body.
  • A preflight request (OPTIONS) from an allowed origin is answered with 204, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, HEAD and Access-Control-Max-Age: 600, so browsers keep it for ten minutes. Preflight requests do not count for the rate limit.
  • Requests without an Origin, such as an app's or a server's, are answered as without AllowedOrigins.
  • Every answer says Vary: Origin, also one to a request without an Origin, so caches between the site and its clients keep the answers for each origin apart and never give an answer without CORS headers to an allowed site. The output cache keeps one answer for all origins and adds the CORS headers to each request.

The API reads no cookies and needs no credentials, so Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is never sent.

Endpoints of a module

A module serves its own content below /api/v1/<key>/ with Parts.API, a router of api.NewRouter(), and answers with the helpers of package api, such as api.Paginate for lists, api.ImageOf for images and api.Modified with api.ItemDates for the Last-Modified of an item, so its answers follow the rules above. See The content API for modules.

Guides.Title: Visitor forms
Guides.Summary: Visitors post comments, votes, sign-ups and messages through forms in the site's templates. This guide explains how those forms reach modules, how they are protected, and how a site adds a form of its own.
Guides.Body:
How a visitor form works

A module that takes posts from visitors receives them below /_/<key>/, its visitor actions. The address does not depend on the page, so any template can show a module's form: a comment form below a post, a newsletter signup in the footer, a poll on the home page.

A post goes through the same steps everywhere:

  1. The visitor sends the form to the module, for example /_/newsletter/subscribe.
  2. The module checks the spam trap and the input, and stores what it should.
  3. It redirects (303 See Other) to the page the form was on, with the result in the query: /en/news/hello?newsletter=check-mail#newsletter.
  4. The page shows the result. Reloading it does not send the form again.

The modules' components render complete forms, such as {{commentThread "comments" .ID}} or {{newsletterForm "newsletter"}} (see Templates). With your own markup, the module's data gives the form as .Form: {{form_open .Form}} … {{form_close}} writes the form with the address it posts to, and {{form_field}} renders a field as the module checks it (see The fields). The module's README lists the fields it reads and the results it returns. A signup form for the newsletter module:

{{with newsletter "newsletter"}}
    <div id="{{.Key}}">
        {{if eq .Result "check-mail"}}<p>{{tl localizer "Please check your inbox and confirm."}}</p>{{end}}
        {{if eq .Result "invalid"}}<p>{{tl localizer "Please enter a valid e-mail address."}}</p>{{end}}

        {{form_open .Form}}
            {{form_field .Form "locale" nil}}
            {{form_field .Form "email" nil}}
            <button type="submit">{{tl localizer "Subscribe"}}</button>
        {{form_close}}
    </div>
{{end}}

The form posts to /_/newsletter/subscribe. The locale field is hidden: it sends the page's language, the language of the confirmation mail.

The hidden fields

{{form_open .Form}} writes two hidden fields after the form tag:

  • a spam trap: go-form's honeypot, a text input named website (frontend.Honeypot), hidden from screen readers and skipped by the keyboard. Its class, form-honeypot, moves it off screen. People leave it empty; many bots fill it in.
  • back: the path of the page the form is on, with the key of the module instance as anchor, such as /en/news/hello#newsletter, so the module knows where to return.

The anchor returns the visitor to the element whose id is the key, so a form further down the page stays in view, also without JavaScript. Give the form, or the element around it, that id, as <div id="{{.Key}}"> above. The key also goes before the ids of the form's fields: the e-mail field of the instance newsletter has the id newsletter-email, so the forms of two instances on one page keep ids of their own.

A template that writes the form tag itself puts {{form_hidden .Form}} inside it, which writes the same two fields and nothing else:

{{with newsletter "newsletter"}}
    <form method="post" action="{{.Action}}" class="signup">
        {{form_hidden .Form}}
        <input type="email" name="email" required>
        <button type="submit">{{tl localizer "Subscribe"}}</button>
    </form>
{{end}}

On the home page, form_hidden writes:

<input type="text" name="website" value="" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" aria-hidden="true" class="form-honeypot">
<input type="hidden" name="back" value="/en/#newsletter">

The trap has no style attribute: webthings.css hides the class form-honeypot, so the trap stays hidden under a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' (see A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own). A theme without webthings.css hides that class in its own stylesheet. A site with a go-form theme of its own (Config.FormTheme) sets the theme's Honeypot to a class its stylesheet hides, such as go-form's templates.HoneypotClass, form-honeypot; without it, the trap gets form-honeypot and an inline style that hides it. go-form's Bootstrap theme gives the trap visually-hidden, its Tailwind themes sr-only. See Configuration.

A module checks the trap with frontend.IsSpam(r), which is go-form's form.IsSpam for that field: a value in the post or in the address counts. The bundled modules answer bots that fill it in as they would answer a person, but store nothing, so the bots learn nothing. When IsSpam reports true, it also tells the site's output cache that the post changed nothing.

frontend.BackPath(r) is the page's path from back, or from the Referer header as with frontend.Back below, without query or fragment, or "" when it is not a path on the site. env.Frontend.BackLocale(r) is that page's language: its first path segment when that is an enabled language, and the site's default language otherwise. The comments module stores a message with both. The bundled modules write their confirmations to visitors in that language.

The fields

A module reads a post into a Go struct whose go-form tags say what each field takes. The bundled modules' structs are comments.PostInput, submissions.ProposalInput, registrations.SignupInput and CancelInput, newsletter.SubscribeInput and polls.VoteInput. Where a theme writes the form itself, the module's data offers it as .Form: the newsletter signup ({{newsletter}}), a registration's sign-up ({{registration}}) and the cancel form on the registration's page, the submissions form, a poll, and the comments module's list and form. {{commentInput "remarks" .ID}} gives the comment form of any post, and {{submitInput "tips"}} the submissions form of the instance tips. A poll's form returns to its .Anchor, <key>-<ID>, rather than to the key, since a page can show several polls. The registrations module's lookup page offers its form as .Form too, of registrations.LookupInput: it is sent with GET to the page itself, with the code as ?code=, so it has no hidden fields, and its field's id is registration-code.

{{form_field .Form "email" nil}} renders one field: its label, its help text and the input with the limits the module checks, such as required and maxlength, and hints such as autocomplete. The browser then checks what the module checks, and a limit changes in one place. form_field takes the field's name in the post, such as email, not the name of the Go field: "Email" fails the template with an error that lists the names the form has, form: no field "Email" (fields: email, name, locale). Its last argument holds errors to show at the field. A visitor form passes nil: after a post with mistakes the form brings the visitor's values and the messages itself (see A post with mistakes). A field written by hand with the same name works as well, for example when its limits depend on the data.

The fields render with go-form's markup and the classes of webthings.css, such as wt-form__field, wt-form__label and wt-form__input. Radio and checkbox groups, such as a poll's options or go-form's multicheckbox, render as a fieldset with their label as the legend: the fieldset has the field's classes and wt-form__fieldset, which removes the browser's border and padding, and the legend has the label's. A site with CSS of its own registers a go-form theme with its classes and names it in Config.FormTheme; see Themes. Such a theme adds classes of its own to the fieldset and the legend with go-form's ThemeClasses.Fieldset and Legend, or its CSS resets fieldset and styles legend like label. Labels and help texts are translated with the site's .po files, and go-form's own texts, such as the "(required)" that screen readers announce, with go-form's catalogue; see Languages. Template functions lists form_field and go-form's other functions: form_open, form_hidden, form_errors, form_buttons, form_close and form_render. form_render writes the whole form, with the same hidden fields as form_open.

Results on the page

frontend.Back(w, r, key, result) sends the visitor back to the back path with ?<key>=<result> added. A #fragment is kept. Only paths on the site itself are followed. Without such a back field, as when a post over the body limit could not be read, the visitor returns to the address in the Referer header when that is on the site, and to / otherwise.

frontend.BackWith adds more query values, for example a code the page shows:

frontend.BackWith(w, r, "signup", "registered", url.Values{"code": {code}})

Modules give the result to their templates, usually as .Result, or through a function such as {{newsletterResult "newsletter"}}. They only pass on results they know, so a made-up value in the address shows nothing. frontend.Result(r, key, allowed...) reads a result that way: it returns "" for anything not in allowed.

A post with mistakes

A post that fails its checks returns to its page with a result such as invalid.
