Hidden fields, such as the newsletter's locale, are rendered with form_field too. Forms renders its whole form with {{form_render .Form .Errors}}. Template functions covers the form_* functions.

After a post with mistakes, the visitor returns to the form with ?<key>=invalid, and the form of Comments, Newsletter, Registrations or Submissions shows their values again, with the messages at their fields; a poll shows the vote form again with the message at its options. form_field and form_render do this with nil as errors, so the templates need no change; inputs written by hand do not show them. See A post with mistakes. A post that fails for another reason, such as an unreachable database, gets the theme's 500.gohtml.

The e-mail fields of the bundled modules that store an address, in visitors' forms and in the admin, are checked with validate:"mail" (mail.Rule): one address mail can be sent to, with a dot in it, so anna@localhost gets the message of an invalid address. The email fields editors build in Forms are checked with mail.Rule too, since a reply to the notification goes to that address.

Reach an instance from Go

Every bundled module has Of(app, key), which returns the instance's typed service once the app has started, and nil before or for an unknown key. app.Service(key) returns the same value untyped. To use it before serving, start the app first; ListenAndServe does not start it again:

if err := app.Start(ctx); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

latest, err := publishing.Of(app, "news").Latest(ctx, "en", 5)

While an instance is on no page, its service still returns its items, with empty URLs: Publishing's Latest, Gallery's Albums and Album, Directory's Entries and ListCategories, People's List and BySlug, Documents' Latest and InCategory (an empty CategoryURL; the download links work) and Events' Upcoming, Event and Events.

The visitors' forms post to routes named with the instance key in front, so app.Frontend.Route("remarks.post") is /_/remarks/post, the address of the remarks comment form.

Modules whose content editors write offer Store() for imports and seed data, with the same rules as the admin. Comments are imported with comments.Service.Add and newsletter subscribers with newsletter.Service.Import.

Modules and the output cache

The site keeps the pages visitors get in memory for a while, a minute by default (see Caching), so a page with module content, or a module's feed, is not rendered again for every visitor. What editors change in a module's admin section, visitors' posts to its actions and scheduled publication show at once. A visitor's post that stores nothing, such as spam, a post with mistakes or one over the throttle, keeps the pages in the cache; the bundled modules also say so for a closed comment instance or sign-up, every vote that did not count, a proposal whose body cannot be read and a newsletter signup or unsubscribe (frontend.NothingChanged). Changes made from Go show at once too. The bundled modules' stores tell the cache after every committed write visitors see, such as an import or seed through Store(): publishing and unpublishing an item, moving it to the trash and back and, for a collection, saving an item and moving it in the order. Saving a draft of revisioned content changes nothing visitors see. The services of Comments, Polls and Registrations do the same, such as comments.Service.Add and registrations.Service.SaveSettings. Newsletter subscribers and Submissions' proposals do not, as no page shows them, and Redirects works before the cache. The site's own code calls app.Changed() for other changes, such as data its pages show from elsewhere.

  • Polls marks the polls a visitor voted on through the wt_poll cookie, which it registers with Env.PersonalCookie: the cache keeps a page apart for each value of it, so voters see their own choice and other visitors the vote form.
  • Stats and Redirects wrap the site before the cache: Stats also counts the pages the cache answers, and a new redirect works at once, also for an address whose page is in the cache.
  • Pages that are a visitor's own, such as a registration looked up by its code, are sent with Cache-Control: private, no-store, which the cache never keeps.

A module of your own whose content is a content.Revisions or content.Collection sets Changed in its content.Spec to env.Changed in Setup; the store then tells the cache after every committed write visitors see. For its other writes it calls env.Changed() after the commit, such as with db.AfterWrite(ctx, err, env.Changed), and db.AfterCommit(ctx, fn) waits for the end of a transaction; see The output cache in Caching and testing a module.

Links in module content

The admin knows which published content links to which page, so a page's editor can list that content before the page goes offline or changes its address, and Pages › Broken links can list the links that lead nowhere; see Links to a page. Next to the text of the pages, these bundled modules report the links in their published content, and the editors of the items with an address of their own list the content that links to them:

Module Links in Editor lists the links to
Publishing a post's text a post, a category
Events an event's text an event
Gallery an album's description an album
People a person's biography and website a person
Directory an entry's description and website an entry; a category, with the links to its entries apart
Documents a document's description and link
Lists an entry's text and link
Banners a banner's text and button address
Forms the form's introduction and success message, while it is on a page

The other bundled modules report none. A relative link in such content counts from the item's own address, such as a post's, or else from the page the instance is on; content without an address, such as a banner, or of an instance on no page, counts from the home page of its language. The editor of a published post, event, album, person or directory entry, and that of a published category of Publishing or Directory, asks before the item leaves its address, as a page's editor does, and offers the same redirects; see Links to an item. A directory category's entries leave the website with it, so its Unpublish and redirect redirects their addresses too, and an entry's old address leads to its new one when the category gets a new Web address. A module of your own reports its links with Parts.Links and adds this to its editor with editor.Linked; see Links to pages. The redirects module makes the redirects that the editors and the report offer, through Parts.Redirects.

Modules working together

Some modules use another instance, named by its key. Add that instance as well:

err = app.Use(
    events.Module("agenda", "Agenda"),
    registrations.Module("signup", "Sign-ups", registrations.ForEvents("agenda")),
    publishing.Module("news", "News"),
    submissions.Module("tips", "Tips", "news"),
)
  • Registrations with ForEvents lets editors open sign-ups per event of agenda; sign-ups close when the event starts unless editors set a deadline.
  • Submissions saves an accepted proposal as an unpublished post in news, through publishing.Service.Draft.
  • Comments and Registrations attach to any content by an ID the template passes, such as {{commentThread "remarks" .ID}} in a post template.

Inside a module, env.Service(key) returns another instance's service once the app runs; see Writing a module.

Integrations

Integrations with outside services live in go-webthings-contrib, so go-webthings itself needs no extra dependencies:

Package Use it for
mailjet mailjet.Sender sends the site's mail (Config.Mail); mailjet.List keeps a Mailjet contact list in step with a newsletter (newsletter.WithProvider)
s3 s3.New keeps uploaded media in an S3-compatible bucket (Config.Storage) 
err = app.Use(
    newsletter.Module("letters", "Newsletter", newsletter.WithProvider(mailjet.List{
        APIKey:    os.Getenv("MAILJET_API_KEY"),
        SecretKey: os.Getenv("MAILJET_SECRET_KEY"),
        ListID:    12345,
    })),
)

Guides.Title: Writing a module
Guides.Summary: A module adds content or a feature to a site through the same public API the bundled modules use. This guide builds a small links module step by step and points to the bundled modules for more.
Guides.Body:
What a module is

A module is a function that returns a webthings.Module, which the site passes to app.Use:

Field
Type The module's name. Its instances share the type's tables, and templates fall back from <key>/ to <type>/.
Key, Title The instance, as the site names it; see Using modules.
Schema The schema files as an fs.FS, or nil.
Setup func(webthings.Env) (webthings.Parts, error), required. It runs once per instance when the app starts.
Templates The screens the public handler renders. The site writes them.
Funcs Template functions for every template.
Components Parts of a page with default markup, rendered by the module's template functions.
Mail E-mail templates with a default text; see E-mail.
Forms The inputs of the module's visitor forms, structs with go-form's tags, such as SuggestionInput{}. Themes render them with form_open and form_field, translated; see Visitor actions.

Templates, components and mail are frontend.Template values: a Name (the file name without .gohtml), Data (a value of the data type) and an optional Example, which is the default of a component or mail and the starting point App.WriteTemplates writes for a screen.

Setup gets a webthings.Env with the shared services and returns webthings.Parts, what the instance adds to the site. Both are listed at the end of this guide.

The example: a links module

The links module keeps a list of links to other websites, such as partners. Editors write them in the admin, a page can show them, and any template can list them. It is a package in the site's own repository, with the module path example.com/mysite, and the site adds it like any other module:

err = app.Use(links.Module("partners", "Partners"))

Schema files

Schema files sit in one folder, named <YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>[_description].<flavour>.sql, such as schema/20261005120000_init.sqlite.sql. The datetime is the version, and every version needs a file for each flavour: sqlite, postgres and mysql. At start the app runs the current database's files that are newer than the version it recorded for the module type, each in a transaction. Statements end with ; at the end of a line; lines starting with -- are left out.

CREATE TABLE site_link (
    id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    instance   TEXT NOT NULL,
    published  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    position   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    created_by TEXT,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    updated_by TEXT,
    deleted_at TIMESTAMP,
    deleted_by TEXT,
    url        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

CREATE INDEX site_link_instance ON site_link (instance, position);

CREATE TABLE site_link_translation (
    item_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES site_link (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    locale      TEXT NOT NULL,
    title       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, locale)
);

The created_*, updated_* and deleted_* columns are the audit columns that the content engine fills; see Deleting and the trash. The PostgreSQL and MySQL files differ in types, as in ../modules/testimonials/schema: IDs, also in the *_by columns, are UUID and VARCHAR(36), times TIMESTAMPTZ and DATETIME(6), and MySQL declares indexes and foreign keys inside CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE=InnoDB. Core and the bundled modules use tables starting with wt_, so give yours another prefix. Before the site's first release, change the _init files and recreate the development database; after a release, add newer files instead.

The module embeds the folder with //go:embed schema/*.sql and passes it as Schema; below, schema() returns fs.Sub(schemaFiles, "schema"), as Databases shows.

Content

Package content stores multilingual content for modules. A module describes it with two structs, whose db tags name the columns, and a content.Spec:

// Fields are the parts of a link that every language shares.
type Fields struct {
    URL string `db:"url"`
}

// Text is a link in one language.
type Text struct {
    Title       string `db:"title"`
    Description string `db:"description"`
}

type Item = content.Item[Fields, Text]

var errURL = errors.New("links_invalid_url")

func spec() content.Spec[Fields, Text] {
    return content.Spec[Fields, Text]{
        Table: "site_link",
        Complete: func(text Text) bool {
            return text.Title != ""
        },
        Check: func(fields Fields, translations []content.Translation[Text]) error {
            parsed, err := url.Parse(fields.URL)
            if err != nil || parsed.Scheme != "https" || parsed.Host == "" {
                return errURL
            }

            if content.TooLong(2000, fields.URL) {
                return content.ErrTooLong
            }

            for _, translation := range translations {
                if content.TooLong(200, translation.Text.Title) || content.TooLong(1000, translation.Text.Description) {
                    return content.ErrTooLong
                }
            }

            return nil
        },
    }
}

Complete decides whether a translation can be shown; publishing needs a complete translation in the site's default language. Check validates every save, also from imports and seeds, which skip the form's maxLength. content.TooLong(limit, values...) counts characters, not bytes, as the form does; for content.ErrTooLong the editor says "The text is too long." on its own. SlugColumn names the slug of content with pages of its own, and Media lists the media it uses, which the library then refuses to delete, also while the item is in the trash. Deletable can refuse to delete an item; see Deleting and the trash. Changed is called after every committed write that may change what visitors see: publishing, unpublishing, moving an item to the trash and back and, for a Collection, saving an item and moving it in the order. Saving or restoring a draft of a Revisions and purging an item from the trash do not call it. Setup sets it to env.Changed, below, so the output cache shows such a write at once, also one made from Go; see The output cache. A db:"photo_id,null" tag stores an empty string as NULL, for optional references.

content.Collection content.Revisions
Keeps one row per item, with a published flag and an order immutable revisions: drafts, preview, history, restore, scheduled publishing and an optional review
Tables for Table: "x" x, x_translation (as above) x, x_revision, x_translation (see ../content/revisions.go)
Used by most bundled modules Pages, Publishing and Events

Both offer ListPublished, Published and PublishedBySlug for the website, and In(key) returns the content.Store of one instance, for the admin, imports and seeds. Revisions.Outline(ctx, instance, texts...) lists the newest revision of every item with only the named texts, such as "slug" and "title", for a tree or a menu that does not need long texts such as bodies.

The service

The service is the instance's API, for the public handler, the template functions and the site's own code. Like the bundled modules it can also offer Store(), returning s.items.In(s.key), for imports and seeds.

// Service is one instance: the links of one list.
type Service struct {
    key      string
    items    *content.Collection[Fields, Text]
    frontend *frontend.Frontend
}

// Link is a published link as templates see it.
type Link struct {
    ID          string
    Title       string
    Description string
    URL         string
}

// ListView is the data of links/list.gohtml.
type ListView struct {
    Title string
    Links []Link
}

// Of returns the instance with key from a started app, or nil.
func Of(app *webthings.App, key string) *Service {
    service, _ := app.Service(key).(*Service)

    return service
}

// Links returns the published links with a title in locale, in their order.
func (s *Service) Links(ctx context.Context, locale string) ([]Link, error) {
    items, err := s.items.ListPublished(ctx, s.key, locale)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    links := make([]Link, 0, len(items))

    for _, item := range items {
        text, _ := item.Text(locale)
        links = append(links, Link{ID: item.ID, Title: text.Title, Description: text.Description, URL: item.Fields.URL})
    }

    return links, nil
}

Module and Setup

//go:embed translations
var files embed.FS

// Module adds a list of links. key names the instance; title is what
// editors see.
func Module(key, title string) webthings.Module {
    return webthings.Module{
        Type:      "links",
        Key:       key,
        Title:     title,
        Schema:    schema(),
        Setup:     setup,
        Funcs:     funcs(),
        Templates: []frontend.Template{{Name: "list", Data: ListView{}}},
    }
}

func setup(env webthings.Env) (webthings.Parts, error) {
    itemsSpec := spec()
    itemsSpec.Changed = env.Changed

    items, err := content.NewCollection(env.DB, itemsSpec)
    if err != nil {
        return webthings.Parts{}, err
    }

    service := &Service{key: env.Key, items: items, frontend: env.Frontend}

    return webthings.Parts{
        Admin:   []admin.Section{section(env, service)},
        Public:  service.handler(),
        Feeds:   service.feeds(),
        Service: service,
    }, nil
}

section is built in The admin of a module and service.feeds() in Feeds.

The public handler

Parts.Public serves the instance at and below the page it is placed on:

func (s *Service) handler() http.Handler {
    routes := s.frontend.Router()

    routes.Get("/{$}", s.listPage)

    return routes
}

func (s *Service) listPage(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()
    mount := frontend.MountFrom(ctx)

    links, err := s.Links(ctx, mount.Locale)
    if err != nil {
        s.frontend.Fail(w, r, err)

        return
    }

    s.frontend.Render(w, r, frontend.Content{
        Template: "list",
        Title:    mount.Title,
        Data:     ListView{Title: mount.Title, Links: links},
    })
}

frontend.MountFrom tells where the request is: its language, the page's path and its published title. Render shows the screen in the site's layout, from partners/list.gohtml or links/list.gohtml. Without either the screen answers with an error, and the app logs missing template for each theme without it when it starts, with the command that writes it, task templates -- partners in a site made from the starter; that command calls App.WriteTemplates, which writes a starting point with every field of ListView. frontend.Content also takes a Description, an Image shown when the page is shared, Alternates (the content's path in other languages) and an EditURL for the edit link editors see, from env.AdminURL; without it the link goes to the section's index. Fail answers an error: content that does not exist (content.ErrNotFound) gets the 404 page, and any other error is logged with the module and the path and answered with status 500 by the theme's 500.gohtml, rendered as the theme's pages are, with its partials, its asset versions, @model View and the page's language, and with the status text, "Internal Server Error", translated with the site's translations as .Title. Without a 500.gohtml, go-partial's plain error page answers, with that heading and a message that tells nothing of the error, both translated, and the page's language as its lang; see Templates. An HTMX request gets the same page. With Config.Development the page shows the error itself; otherwise no error page names the error or the template that failed, also when 500.gohtml fails itself.

A view that shows an image of the media library, such as a photo, gets it from s.frontend.Image(ctx, id), a media.Image as pages show it: URL is a WebP copy at most media.ImageWidth (1600) pixels wide and never larger than the upload, Srcset lists copies up to that width for a srcset attribute, Width and Height are the size of URL, and OriginalURL is the uploaded file, for downloads. The view gives each as a field of its own, <X>URL, <X>Srcset, <X>Width, <X>Height and <X>OriginalURL, as the testimonials' PhotoURL and the others in ../modules/testimonials/testimonials.go; the original is never the default. A GIF and an address outside the library keep their own URL, and an empty ID gives an empty Image. MediaURL is the address of the uploaded file itself, for a download such as a PDF; see Media and images.

A view of something that takes place at a time, such as an event, gives that time with a method When() frontend.When, as events.Event and registrations.Subject do: Start and End in the timezone they are shown in, End zero without an end, and AllDay. SameDay reports whether it ends on the day it starts. One partial of the theme, with {{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend.When */}}, then shows the time of any of them.

Router returns a go-router of the instance's own. The site serves it at the page's address for each request, so its routes are relative to the page, whatever the page's address: /{$} is the page itself and /{slug} an item below it. Handlers see the whole path, such as /en/partners/go, and r.PathValue("slug") reads a parameter. Every request without a route, any path or method, gets the site's 404 page, which NotFound renders; a route that answers 404 itself keeps its own answer. A module therefore registers no / route. Middleware comes before the routes: routes.Use wraps the routes and the 404 page, so a check of posts also sees posts to a path without a route, and routes.UseAll wraps every answer before a route is matched, for example headers that keep the answers out of caches; see ../modules/forms/public.go. Route names are the module's own. In a handler, routes.For(r) builds their addresses at the page the request is on: with routes.Get("/{slug}", s.linkPage).As("link"), routes.For(r).RoutePathArgs("link", "slug", "go") returns /en/partners/go, and a route /{$} named list is the page itself, /en/partners, without a trailing slash. Any other http.Handler as Parts.Public sees the whole path too and finds its page with frontend.MountFrom, whose Locale and Path, such as en and /partners, make the page's address, /en/partners. Such a handler builds the links below its page itself, where a Frontend.Router builds them from route names.

Content with pages of its own sets SlugColumn, registers a named route such as routes.Get("/{slug}", s.linkPage).As("link"), finds the item with PublishedBySlug and r.PathValue("slug"), links to it with routes.For(r) and lists its paths in Parts.Sitemap. Its form labels the slug Web address, as the bundled modules do, and editor.Slug(in.Slug, in.Title) in Apply makes an empty one from the title, as for posts and events; a title without letters content.Slug can use gives "". The router gives those without a request, below the page: routes.RoutePathArgs("link", "slug", "go") is /go. A service method that lists the items for another page or the search has no request either. Had the service kept the router, a go-router *router.Router, as s.public and env.Pages as s.pages, s.public.At(base) builds the addresses that For(r) gives, below base, the instance's page in a language from MountURL. While the instance is on no page, MountURL is "" and pages.NoLinks stands in: it returns "" for every route, so the items are still listed, without links. pages.Links(routes, base) chooses between the two. It returns go-router's router.PathFunc, to which NoLinks and any RoutePathArgs method value can be assigned, also those of For(r) and At(base):

// paths builds the addresses of the instance's routes in locale outside a
// request: below its page, or none while it is on no page.
func (s *Service) paths(ctx context.Context, locale string) (router.PathFunc, error) {
    base, err := s.pages.MountURL(ctx, s.key, locale)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    return pages.Links(s.public, base), nil
}

paths("link", "slug", "go") is then /en/partners/go. See ../modules/gallery/module.go and the Albums method in ../modules/gallery/gallery.go.

Template functions

A template function whose first parameter is a context.Context gets the context of the request. frontend.ServiceOf[*Service](ctx, key) returns an instance's service while a page renders, and frontend.Locale the page's language:

func funcs() template.FuncMap {
    return template.FuncMap{
        "links": list,
    }
}

// list returns the published links of an instance in the page's language,
// for example {{range links "partners"}} in a footer.
func list(ctx context.Context, key string) []Link {
    service, ok := frontend.ServiceOf[*Service](ctx, key)
    if !ok {
        return nil
    }

    links, err := service.Links(ctx, frontend.Locale(ctx))
    if err != nil {
        slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "template links", "module", key, "error", err)
    }

    return links
}

Use ServiceOf rather than frontend.Service(ctx, key).(*Service): a key the site has no instance of this module for is a mistake in a template that would show nothing, so ServiceOf logs it once at WARN as template mistake, with the function's name in the template and the keys there are, such as links: no links instance "partner" (known: partners), and with Config.Development the page fails with that message. Outside a render it reports false.

Instances of one type share the functions, so the key is their first argument. When two module types offer the same name, the app does not start; the same goes for a name go-partial or core's renderer uses, such as url, locale, slot, requiredSlot, deferredSlot, targetHeader, targetValue or targetIs, or one starting with _ (render.ErrReserved; render.Reserved(name) checks one).

Components

A component is a part of a page with default markup. Declare it in Module.Components with its default as Example, under a name none of the module's screens has, and render it from a template function with frontend.Component:

const boxExample = `<aside class="links">
    <h2>{{tl localizer "Links"}}</h2>
    <ul>{{range .}}<li><a href="{{.URL}}" rel="external">{{.Title}}</a></li>{{end}}</ul>
</aside>
`

// box renders the box component, for example {{linkBox "partners"}}.
func box(ctx context.Context, key string) (template.HTML, error) {
    links := list(ctx, key)
    if len(links) == 0 {
        return "", nil
    }

    return frontend.Component(ctx, key, "box", links)
}

With Components: []frontend.Template{{Name: "box", Data: []Link{}, Example: boxExample}} and "linkBox": box in funcs, a theme can replace the markup with partners/box.gohtml or links/box.gohtml. Write default texts with tl localizer, so the site's translations apply.

Write a module's default templates and components without style attributes, <style> elements, inline scripts and event handler attributes, as the bundled modules do: the site's Content-Security-Policy blocks them under Enforce. Give the markup classes that webthings.css or the theme styles, and show a share as a <meter>, as the polls module does. See A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own.

Topic guides

These guides continue the links module:

  • The admin of a module builds the admin section that Setup returns, and covers screens of a module's own, deleting and the trash, and previews and review.
  • Visitor actions and forms of a module adds a form for link suggestions and covers how a module receives, checks and keeps visitors' posts.
  • Feeds, structured data, API and links of a module adds the links module's feed, its endpoints in the content API and the links in its content to the site's pages, and covers structured data for search engines.
  • Caching and testing a module explains how the output cache keeps a module's pages and learns of its changes, and how to test a module.

Parts

Field Adds
Admin Admin sections, usually one at /<key> below the admin, /admin/<key> by default.
Public The handler at and below the instance's page, usually a Frontend.Router. Nil means it cannot be placed on a page.
Service The API that App.Service, Env.Service and frontend.Service return.
Sitemap The paths below the page per language, for sitemap.xml.
Feeds Atom and RSS feeds below the instance's page, as routes of Public, which is then a Frontend.Router; see Feeds.
ActionBodyLimit The largest request body the routes of Env.Actions accept in bytes; zero is 1 MiB (webthings.DefaultActionBodyLimit).
Middleware A wrapper around the public site, for example to redirect old addresses. It runs before the output cache and compression, so it sees every request for the site's pages, also those the cache answers, and a response it reads may be gzip-compressed (Content-Encoding). Editors are recognised before it, so frontend.Editor(r.Context()) tells them from visitors. App.CorePaths() lists the addresses core serves itself, such as the admin's (Config.AdminPath), /_ and /media; requests below most of them never reach it. env.IsCorePath(path) checks one. Both come from the app's own routes, so the list is complete, and they work from webthings.New on.
Close A function run when the app closes, before the database, for example to write buffered data.
Search Results for the site search; ../modules/lists/search.go scores them with frontend.ParseQuery. See Search and SEO.
Scheduled Planned publication of revisioned content, a []content.Scheduler: usually []content.Scheduler{posts.Scheduler(env.Key)} for a content.Revisions.
Links The links in the module's published content, a links.Func, so the admin knows which content links to a page; see Links to pages.
Redirects A links.Redirector when the module redirects old addresses: the admin then offers to redirect the addresses a page or an item leaves. The first module that sets it is used.
API The module's endpoints in the content API, a go-router of api.NewRouter(), mounted at /api/v1/<key>/ while Config.API turns the API on; see The content API.
StructuredData A frontend.StructuredDataFunc that adds to the structured data of other modules' pages, or changes it; a module's own pages give theirs in frontend.Content.StructuredData. See Structured data.

Env

Field
Key, Title The instance.
DB The database, with Get, Select, Exec, Tx and ? placeholders on every database.
Locales, Site The site's languages and settings.
Auth, Media, Pages Accounts, the media library and the page tree. Pages.MountURL(ctx, key, locale) is the address of the instance's page, such as /en/partners, or "" while it is on no page; pages.Links(routes, base) builds the addresses of the public router's routes below it, with routes.At(base), or none with pages.NoLinks while it is ""; see The public handler.
Frontend Render, NotFound, Fail, Router, Route, Image, MailImage, AltText, MediaURL, Markdown, AbsoluteMarkdown, MarkdownOptions, TagURI, ModulePreviewURL, SocialImageURL, Mail, SendMail, BackLocale, BindForm, KeepForm and ValidateSchema. Markdown keeps what it rendered, so a handler can render a body on every request. AbsoluteMarkdown and TagURI are for feeds, and MarkdownOptions for Markdown rendered in your own code, such as for e-mail; see Feeds. SocialImageURL is for structured data; see Structured data.
Mail The site's mail.Sender.
BaseURL, AbsoluteURL(r, path) Absolute links, for e-mail.
AdminLanguage The admin's language, for mail to staff.
Service(key) Another instance's service once the app has started, nil before: resolve it in handlers, not in Setup.
Secret(ctx, name) A random 32-byte key of the instance, the same in every process, for example to hash visitors' addresses.
VisitorID(ctx, r, parts...) A visitor's address hashed with the instance's secret, as 64 hexadecimal digits; the parts, such as the date, narrow it.
AdminURL(name, args...) The address of a named admin route once the app has started, "" before; see The admin section.
Actions() The go-router of the instance's visitor actions at /_/<key>/; see Visitor actions.
IsCorePath(path) Whether core serves path itself, such as the admin's pages; see Middleware in Parts.
Links() The site's link check, a *links.Check, for the editor of items with an address of their own (editor.Linked); see Links to pages. Nil on an Env made without an app.
Changed() Tells the output cache that what visitors see of the module changed. Stores whose content.Spec has Changed set to it call it themselves. Call it after the commit, such as with db.AfterWrite; App.Changed() is the same for the site's own code. See The output cache.
PersonalCookie(name) Names a cookie of the module that changes what a page shows to the visitor who has it, so the output cache keeps the page apart per value; call it in Setup.

Rules for modules

The bundled modules are built like a module from any other repository. ../testsuite/architecture_test.go checks that:

  • core never imports a module;
  • modules use core's public packages, never internal/;
  • modules add no dependencies beyond the standard library, core, other modules and the libraries core already uses, such as go-form; anything else belongs in go-webthings-contrib;
  • nothing imports go-webthings-contrib;
  • sitetest, with sitetest/catalogtest, and db/dbtest are used in tests only.

A module in your own repository cannot import internal/ packages either, and may depend on what it needs.

Fuller examples

  • Testimonials and Lists: collections like the links module, with an image; Lists also joins the site search.
  • Gallery and People: items with pages of their own and a sitemap.
  • Publishing and Events: revisions, previews, scheduled publishing, feeds, structured data and endpoints in the content API.
  • Comments, Polls and Registrations: visitor actions, components and mail; Registrations also sets Parts.StructuredData.
  • Submissions: records in a table of their own, with a list screen, filter tabs, a settings screen and the trash.
  • Redirects and Stats: middleware and a Close function; Redirects also sets Parts.Redirects.

Guides.Title: The admin of a module
Guides.Summary: This guide continues the links module of Writing a module in the admin: the section in which editors write the links, screens of a module's own, deleting and the trash, and previews and review for content with revisions.
Guides.Body:
The admin section

Package admin/editor is the generic admin for content stores: an overview with language tabs and a search field, an editor per language, publication and, for ordered stores, arrow buttons to move items. Its save button reads Save for a content.Collection and Save draft for a content.Revisions, whose saves are drafts; Unpublish asks "Take this off the website?" and Move to trash "Move this item to the trash?". The module supplies a go-form struct for one language and two mapping functions:

type linkInput struct {
    Title       string `form:"input,text" label:"Title"       required:"true" maxLength:"200"`
    URL         string `form:"input,text" label:"Address"     required:"true" maxLength:"2000" placeholder:"https://" trim:"true"`
    Description string `form:"textarea"   label:"Description"                 maxLength:"1000"`
}

func section(env webthings.Env, service *Service) admin.Section {
    return editor.New(editor.Config[Fields, Text, linkInput]{
        ID:       env.Key,
        Title:    env.Title,
        Icon:     "link",
        NewLabel: "New link",
        Store:    service.items.In(env.Key),
        Locales:  env.Locales,
        Files:    files,
        Label: func(text Text) string {
            return text.Title
        },
        Form: func(_ context.Context, item Item, locale string) (linkInput, error) {
            text, _ := item.Text(locale)

            return linkInput{Title: text.Title, URL: item.Fields.URL, Description: text.Description}, nil
        },
        Apply: func(_ context.Context, in linkInput, draft *content.Draft[Fields, Text], locale string) error {
            draft.Fields = Fields{URL: in.URL}
            draft.Translations = content.SetText(draft.Translations, locale, Text{
                Title:       in.Title,
                Description: in.Description,
            })

            return nil
        },
        Issue: func(err error) string {
            if errors.Is(err, errURL) {
                return "Enter an address starting with https://."
            }

            return ""
        },
    })
}

Form fills the form for one language; the item is empty for a new link. Apply writes a submitted form into the draft, and Issue turns the module's errors into a message for the editor. go-form checks the tags first: required:"true" counts a value of only spaces as empty, and minLength does not count spaces around the text. An address of only spaces therefore gets go-form's "This field is required.", not the message from Issue. trim:"true" removes the white space around the address as the form is read, before Apply sees it. Path is the section's address below the admin; empty, as here, is / followed by ID, such as /partners. The admin itself is at /admin unless Config.AdminPath moves it; see Configuration. Other fields add buttons on the overview (Links, each to a URL or to an admin route by name in Route), notes per item (Notes), a preview on the website (PreviewURL; see Previews and review), names in the revision history (Names: env.Auth.Names), a count in the navigation and under Needs attention on the dashboard (Badge), an overview of the module's own instead of the list (Overview; editor.Status(item, revisioned) names an item's state there, such as "Draft" or "Published", for the template to translate), items that stay on the website by their nature, such as the home page (Permanent; see Deleting and the trash), screens of the module's own (Routes; see Screens of your own), notices and other changes on the edit screen of an item (Edit; see Links to pages), a follow-up after an existing item is saved (Saved; see the same section) and deleted records of the module's own in the trash (Trash; see Deleting and the trash). editor.MediaChoices makes a dropdown of the media library's files by name, or of its images only. Its field, a form.SortedSelect[string], needs a placeholder, such as placeholder:"—", to offer no file; see ../modules/lists/module.go.

Editor sections also feed the admin's dashboard and trash on their own: their most recently edited items, their planned publication changes, their revisions waiting for review, a "New …" quick action and their deleted items. An admin.Section of your own can do the same with NewLabel and NewRoute, Recent, Scheduled, Review and Trash. NewRoute is the name of the section's route for a new item, such as new, which editor sections set; route names are explained below. A name the section did not register shows no quick action. NewPath, a path below the admin like Path, such as /partners/new, applies only while NewRoute is empty. Admin.QuickActions(r) returns the sections' "New …" actions that the user may take, in the order of the navigation, each an admin.QuickAction with a Label, the Section and a URL, for a screen of your own that suggests what to add first, as the Pages step of the setup guide does. Recent, Scheduled and Review are each a func(ctx, limit), returning []admin.RecentItem, []admin.ScheduledItem and []admin.ReviewItem, whose URL links to the item; admin.RouteURL(ctx, name, args...) builds it from a route name. They run on every dashboard view, so each reads at most limit items and leaves deleted items out: Recent the newest first, Scheduled the earliest planned change first and Review the oldest request first. A content store's Recent(ctx, limit) does this for Recent. Group lists a section under a heading in the navigation; webthings.Module.Group sets it for all of a module's sections and wins over the section's own, and without either the section is listed under admin.GroupModules. See Using modules.

Callout, a func(ctx) (admin.Callout, bool), shows a card above the dashboard's panels that asks the user to finish something, such as the Site settings' "Finish setting up your site" with "2 of 5 steps done". An admin.Callout has a Title and a Text, shown as written, so translate them first, a button to URL with the text Action, a translation key such as "Continue setup", and a progress bar of Done of Total, none while Total is zero. The dashboard asks it for the users who may view the section, with a context that carries the signed-in user (auth.CurrentUser), on every view, so keep it cheap; false shows no card. The Site settings and Theme sections of core are built with siteadmin.New(settings, options) and siteadmin.NewTheme(settings, options), which take one siteadmin.Options for both: Media, Fixed, Frontend, Public, Pages, Modules, Mail and BaseURL, what the settings, the theme cards and the setup guide need. The app builds both at start.

The dashboard shows at once and loads its panels after it. Each panel asks all sections at the same time, for at most eight items, and waits five seconds at most. A section that fails, panics or has not answered by then is named in the panel as one that could not be loaded; the other sections still show. Badge runs on every admin page, for each section in the navigation. The badges are asked for at the same time too, and one that takes longer than a second shows no count, so keep it to one cheap query. All of these get a context that ends at the timeout: pass it on to the database, so a slow query stops. Editor sections list planned changes only from stores that implement content.Planner, as those of a content.Revisions do; a store of your own that wraps one needs Planned too, or the dashboard shows none of its plans. Editing shows the dashboard as editors see it.

Every page of a section, also a screen of your own, shows in its header who else is looking at it, to the users who may view the section. The admin does this on its own. A page is its path without the query, so the language tabs of an editor are one page. A page must be the address of one of the section's routes, and forms for new items, routes named new or with a name ending in -new, such as mailing-new, show no one. See Editing.

Every admin route needs an action in its section: admin.View, admin.Create, admin.Edit, admin.Publish, admin.Delete, admin.Review or admin.Export. The editor asks View to look, Create for new items, Edit to save, move and submit for review, Publish to publish and plan, Delete to move items to the trash, and Review to approve and reject. Each section is a row in the groups' permission matrix, unless its Permission names another section whose row it shares. Only sections with Review offer the Review right. admin.Export is for downloads of personal data, such as subscribers as CSV: only sections that register a route with it offer the Export right, and the matrix shows the Export column only when one does. A user without the right gets status 403. An admin.Section of your own registers handlers in Routes with routes.Get(pattern, action, handler) and routes.Post, at patterns below the section's path, such as /{id}. Handlers see the full path, and r.PathValue("id") reads a parameter. .Use(middleware...) after a route adds middleware inside its permission check: with admin.AdministratorsOnly, every user who is not an administrator gets status 403, for changes only administrators may make, such as the site's security settings. A page that shows such settings to other users shows them read-only itself. Handlers show pages with routes.Admin().Render; see ../modules/submissions/module.go and Accounts and permissions.

Links into the admin are built from route names, never from paths, as the admin may be anywhere. .As(name) after Get or Post names a route admin.<section ID>.<name>, which Section.RouteName(name) and admin.RouteName(section, name) return. By convention a section's own page is index, the form for a new item new and an item's page edit or show; a post to the address of a named page needs no name of its own. A route or a name registered twice makes admin.New fail, so the app does not start. routes.URL(name, args...) builds the address of one of the section's routes, with name and value pairs for its parameters and url.Values for a query. Admin.URL does the same for any route by its full name, such as the admin's own admin.dashboard and admin.trash, and so does {{route name args...}} in admin templates, next to go-router's other functions, such as hasRoute and routeOr. Editor sections name their routes too, such as index, new and edit: routes.URL("edit", "id", id) is the editor of one link, so screens a module adds to an editor section choose other names. Outside the admin, such as in a public handler or an e-mail to staff, env.AdminURL does the same once the app has started. They panic on an unknown name or a missing parameter, a mistake in the code, and the request gets status 500; Admin.TryURL returns an error instead.

Labels and messages are written in English and translated into the admin's language (Config.AdminLanguage) from translations/<locale>.po in the section's Files, such as translations/nl_NL.po with msgid "New link" and msgstr "Nieuwe link". Copy the header from a bundled module, such as ../modules/lists/translations/nl_NL.po. go-form's own messages, such as "This field is required.", come with go-form in English and Dutch, so a module's catalogues leave them out; a field's own message from a tag, such as urlMsg, is translated like a label. A site can change any text: a catalogue on disk, such as <StateDir>/translations/nl_NL.po, wins over the embedded ones, and an entry left empty there keeps the embedded text. That folder is optional, and the admin writes nothing to it: it does not record the texts it looks up while it serves, so keep a module's texts in the module's own catalogues. The admin finds a catalogue for its language as go-translator's language fallback does, message by message: nl uses nl.po and, for what that lacks, nl_NL.po. See Languages. A test with catalogtest.Complete checks that the catalogues miss none of the texts of the section's forms; see Testing.

Screens of your own

A screen of your own looks and works like the editor's when it uses the admin's shared parts. ../modules/submissions/admin.go is a list built this way.

Every list in the admin has a search field. Every admin page offers it as the go-partial model Search, an admin.SearchBox that is computed only when a template uses it. Declare it at the top of the screen's template with {{/* @model Search github.com/donseba/go-webthings/admin.SearchBox */}}, put {{template "admin-search" Search}} in the actions of the screen's header, and {{template "admin-empty" Search}} where the list is empty; it says that nothing matched, or that there is nothing yet. On the overview of a section with a NewLabel, the empty list also offers that action, such as "New link", to users who may create.

admin.ListPage reads the page of a list that a request asks for, with its page and q parameters. Without a search, Load(ctx, limit, offset) reads that page from the database: at most limit rows from offset, in the order of SQL's LIMIT and OFFSET, and whether more follow. With a search, it reads at most admin.SearchLimit() rows (5000), keeps those whose Fields match and pages the matches. A row matches when every word occurs in one of its fields, ignoring case and accents. A list that is read whole sets All instead of Load. Read returns the page's Rows and its Pager, which {{template "admin-pager" .Pager}} shows below the rows. Size is the number of rows per page, admin.DefaultPageSize (50) when zero.

This handler lists the link suggestions of Visitor actions, had the module stored them. screens holds the service, routes.Admin() and the section's routes, which registered the list with routes.Get("/suggestions", admin.View, list.suggestions).As("suggestions"):

func (s screens) suggestions(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()

    list, err := admin.ListPage[Suggestion]{
        Path: s.routes.URL("suggestions"),
        Load: s.service.Suggestions,
        Fields: func(suggestion Suggestion) []string {
            return []string{suggestion.URL, suggestion.Name}
        },
    }.Read(r)
    if err != nil {
        s.admin.Fail(w, r, err)

        return
    }

    view := SuggestionsView{Pager: list.Pager}

    for _, suggestion := range list.Rows {
        view.Rows = append(view.Rows, SuggestionRow{
            URL:  suggestion.URL,
            Name: suggestion.Name,
            Sent: admin.DateTime(ctx, suggestion.CreatedAt),
        })
    }

    s.admin.Render(w, r, admin.Page{
        Title:    "Suggestions",
        Template: "templates/suggestions.gohtml",
        Files:    files,
        Data:     view,
    })
}

The template sits in files next to the translations (//go:embed translations templates). Page.Title is translated. A title that editors typed, such as the name of the item on the screen, goes in Page.Label instead, which is shown as written. Editor sections search on their own, in each item's label and note.

Admin pages get the site's Content-Security-Policy when it is on, with the hash of the admin's import map, Admin.ImportMapHash(); see A Content-Security-Policy of the site's own. Under Enforce browsers block a style attribute, a <style> element, an inline script and an event handler attribute, such as onclick or hx-on, so a screen's template has none. Style its markup with the classes of the admin's stylesheet, listed in ../admin/doc.go, and with a stylesheet of the section's own: Section.Stylesheet names a CSS file in the section's Files. A bar of a chart is <span class="bar bar-40"></span>, with a class from bar-0 to bar-100 for its height in percent, and a share bar is <progress class="meter" max="100" value="40">. The admin's own parts work the same way. The chip of an admin.PresenceViewer has the class presence-hue-<Hue>, with Hue from 0 to 11. A crop preview of the media library, a mediaadmin.CropPreview, has its focal point in Class, a class of focal-points.css such as fp-35-60. frontend.FocalPointsStylesheet() gives that focal-points.css to a part of the site that serves it with its own files, as the admin does for these previews.

Filter tabs above a list, such as its statuses, come from admin.FilterTabs(r, label, path, name, current, tabs...) and show with {{template "admin-tabs" .Tabs}}. Each admin.Tab sets the parameter name to its Value, and Count with Counted adds a badge. The links of the tabs and the pager keep the request's other parameters, such as the search. Content in several languages gets language tabs: admin.ContentLocale(r, config) reads the language from the locale parameter, with config from env.Locales.Configuration(ctx), and admin.LocaleTabs(config.Enabled, locale, path, nil) with {{template "locale-tabs.gohtml" .Tabs}} shows them, each named in its own language, with the code only where two languages share a name. A list built in another way uses the parts: admin.SearchOf(r) reads the search, its Matches checks one row, admin.Filter and admin.Paginate filter and page a slice, and admin.NewPager makes the pager.

A page with one form, such as the settings of an instance, is an admin.FormScreen[In]. Show fills the form with Load. Post validates a post, stores it with Save and returns to the page with "Changes saved.". Register both at one address, such as routes.Get("/settings", admin.View, settings.Show).As("settings") and routes.Post("/settings", admin.Edit, settings.Post): the form posts to the address it is shown at, so it needs no Action. Save refuses a single field with admin.FieldError(field, message), which shows at that field with status 422; translate the message first. ../modules/comments/admin.go edits its settings this way.

A part of a screen that HTMX asks for on its own, such as a list a form updates, is a fragment. List it in admin.Page.Fragments as a render.Fragment with the ID of its element, its template and its data, and place it with {{slot "ID"}} or {{requiredSlot "ID"}}; for an ID the page has no fragment of, requiredSlot fails the render and slot shows nothing. A request aimed at that ID gets the fragment alone. Dot in place of Data, such as go-partial's partial.DotFuncOf(load), computes the fragment's data only when it renders, and Page.Dot the page's, so a request for the fragment alone does not pay for the rest of the page. A Deferred fragment loads after the page: the page shows a placeholder that asks for the fragment as soon as the page loads, and never computes the fragment's data. Placeholder names a template of the page's Files for that placeholder and defers the fragment too. Its dot is go-partial's slots.PlaceholderData, and its outer element must carry id="{{.ID}}" and {{.Attrs}}, which make it ask for the fragment. The fragment's PlaceholderData is the placeholder's .Data, so one placeholder template serves several fragments. The dashboard's panels load this way, with their heading as .Data and "Loading" as the placeholder. See HTMX.

Ordered lists use arrow buttons. admin.Moves(upURL, downURL) returns the pair for one row and {{template "admin-moves" .Moves}} shows it; an empty URL shows that arrow disabled, at the first or the last place. Register each URL as a post route with admin.Edit, as the editor does. The editor hides the arrows while searching, since moving needs the whole list. ../modules/gallery/admin.go orders an album's images this way.

Notices show as toasts in the corner of the screen. After a post, Admin.Redirect shows one on the next page, chosen by the name of the post's route, the part after its last dot or dash: "Published." after a route named publish or revision-publish, "Unpublished." after unpublish, "Moved to the trash." after delete, "Revision restored as a new draft." after restore, "Publication scheduled." after schedule, "Schedule cancelled." after unschedule, and "Changes saved." after other posts. A post without a name of its own has the name of the page at its address. Admin.RedirectNotice shows a success message of your own, written in English, which it translates before it redirects. Other toasts are messages of go-partial's flash package (github.com/donseba/go-partial/exp/flash). Admin.RedirectFlash(w, r, target, message) shows one of any level after a post, such as flash.Warn(text). A handler that renders a page itself adds them to the request before Render: admin.WithError an error, for a problem with the whole post, such as a file that cannot be read, and flash.Add one of any level. Their text is shown as given, so translate it first:

r = admin.WithError(r, admin.T(r.Context(), "The file could not be read."))

flash.Success and flash.Info hide after five seconds; flash.Warn and flash.Error stay until the editor closes them.

A handler that refuses a request without showing a page answers with Admin.Forbidden (403, "You are not allowed to do this."), or with Admin.BadRequest (400, "This request could not be read.") for a post that no form of the screen sends. Admin.Fail logs an unexpected error and answers 500 with "The request failed. Please try again.". The texts are in the admin's language. An HTMX request gets the text as an error toast and leaves the screen as it is; any other request gets the text alone.

Templates translate statuses and other labels with {{tl localizer .Status}}. Fixed choices in a form, such as a dropdown of statuses, get translate:"true" on their field: go-form then translates the option labels, written in English, from the module's catalogue, with the label as the msgid. Labels from a values: tag are translated without it; choices made of the site's own data, such as categories, stay as they are. required:"true" works on these fields too: an empty or unknown choice counts as missing. Dates and money follow the admin's language and the site's timezone: admin.DateTime(ctx, t) writes "5 Oct 2026 14:05", admin.Date(ctx, t) "5 Oct 2026", and admin.Format(ctx) formats the rest, such as admin.Format(ctx).Money(1250, "EUR"). admin.LanguageName("nl") names a language in its own language ("Nederlands"), as the language tabs do, and admin.LanguageLabel("nl") adds the code ("Nederlands (nl)"), as the languages of the site settings do; and admin.TimezoneChoices(selected) is a dropdown of time zones with their offset from UTC.

A screen of your own with a form reads its post with Admin.Bind(r, &input), which maps the post onto the form's struct and validates it, as the editor and FormScreen do. It returns the field errors, translated, for the form to show at their fields; answer them with status 422. A value it cannot read as its field's type, such as "abc" for a number, a date in another format or a choice the form does not offer, is not mapped: it comes back as a field error, in place of what validation says about that field. Admin.MapForm(r, &input) maps the same way without validating. Both return an error only for a post they cannot map at all, which no form of the screen sends:

func (s screens) saveNote(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    var input noteInput

    errs, err := s.admin.Bind(r, &input)
    if err != nil {
        s.admin.BadRequest(w, r)

        return
    }

    if len(errs) > 0 {
        s.noteForm(w, r, input, errs, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity)

        return
    }

    // Store the note, then return with s.admin.Redirect.
}

noteForm renders the screen as its GET route does, with the post and its errors in the page's data. Its template shows them with {{form_render_localized localizer .Form .Errors}}, where .Form is Admin.Form(r, input, action, submit). ../modules/comments/admin.go answers comments this way.

A time that editors enter in a form:"input,datetime-local" field has no timezone. The admin reads and shows it in the site's timezone, Admin.Location(r), in a time.Time field, or a *time.Time that stays nil when the field is empty. The editor reads its form this way, and so do Admin.Bind and Admin.MapForm; go-form's own form.MapForm reads the time in UTC. The admin's localizer is a go-form form.TimeLocalizer of the same timezone, so the field shows a stored time as the editor entered it. Convert the time with UTC() before storing it, as ../modules/polls/module.go does with a poll's closing time. A time of another timezone than the site's, such as an event's start in the event's own timezone, gets wallclock:"true": the field is read and shown as typed, as a time in UTC, and go-form's form.WallTime(t, location) turns it into the instant at which the clocks in location show that time, as ../modules/events/module.go does. Visitor forms read and show date-times in the site's timezone too (BindForm). Date, time and month inputs hold no instant: go-form reads them in UTC and shows them without converting, so a date does not move a day.

An import takes its file in a go-form file field, a *multipart.FileHeader with form:"input,file". Its accept and maxSize tags refuse another type or a larger file at the field, and Section.MaxBodyBytes raises the admin's limit of 512 KiB per request. A larger request gets status 413 with "Upload request too large.", as a toast or as text like the refusals above; see ../modules/directory/import.go. admin.ReadCSV reads a file saved by a spreadsheet program: it skips a byte order mark and splits on the comma, semicolon or tab that the first line has most of. For an export, admin.WriteCSV(w, name, header, rows) answers with a CSV download that is never cached. It puts an apostrophe before every value that a spreadsheet would run as a formula (admin.CSVCell). Register the export's route with admin.Export.

Deleting and the trash

Deleting moves an item to the trash. Store.Delete sets its deleted_at and deleted_by, and the item leaves the website, every list and the dashboard. It keeps its place, its publication and the media it uses, so Undelete brings it back as it was; revisioned content loses its planned publication. Trashed lists the deleted items, the most recently deleted first, and Purge removes one for good. Collection and Revisions have the same methods, with the instance as an extra argument. Editing shows the trash as editors see it.

The content engine fills the audit columns of the schema in Schema files. created_by, updated_by and deleted_by hold the signed-in user, or NULL for visitors and the scheduler. Tables for records of your own need the same columns and fill them with db.Stamp(ctx), which returns the time and the signed-in user; see Databases.

Spec.Deletable can refuse a delete with an error, for example while live items of another type still use the item. The editor shows the error through Issue. ../modules/directory/directory.go refuses to delete a category that still has entries.

Permanent items stay on the website. Their editor offers no unpublish, no planned unpublication and no delete, and refuses them with status 422 when they are posted anyway; planning a publication stays allowed. Some items are permanent by their nature: editor.Config.Permanent names them, such as the home page, and Issue can explain editor.ErrPermanent for them. Administrators mark other items permanent in their editor, with Make permanent and Remove permanent mark; the mark of an item that is permanent by its nature cannot be removed. Editor sections do all this on their own. See Editing.

The app keeps the marks with admin.NewPermanence, in core's table wt_permanent_items, by section ID and item ID. A screen of your own that unpublishes or deletes items of an editor section checks them first. Admin.Permanence() (e.Admin().Permanence() in the editor's Routes) returns nil when the admin keeps no marks (admin.Options.Permanence); otherwise its Permanent(ctx, section, id) reports whether an item is marked, with the editor's ID as the section. Check Config.Permanent too, and refuse the change when either holds. In the editor's Routes, e.RefusePermanent(w, r) does both for the item whose ID is the route's {id}: for a permanent item it shows the editor with the reason, with status 422, and returns true. It also returns true when it answered an error itself, such as 404 for an unknown item, so the handler returns when it does. The content stores check neither, so imports and seeds can still unpublish and delete permanent items.

The admin's trash lists the deleted items of every section with a Trash. Editor sections have one. Records of your own, outside a content store, get one from admin.RecordTrash, and db.SoftTable writes the statements of their table: Delete moves a row to the trash, Undelete brings it back, Purge removes it for good and Trashed reads the trash. Had the module stored the link suggestions in a table site_link_suggestion of its own, with the audit columns, and kept the database in the service as s.db:

// suggestions is the instance's part of site_link_suggestion.
func (s *Service) suggestions() db.SoftTable {
    return db.SoftTable{DB: s.db, Table: "site_link_suggestion", Scope: "instance=?", Args: []any{s.key}}
}

// trash lists the deleted suggestions in the admin's trash.
func (s *Service) trash() admin.Trash {
    return admin.RecordTrash(admin.TrashRecords[Suggestion]{
        Load: func(ctx context.Context, limit, offset int) ([]Suggestion, int, error) {
            var trashed []Suggestion

            columns := "id, url, name, deleted_at, deleted_by"
            total, err := s.suggestions().Trashed(ctx, &trashed, columns, limit, offset)

            return trashed, total, err
        },
        Fields: func(suggestion Suggestion) []string {
            return []string{suggestion.URL, suggestion.Name}
        },
        Item: func(suggestion Suggestion) admin.TrashItem {
            return admin.TrashItem{
                ID:        suggestion.ID,
                Title:     suggestion.URL,
                DeletedAt: *suggestion.DeletedAt,
                DeletedBy: suggestion.DeletedBy.String(),
            }
        },
        Undelete: func(ctx context.Context, id string) error {
            return s.suggestions().Undelete(ctx, id)
        },
        Purge: func(ctx context.Context, id string) error {
            return s.suggestions().Purge(ctx, id)
        },
    })
}

Suggestion reads deleted_at into a *time.Time and deleted_by into a db.Ref. Load(ctx, limit, offset), with the arguments in a list's order, returns one page of the trash, the most recently deleted first, and how many records it holds in all; SoftTable.Trashed reads both. A search of the trash reads at most admin.SearchLimit() records and matches their Fields. A delete button posts to a route with admin.Delete that calls s.suggestions().Delete(ctx, id). Scope limits every statement to the instance's rows. Each returns db.ErrNotFound for a row that is not where it should be, which the trash explains to the editor (admin.NotInTrash). Undelete(ctx, id, checks...) runs checks first, in one transaction with the change, to keep a record in the trash that may not come back. Purge(ctx, id, steps...) runs steps first, for what goes with the record, such as the media it uses. TrashRecords.Reason explains the module's own errors, in English: the editor sees the reason at that record, and the other records of the selection go ahead. A trash that needs more implements admin.Trash itself, with admin.EachTrashItem for its Restore and Purge.

Set the trash as Trash on an admin.Section of your own, or as editor.Config.Trash to list the records next to the deleted items of the editor's store. admin.JoinTrash combines several. Admin.TrashURL(section), such as routes.Admin().TrashURL(env.Key), links to the section's part of the trash, for a link on its overview. See ../modules/submissions/trash.go and ../modules/forms/trash.go. Seeing a section's trash needs admin.View; restoring and deleting for good need admin.Delete. In screens of your own, Admin.Form asks "Move this item to the trash?" before a form is sent to a route named delete or with a name ending in -delete, such as mailing-delete, and "Take this off the website?" before one is sent to a route named unpublish or with a name ending in -unpublish, as the toasts of Admin.Redirect follow the route name; Admin.Confirm sets another question, for example for a delete that cannot be undone.

A unique value, such as a slug or an e-mail address, must ignore deleted rows. Otherwise an item in the trash keeps other items from using it. Use a partial index on SQLite and PostgreSQL and a generated column on MySQL; see Databases. A content store's Undelete fails with an error that wraps content.ErrDuplicateSlug, for errors.Is, when another item took the item's slug or unique value meanwhile; the item then stays in the trash. For records of your own, SoftTable.Undelete then fails with an error that db.IsUnique recognises, unless a check refuses first with an error of the module's own. content.UniqueSlug(slug, taken) gives a new item a free slug, such as team-2.

Previews and review

Both are for content in a content.Revisions; the links module, a collection, has neither.

Editors preview a revision at its own address on the website, with ?revision=<id> (frontend.PreviewParam) added. The editor's preview button goes to the address that editor.Config.PreviewURL returns. ModulePreviewURL makes it below the instance's page, or returns "" while the instance is on no page:

PreviewURL: func(ctx context.Context, item Item, locale string) string {
    text, _ := item.Text(locale)

    return env.Frontend.ModulePreviewURL(ctx, env.Key, locale, "/"+text.Slug, item.Revision.ID)
},

The public handler then shows that revision instead of the published item. frontend.PreviewRevision returns the revision a request asks for when a signed-in editor who may view the admin section at the given address, such as its index, sends it, and "" otherwise. PreviewBySlug returns that revision when it belongs to the content at the slug, also when it was never published, and what PublishedBySlug returns otherwise. frontend.RevisionOf as Content.Revision marks the page as a preview: the layout's .Preview and .Revision are set, for a banner, and the page stays out of caches and search engines. A handler for posts at /{slug}, kept in a content.Revisions as s.posts, with env.AdminURL kept as s.adminURL:

func (s *Service) postPage(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()
    mount := frontend.MountFrom(ctx)
    preview := frontend.PreviewRevision(r, s.adminURL(admin.RouteName(s.key, "index")))

    item, err := s.posts.PreviewBySlug(ctx, s.key, mount.Locale, r.PathValue("slug"), preview)
    if err != nil {
        s.frontend.Fail(w, r, err)

        return
    }

    text, _ := item.Text(mount.Locale)

    s.frontend.Render(w, r, frontend.Content{
        Template: "post",
        Title:    text.Title,
        Data:     text,
        EditURL:  s.adminURL(admin.RouteName(s.key, "edit"), "id", item.ID),
        Revision: frontend.RevisionOf(r, item, preview),
    })
}

../modules/publishing/module.go previews posts this way.

A site can require a review before publishing, per instance in Site settings › Review; it is off by default. See Editing. Editor sections of a content.Revisions store get the workflow on their own: the buttons to submit, approve and reject, the Review right in the permission matrix, an e-mail to the reviewers when the site sends mail, and the revisions waiting for review under Needs attention on the dashboard, through Section.Review. The setting names the instance key, so the editor section's ID must be env.Key. While review is on, the store refuses, with content.ErrNotApproved, to publish or schedule a revision that is not approved, and the editor tells why. Only the admin and the scheduler apply the setting (content.WithReview), so imports and seeds publish as before. A store of your own that wraps a content.Revisions gets the workflow by implementing content.Reviewing, for example with Revisions.Reviews(key).

Guides.Title: Visitor actions and forms of a module
Guides.Summary: Visitor actions are the forms visitors post to and the links they follow. This guide adds a form for link suggestions to the links module of Writing a module: the action that receives it, the form a theme shows, how the post is checked and kept, and how the form's texts reach the site's translations. Visitor forms explains these forms as a site sees them.
Guides.Body:
Visitor actions

env.Actions() returns the go-router of the instance's visitor actions: the forms visitors post to and the links they follow, from any page. The site serves it at /_/<key>/, so its routes are relative to that; posts from other websites are refused, and so are bodies over 1 MiB unless Parts.ActionBodyLimit allows more. Every call returns the same router, so the service can keep it, here as s.actions. frontend.Limits adds the module's own limits as middleware, always in the same order: first the size of the body, then the posts per visitor. A visitor over the limit returns to the form with ?<key>=throttled (frontend.ResultThrottled), or gets ActionLimits.Throttled. A Posts or Window of zero does not throttle, and a Body of zero keeps the site's limit. Actions for link suggestions at /_/partners/suggest, with bodies up to 64 KiB and at most 5 posts per visitor in 10 minutes:

// SuggestionInput is the form a visitor posts to /_/<key>/suggest.
type SuggestionInput struct {
    URL string `form:"input,url" name:"url" label:"Address" required:"true" maxLength:"2000" url:"https" line:"true"`
}

// registerActions registers the instance's actions on its action router.
func (s *Service) registerActions() {
    s.actions.Use(frontend.Limits(s.key, frontend.ActionLimits{
        Body:   64 << 10,
        Posts:  5,
        Window: 10 * time.Minute,
    }))
    s.actions.Post("/suggest", s.suggest).As("suggest")
}

func (s *Service) suggest(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // Bots that fill in the honeypot get the answer a person would get.
    if frontend.IsSpam(r) {
        frontend.Back(w, r, s.key, "sent")

        return
    }

    var in SuggestionInput

    errs, err := s.frontend.BindForm(r, &in)
    if err != nil || len(errs) > 0 {
        s.frontend.KeepForm(w, r, s.key, in, errs)
        frontend.Back(w, r, s.key, "invalid")

        return
    }

    slog.InfoContext(r.Context(), "link suggested", "module", s.key, "url", in.URL)
    frontend.Back(w, r, s.key, "sent")
}

The Service keeps the router in a field actions *router.Router: Setup sets it with actions: env.Actions() and calls service.registerActions() before it returns.

Body can only lower the site's limit; for a larger body, such as an upload, raise Parts.ActionBodyLimit. Use comes before the routes and limits all of them; s.actions.Post(pattern, handler).Use(...) limits one route, as ../modules/newsletter/module.go limits its signups only. The routes become part of the site's routes: handlers see the whole path, such as /_/partners/suggest, and r.PathValue reads a parameter. The site puts the key in front of an action route's name, so a module that runs more than once names its routes alike: the route named suggest is <key>.suggest for the site, such as partners.suggest, and suggest for the action router itself. s.actions.RoutePath("suggest") returns its address, /_/partners/suggest, and s.actions.RoutePathArgs(name, args...) fills in parameters. Both work without a request, such as for a link in an e-mail, and env.Frontend.Route("partners.suggest") returns the same. An Env made without an app, as in a test, gives the same addresses, with a new router on every call: webthings.Env{Key: "partners"}.Actions(). A request without a route gets a plain 404, or 405 for a path that has routes for other methods. frontend.Actions(key, handler, limits) adds the same limits to a single handler.

A screen or component shows the form as a go-form model, as the bundled modules' views do in a field Form of type form.RenderModel. frontend.VisitorForm(ctx, SuggestionInput{}, s.actions.RoutePath("suggest"), s.key) makes one that posts to the action, with the honeypot (frontend.Honeypot) and a hidden field back: the page being shown, followed by # and the key. A theme renders it with {{form_open .Form}}, a field by its name with {{form_field .Form "url" nil}}, with its label and its limits, such as maxlength, in the page's language, and {{form_close}}. A template that writes the form tag itself adds the hidden fields with {{form_hidden .Form}}. See Template functions. The key also goes before the ids of the fields, so the forms of two instances on one page keep ids of their own: the url field of partners has the id partners-url.

Back returns the visitor to the form's page with ?partners=sent, at the element whose id is the key, so a theme puts the form and its result in an element with that id. BackWith adds more values to the query. When the post names no page on the site, as one over the body limit, which cannot be read, both return to the Referer when that is an address on the host the post was sent to, and to the home page otherwise. A template function reads the result with frontend.Result(frontend.Request(ctx), key, allowed...), which returns only one of the allowed results, so a made-up address shows none. In the handler, frontend.BackPath(r) is the path of the form's page, found the same way, and env.Frontend.BackLocale(r) its language, for example to store a message in the visitor's language.

Check every value a visitor sends. env.Frontend.BindForm, here s.frontend.BindForm, maps the post onto the input's struct and checks the struct's go-form tags: required, maxLength in characters, url and the others, line:"true" for a single line, such as a name or a subject: valid UTF-8 without tabs, line breaks or other control characters, and validate:"mail" for an e-mail address that mail will go to (mail.Rule; see E-mail). It trims the text and reads line breaks as \n, as browsers count them for maxlength, and reads a datetime-local field in the site's timezone, in which the form shows it. A value it cannot read as its field's type, such as "abc" for a number, comes back as an error with the rule invalid; the other errors carry the rule they broke (form.FieldValidationError.Rule), for a result per rule. err is set only when the post cannot be mapped at all. The messages are in the language of the page the form was on (BackLocale). It is go-form's Bind, so an input that implements form.Overrider, with limits that change at runtime, such as the places left, is checked against those. A form that is not a struct but a go-form form.Schema, such as one editors put together, is checked with env.Frontend.ValidateSchema(r, schema, values), with the messages in the language of the page being served; ../modules/forms/public.go receives its form on its page this way, to show it again with the errors.

s.frontend.KeepForm(w, r, s.key, in, errs) before Back keeps a post with mistakes for the form's page. There the form that VisitorForm makes for the same key and action shows the visitor's values again, with the messages at their fields, without a change to the templates. The post waits on the server for five minutes at most, with only a token in a cookie for that page, and shows once; see Visitor forms. Show such a form with the page or in a fragment placed with slot or requiredSlot, not deferredSlot, whose later request comes after the page took the post. The bundled comments, newsletter, registrations and submissions modules keep their posts this way; ../modules/comments/actions.go also keeps a post its service refuses, with nil errors, so it shows the values alone.

A post that fails for another reason, such as a database that cannot store it, answers with s.frontend.Fail(w, r, err), as the bundled modules' actions do: the error is logged with the module's key and the path, and the visitor gets the theme's 500.gohtml in the language of the form's page, rendered as the theme's pages are, with its asset versions, as with Fail in The public handler. An HTMX post gets that page too, which the client shows as the whole page with reloadOnError; see HTMX.

List the inputs in Module.Forms, such as Forms: []any{SuggestionInput{}}: when a theme or a module's default template renders forms with form_open, form_field or form_render, the starter's task translations adds their labels, descriptions, placeholders, option labels, submit texts and messages to translations/translations.pot, referenced as module:<type>/forms. The texts of the module's default templates, components and mail come with them, as module:<type>/<name>.gohtml and module:<type>/mail/<name>.gohtml, unless every theme replaces the file. App.TranslationCatalog() returns all these texts as a go-translator *extract.Catalog, also in a test, without Start; see Languages.

env.VisitorID(ctx, r, parts...) identifies a visitor without storing their address, for example per day with the date as a part. env.Frontend.SendMail(ctx, env.Mail, frontend.Letter{...}) writes a mail template and sends it, also when the visitor leaves the page, and logs a failure; send it after the post is stored. See Visitor forms and E-mail.

Guides.Title: Feeds, structured data, API and links of a module
Guides.Summary: This guide continues the links module of Writing a module beyond its pages: Atom and RSS feeds of its content, structured data for search engines, endpoints in the content API, and the links in its content to the site's pages, which the admin keeps track of.
Guides.Body:
Feeds

A module offers Atom and RSS feeds of its content with Parts.Feeds, a list of frontend.Feed.
