Each feed has a Name, "feed" by default, a Path below the instance's page without the extension, "/feed" by default, an optional Page, explained below, and Build, a frontend.FeedFunc that returns the feed for a request. Setup in Module and Setup adds the links module's feed, its newest links at /en/partners/feed.atom and /en/partners/feed.rss, with Feeds: service.feeds():

// feeds are the instance's feeds below its page: its newest links at
// feed.atom and feed.rss.
func (s *Service) feeds() []frontend.Feed {
    return []frontend.Feed{{Build: s.feed}}
}

// feed is the newest published links in the page's language.
func (s *Service) feed(r *http.Request, limit int) (feed.Feed, error) {
    ctx := r.Context()
    locale := frontend.MountFrom(ctx).Locale

    items, err := s.items.ListPublished(ctx, s.key, locale)
    if err != nil {
        return feed.Feed{}, err
    }

    slices.SortStableFunc(items, func(a, b Item) int {
        return b.CreatedAt.Compare(a.CreatedAt)
    })

    var built feed.Feed

    for _, item := range items[:min(limit, len(items))] {
        text, _ := item.Text(locale)

        built.Entries = append(built.Entries, feed.Entry{
            ID:        s.frontend.TagURI(r, item.CreatedAt, s.key+"/"+item.ID),
            Title:     text.Title,
            Link:      item.Fields.URL,
            Summary:   text.Description,
            Published: item.CreatedAt,
            Updated:   item.UpdatedAt,
        })
    }

    return built, nil
}

The app registers each feed on the instance's Public router, which must then be a Frontend.Router, as two routes: <Name>.atom at <Path>.atom below the page and <Name>.rss at <Path>.rss, here feed.atom and feed.rss. Links to a feed come from its route names, as those to the module's other routes: routes.For(r).RoutePath("feed.atom") in a handler is /en/partners/feed.atom, and paths("feed.atom") of The public handler builds it outside a request. Build runs as the router's handlers do: frontend.MountFrom(r.Context()) gives the page and its language, and r.PathValue the wildcards of the feed's Path. An instance on no page has no feeds; their addresses get the 404 page.

A Path with wildcards gives a feed per item of a route, such as Publishing's feed per category: {Name: "category-feed", Path: "/category/{slug}/feed", Page: "category", Build: s.feed} is at /en/news/category/<slug>/feed.atom and .rss, and routes.For(r).RoutePathArgs("category-feed.atom", "slug", slug) builds its address. Page names the route whose pages link to the feed, here the list of a category at /category/{slug}, and the feed's wildcards are filled in with those of that page, so a Path with wildcards needs a Page. A feed without one is linked from every page of the instance. The last segment of a Path is a name, never a wildcard. Start fails for a feed the app cannot serve: one without Build, a Path that does not start with a slash or that ends in a wildcard, wildcards without a Page, a Page the router has no route for, or a route name or path the router has already.

limit is how many entries the feed lists: the feed's Limit, or, while that is zero, the site setting Items in feeds in Site settings › General (site.Settings.FeedLimit: 20 by default, at most 100). Limit gives a feed a size of its own, such as from an option of the module: Publishing's publishing.WithFeedSize(n) sets it on the feeds of an instance, its category feeds included, and Events' events.WithFeedSize(n) on its feed. Start fails for a Limit below zero or above site.MaxFeedSize (100). Give the entries in the order readers should see them, usually the newest first; the app leaves out those beyond the limit. It also fills in what the feed leaves empty: Title is the page's title, Link the instance's page, ID the absolute address of the feed's Atom document, Language the page's language, Author the site's name, or else its organisation, and Subtitle the site's tagline; a feed without entries gets the time of the page's published revision as Updated. It sets Self to the address of the format served, makes the links and image addresses that are paths on the site absolute, such as an entry's Link from routes.For(r), and gives an image without a Type the one of its extension. Readers see the title with the site's name, such as "Partners from My site", translated with the site's translations as %[1]s from %[2]s; a title that is the site's name stays as it is. An error from Build that wraps db.ErrNotFound, such as for a category that does not exist, gets the site's 404 page. Other errors, and a feed that is still not valid, are logged and get the error page, as with Fail.

Each entry needs an absolute ID, a Title, a Published or Updated time and a Link or Content. Frontend.TagURI(r, date, specific) makes an ID that stays the same when the entry's address changes: a tag: URI such as tag:example.com,2026-10-07:partners/<ID>, on the host of Config.BaseURL, or else of the request, without its port. date is a day the site had that host, such as when the item was created, and specific tells the item apart from everything else the site named that day, such as the key and the item's ID. Set BaseURL in production, so the IDs do not change with the address a reader used. Content is HTML with absolute addresses, as readers show it away from the site: Frontend.AbsoluteMarkdown(r, source) renders editor content as Markdown does, in the page's language, but with every address on the site absolute and images as e-mail shows them (MailImage). Relative links lead from the feed's own address, as a reader resolves them. Publishing and Events give their text this way, with their image as Image, an enclosure; see ../modules/publishing/feed.go and ../modules/events/feed.go.

Frontend.MarkdownOptions(ctx, locale, base, mail) gives the markdown.Options the site renders editor content with, for markdown.Render and markdown.PlainMedia in your own code: links to media give the file, and an image without a description in the Markdown gets its alternative text in locale from the media library. base is Options.Base, such as https://example.com/en/, or "" for the site's own pages (see Media and images). Without mail, images are shown as a page shows them (Image), with a srcset; with mail, as e-mail shows them (MailImage), one copy with its size. AbsoluteMarkdown renders with mail and the feed's address as base, and the newsletter its mailings with mail and the home page of the mailing's language as base; see ../modules/newsletter/sending.go.

{{feedLinks}}, which core's head tags have, writes a <link rel="alternate"> in the page's <head> for each format of each feed of the page shown, with absolute addresses, so browsers and feed readers find them; see Themes. An error page gets none, also the 404 that NotFound or Fail renders for an address below the module's page. {{feedURL "atom"}} gives the address of the page's feed for a visible link, and Frontend.FeedURL(r, format, name...) the same in Go; see feedURL. Feeds are pages of the site for caching: the output cache keeps them for visitors and renders them again after the same changes as the pages (see The output cache), and they get an ETag, the site's Cache-Control for pages (Site settings › Performance) and a Last-Modified that never goes back: when the app first served the feed as it is now, or the feed's own time when that is later (feed.Feed.LastModified: Updated, or else the newest time of an entry). Unpublishing the newest item therefore moves it forward too. A reader that sends the ETag in If-None-Match, or only If-Modified-Since, gets 304 Not Modified while the feed is unchanged, and the whole feed after a change. Each process of the app keeps these times itself, so after a restart, or from another process, a reader that asks by the date gets the whole feed once more; see Deployment. A time the clock has not reached yet is not sent, such as an Updated in the future. Feeds are never in sitemap.xml. Pages send no Last-Modified. A handler of the module that sets one itself gets the same 304 Not Modified by it, from go-router's middleware.LastModified and the output cache, so it must never go back.

Package feed writes the documents from one model, a feed.Feed with its feed.Entry values: Atom 1.0 with feed.Atom.Write(w, f) and RSS 2.0 with feed.RSS.Write(w, f). Both call Validate first, which checks what both formats require, and write nothing for a feed that misses it: the error wraps feed.ErrInvalid and names each problem. The app writes a module's feeds itself. The package uses the standard library only.

Structured data

Search engines read what a page is about from its structured data: schema.org items in JSON-LD, which core's head tags write in the page's <head> with {{structuredData}}; see Search and SEO. Core describes the site, its organisation, the page and its place in the page tree. A module describes the content its page shows with frontend.Content.StructuredData, a []frontend.Thing. The first item is the page's main entity: core gives it a mainEntityOfPage with the page's canonical address, unless it has one.

A frontend.Thing is a map[string]any: the item's "@type" and its properties, as encoding/json writes them. Empty values, such as "", nil, a zero time.Time and empty lists, are left out, so a module can name every property without checking for content first; an item with nothing but its type is left out altogether. Addresses may be paths in the properties that hold them, @id, url, image, logo, item, sameAs, contentUrl, thumbnailUrl and urlTemplate: they are made absolute, on Config.BaseURL or the request's address. Give dates as text, in the content's own timezone, such as "2026-10-07" or "2026-10-07T19:30:00+02:00". An item refers to the site's organisation, which core describes from the site settings, with frontend.Thing{"@id": frontend.OrganizationID}. env.Frontend.SocialImageURL(ctx, ref) is the image shown when a page is shared, a 1200 × 630 JPEG cut around the focal point, of an asset ID or a media URL, for an item's image.

With the posts of Previews and review as PostItem values, a content.Item whose fields have a Date and an Image and whose text an Excerpt, a post's page describes the post as an article by the site's organisation, as the posts name no author:

// article is the structured data of a post's page: an Article in locale,
// published on the post's date by the site's organisation.
func (s *Service) article(ctx context.Context, item PostItem, locale string) frontend.Thing {
    text, _ := item.Text(locale)
    organization := frontend.Thing{"@id": frontend.OrganizationID}

    return frontend.Thing{
        "@type":         "Article",
        "headline":      text.Title,
        "description":   text.Excerpt,
        "image":         s.frontend.SocialImageURL(ctx, item.Fields.Image),
        "datePublished": item.Fields.Date.Format(time.DateOnly),
        "dateModified":  item.Revision.CreatedAt.Format(time.RFC3339),
        "inLanguage":    locale,
        "author":        organization,
        "publisher":     organization,
    }
}

The post's page gives it with its content: StructuredData: []frontend.Thing{s.article(ctx, item, mount.Locale)} in the frontend.Content of postPage. Pages that are not found or fail have no structured data: the 404 page and the theme's error page, 500.gohtml, write none, whether Fail answered with it or a template failed. A page that lists items with pages of their own, such as a list of posts, gives frontend.ItemList(name, urls...): an ItemList named name of the items' addresses, in the order the page shows them. Empty addresses are left out, and without any it returns nil, which adds nothing. ../modules/publishing/structured.go builds a post's Article this way, and ../modules/events/structured.go an event's Event.

A module that adds to the pages of other modules, or changes their items, sets Parts.StructuredData to a frontend.StructuredDataFunc, func(ctx, view, items) []frontend.Thing. It runs for every page that has structured data, in the order of the modules, with the page's frontend.View and the items of the page's module and of the functions before it, and returns them with its own. view.Module is the key of the instance whose screen the page is, and view.Content its data, such as an events.Event. The items are the other module's, so change one in a copy, such as with maps.Clone. The registrations module gives an event its offers this way; see ../modules/registrations/structured.go.

The content API

While the site's content API is on (Config.API), a module can serve its published content as JSON below /api/v1/<key>/, such as Publishing's posts at /api/v1/news/posts. Parts.API is a go-router of api.NewRouter(). The app mounts it at /api/v1/<key> when it starts, and leaves it out while the API is off. Its routes are relative to that address, and their names get api.<key>. in front for the app's other routers. A request without a route, any path or method, gets the API's 404 not_found as JSON. The links module's endpoints, its published links in their order and one link by its ID:

// APILink is a published link in the content API.
type APILink struct {
    ID          string `json:"id"`
    Title       string `json:"title"`
    Description string `json:"description"`
    URL         string `json:"url"`
    APIURL      string `json:"api_url"`
}

// apiRoutes are the instance's endpoints below /api/v1/<key>.
func (s *Service) apiRoutes() *router.Router {
    routes := api.NewRouter()

    routes.Get("/links", s.apiLinks).As("links")
    routes.Get("/links/{id}", s.apiLink).As("link")

    return routes
}

// apiLinks answers /links: a page of the published links.
func (s *Service) apiLinks(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    links, err := s.Links(r.Context(), api.Locale(r))
    if err != nil {
        api.Fail(w, r, err)

        return
    }

    items := make([]APILink, 0, len(links))

    for _, link := range links {
        items = append(items, s.apiItem(r, link))
    }

    api.Write(w, r, api.Paginate(r, items))
}

// apiLink answers /links/{id}: a published link in the request's language.
func (s *Service) apiLink(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    locale := api.Locale(r)

    item, err := s.items.Published(r.Context(), s.key, r.PathValue("id"), locale)
    if errors.Is(err, content.ErrNotFound) {
        api.NotFound(w, r)

        return
    }

    if err != nil {
        api.Fail(w, r, err)

        return
    }

    text, _ := item.Text(locale)
    link := Link{ID: item.ID, Title: text.Title, Description: text.Description, URL: item.Fields.URL}

    api.Modified(w, item.UpdatedAt)
    api.Write(w, r, s.apiItem(r, link))
}

// apiItem is a link in the content API, with its own address there.
func (s *Service) apiItem(r *http.Request, link Link) APILink {
    self, _ := s.api.RoutePathArgs("link", "id", link.ID)

    return APILink{
        ID:          link.ID,
        Title:       link.Title,
        Description: link.Description,
        URL:         link.URL,
        APIURL:      api.URL(r, self+"?"+url.Values{"locale": {api.Locale(r)}}.Encode()),
    }
}

The Service keeps the router in a field api *router.Router: Setup sets it with service.api = service.apiRoutes() and returns it with API: service.api. With the instance partners, /api/v1/partners/links lists the links, and s.api.RoutePathArgs("link", "id", id) is /api/v1/partners/links/<id>, as is app.Frontend.Route("api.partners.link", "id", id) for the site's own code. The site lists the instances with endpoints at /api/v1/site, each with its api_base, such as https://example.com/api/v1/partners.

Package api answers as the core endpoints do; see Content API:

  • api.Locale(r) is the language of the request: its locale parameter, or the site's default language. A language the site does not offer is answered with 404 unknown_locale before the handler runs.
  • api.URL(r, path) makes an address of the site absolute, on Config.BaseURL or the request's address. Links to the instance's pages come from pages.Links(s.public, base), as in The public handler; they are empty while the instance is on no page, and api.Optional makes such a value null.
  • api.HTML(r, source) renders editor content, which is Markdown, as HTML for readers away from the site, for a body_html field: in the request's language, with every address of the site absolute and images with their srcset, size and alt text. Relative links lead from the home page of that language, such as https://example.com/en/.
  • api.ImageOf(r, id) is an image of the media library as an *api.Image, with its address, srcset, size, alt text and original, all absolute; nil, which is null, without one.
  • api.Paginate(r, items) is the page of a list that the request asks for with limit and offset, as an api.List, with the address of the next page in next.
  • api.Modified(w, dates...) gives the answer for one item a Last-Modified, the latest of the dates of everything it shows, so a client that asks with If-Modified-Since gets 304 Not Modified while none of them changed; call it before api.Write. A zero date, of something whose date is unknown, such as a category that was deleted, sends none, and so does a date ahead of the clock. api.MountModified(r, key) is the date of the page the instance is on and of the pages above it, which the item's url holds, zero while the instance is on no page, and api.MediaModified(r, source, ids...) that of the media in a Markdown text and of images by their ID, such as a featured image. api.ItemDates(r, key, item, source, ids...) gives these dates for one item of a content store: its last change, the revision it shows for content with revisions, the instance's page (MountModified) and the media of source and ids (MediaModified). Add the dates of anything else the answer shows: api.Modified(w, api.ItemDates(r, s.key, item, text.Body, item.Fields.Image)...). The gallery, lists, people and testimonials date an item this way, and ../modules/publishing/api.go adds a post's categories. A link of the guide shows neither its page nor media, so apiLink above passes item.UpdatedAt alone. Give lists none: an item that leaves a list leaves no newer date behind. An item whose answer counts other items gets none either, such as a directory entry or a document, whose category holds the number of its published items. See Caching.
  • api.Write(w, r, v) answers with v as JSON. api.NotFound(w, r) answers 404 not_found, api.Fail(w, r, err) logs the error and answers 500 internal_error, and api.Error(w, r, status, code) answers another error.

Name the fields in snake_case and give times as time.Time, which JSON writes in RFC 3339. Show only what visitors see on the site: published content, as ListPublished and Published return it, never drafts or previews, and no personal data, such as visitors' entries. Every answer is then the same for everyone, and the output cache keeps it as it keeps pages; env.Changed, through the store's Changed, renders it again after a change. The API's rate limit and CORS apply to the module's endpoints too. ../modules/publishing/api.go and ../modules/events/api.go serve posts, categories and events this way. A test turns the API on with sitetest.Options.Configure, setting config.API to api.Config{Enabled: true}.

Links to pages

The admin knows which published content links to which page. The editor of a published page lists that content and asks before the page leaves its address, and Pages › Broken links lists the links that lead to no page; see Editing. The app reads the text of the published pages itself. A module reports the links in its published content with Parts.Links, a links.Func: func(ctx, locale) ([]links.Source, error), which lists what visitors can see in locale, never drafts, with a links.Source per item:

Field
ID, Title The item, as editors know it.
URL The item's own address on the site, such as /en/news/hello. Its relative links lead from there, as a browser follows them; empty, they lead from the home page of locale, as for a banner, which has no address of its own.
EditURL The item's editor, which the editors of pages and items and the report link to: env.AdminURL(admin.RouteName(env.Key, "edit"), "id", id, url.Values{"locale": {locale}}).
Markdown Texts in Markdown, such as a body. Their links count, images do not (markdown.Links).
Addresses Link fields, such as the address of a button.
Revision The revision Markdown comes from, for a content.Revisions: the links found in it are kept with the revision, as those of pages are, and not looked for again. Empty finds them again for every index.

Only links to an address on the site count: a path, a relative link or a full URL on the host of Config.BaseURL; without BaseURL, no full URL counts. Links to other websites, mailto: and tel: links, media files (media:) and the addresses core serves itself (env.IsCorePath) are left out, and the query and the fragment are dropped. A link below a module page counts as found, since the module answers there. With env.Pages kept as s.pages and env.AdminURL as s.adminURL, as in The public handler and Previews and review, the links module reports the address of each link, which counts when it leads to the site itself:

// linkSources lists the published links in locale for the admin: an
// address counts when it leads to a page of the site.
func (s *Service) linkSources(ctx context.Context, locale string) ([]links.Source, error) {
    base, err := s.pages.MountURL(ctx, s.key, locale)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    items, err := s.items.ListPublished(ctx, s.key, locale)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    sources := make([]links.Source, 0, len(items))

    for _, item := range items {
        text, _ := item.Text(locale)

        sources = append(sources, links.Source{
            ID:        item.ID,
            Title:     text.Title,
            URL:       base,
            EditURL:   s.adminURL(admin.RouteName(s.key, "edit"), "id", item.ID, url.Values{"locale": {locale}}),
            Addresses: []string{item.Fields.URL},
        })
    }

    return sources, nil
}

Setup returns it with Links: service.linkSources. links.Source is of go-webthings' package links: the example's package has the same name, and Go lets it import that package as it is. The app calls these functions only to make its index of links, for the editor of a published page or item and for the report, never for a visitor's request. It keeps the index until what visitors see changes on this server, as for the output cache, or until Config.CacheTTL has passed, so changes on other servers show too. A function that fails is logged, and the links of the other modules still count. ../modules/publishing/links.go reports posts with their revision and ../modules/banners/links.go the address of a banner's button.

A module that redirects old addresses, as the redirects module does, sets Parts.Redirects to a links.Redirector: Redirected(ctx, address) returns where a redirect sends the visitors of an address on the site, such as /en/about, and Redirect(ctx, address, target) sends them to target with a permanent redirect from now on. The admin then offers redirects in the editors of pages and items and in the report to users with the create right in the section whose ID is the instance's key. The first module that sets it is used.

The page editor shows its notices through editor.Config.Edit, which every editor section can set. It runs when the edit screen of an existing item is built, before it renders, with the request, the Editor, the item, the language and the *editor.EditView. It may add Notices, shown above the form: each an editor.Notice with a Text, Items, which are editor.NoticeItem values with a Label, an optional URL and a Note shown muted after it, and Forms. It may also change or replace the view's forms, such as with a question before Unpublish (Admin.Confirm) or with a form that posts to a route of the module's own in Routes. Texts are shown as written, so translate them first, such as with admin.T. An error from Edit answers the request with status 500. A route of the module's own explains a refused change with e.Issue(r, err), the translated message the editor shows for an error: that of Config.Issue, or the editor's own for the errors of package content, or "" for an unexpected error. It checks a change that takes the item off the website with e.RefusePermanent(w, r) first; see Deleting and the trash.

The editor of items with an address of their own, such as posts, gets the same notices and redirects as a page's editor from editor.Linked; see Links to an item. Its Check is the site's link check, which env.Links() returns, and its Address returns where visitors find an item on the site in a language once it is published, for any revision of it: "" when it has none there, such as while the instance is on no page. Linked asks it only for the languages in which the item is complete (content.Spec.Available). With the posts of Previews and review at routes.Get("/{slug}", s.postPage).As("post") and the paths method of The public handler:

// postAddress is the address of a post, in any revision, on the site in
// locale, such as /en/partners/hello; "" while the instance is on no page.
func (s *Service) postAddress(ctx context.Context, item PostItem, locale string) (string, error) {
    paths, err := s.paths(ctx, locale)
    if err != nil {
        return "", err
    }

    text, _ := item.Text(locale)

    // A post without a slug in locale has no address there.
    address, _ := paths("post", "slug", text.Slug)

    return address, nil
}

The methods of Linked are hooks of the editor.Config of the posts, whose form for one language is a postInput:

linked := editor.Linked[PostFields, PostText, postInput]{Check: env.Links(), Address: service.postAddress}

posts := editor.New(editor.Config[PostFields, PostText, postInput]{
    // ID, Store, Form, Apply and the rest, as for the links.
    Edit:   linked.Edit,
    Routes: linked.Routes,
    Saved:  linked.Saved,
})
  • Edit lists the published content that links to the item's address and asks before the item is unpublished or moved to the trash. Users who may unpublish it and add redirects (editor.Redirector) also get Unpublish and redirect. For a content.Revisions, it shows how publishing the revision changes the address. The publish form then redirects the old addresses for users who may add redirects, and asks first for other users while content links to the old address.
  • Routes adds the routes these forms post to: unpublish-redirect, and revision-publish-moved for a content.Revisions, both with admin.Publish. A user without the create right in the redirects module gets status 403 from the first; the second then publishes without redirects.
  • Saved redirects the old addresses of a published item of a content.Collection to its new ones when it is saved with other addresses, such as a new slug, and the user may add redirects.

Below, when set, returns the addresses below the item's address in a language that go offline with the item, such as the entries of a directory's category: func(ctx, item, locale) ([]string, error), asked only for the languages in which the item is complete. Edit then counts the links to them apart from those to the item itself, as "1 published item links to an address below this item.", and asks "Published items link to addresses below this item. Unpublish it anyway?" while only such links exist. Unpublish and redirect redirects them too, to the same page. Saved gives only the item's own address a redirect, so a module whose addresses below the item keep working under its new slug sends them on itself, as the directory does for an entry whose category was renamed. Without Below, links below the item's address count as links to the item. ../modules/directory/module.go sets Below: service.entryAddresses.

editor.Config.Saved runs after an existing item is saved, with the request, the Editor, the item before and after the save and the language. It may act on the change and returns the toast, a *flash.Message of go-partial's flash package, or nil for the editor's own: "Changes saved." for a content.Collection and "Saved as a draft. Publish it to show it on the website." for a content.Revisions. A module with hooks of its own calls the methods of Linked from them, as ../modules/gallery/module.go does with Routes. ../modules/publishing/links.go gives the addresses of a post and of a category, whose editor uses Linked too, and ../modules/directory/links.go those of an entry, below its category, and of a category.

Screens of a module's own use the same parts. editor.Redirector(r, admin, check) returns the module that redirects when the user may add redirects to it, and nil otherwise. env.Links().Table(ctx) returns the published page table, from which editor.RedirectTargets(table, locale, leaving, selected) lists the pages to redirect to, for the Target of an editor.RedirectInput: without the page leaving and the pages below it, unless it is empty, and with selected chosen. editor.MovedInput is the publish form with the box Redirect the old addresses to the new ones, and editor.PublishLinked the question before a revision is published that leaves an address published content links to. editor.LinkItems lists the content that links, from Index.To, as notice items linked to its editor, and editor.LinkItem names one. editor.RedirectedNotice is the toast after a change, which says how many old addresses redirect now.

Guides.Title: Caching and testing a module
Guides.Summary: This guide continues the links module of Writing a module. It explains how the site's output cache keeps the pages a module renders and learns of its changes, and how to test a module with a whole site, on the databases and for the admin's translations.
Guides.Body:
The output cache

The site keeps the pages it renders for visitors in memory and serves them again without rendering them, for 60 seconds and up to 32 MB unless Site settings › Performance or Config.OutputCacheTTL says otherwise; Config.Development and Config.ReloadTemplates turn it off unless OutputCacheTTL is set. See Deployment. A module's public handler, template functions and components therefore do not run for every view of a page. The cache keeps a whole page and an HTMX navigation of the same address side by side, up to four lists of request headers that the answers of one address vary on (go-router's CacheOptions.MaxVarySets), and many requests at once for a page it does not have render it once per variant. /metrics shows its hits, misses, skips, evictions, entries and bytes to requests with Config.MetricsToken; see Deployment.

Changes made by the site's own process show at once. The app renders the pages again after every successful post to a module's admin sections or to the trash, and after scheduled publication. A visitor's post to the visitor actions below /_/ or to a page counts only when it succeeded, with a status below 400, and did not say it changed nothing. Spam, a post with mistakes and a post over the throttle say so on their own: frontend.IsSpam when it reports true, KeepForm and the throttle over its limit call frontend.NothingChanged(r). A module calls it itself for its other answers that store nothing a page shows, as the bundled modules do: comments when they are closed, polls for every result but voted, submissions for a body it cannot read, registrations when sign-up is closed, and the newsletter for a signup and a one-click unsubscribe, since no page shows subscribers. A post counts as a change unless it says otherwise, so a module that forgets to mark a post that changed nothing only costs the pages a render, never a page that is out of date. The app gives every visitor's post the record that NothingChanged sets with frontend.TrackChanges(r), and reads it with frontend.Changed(r): true unless NothingChanged was called. A test of a handler does the same to check what it says; without TrackChanges, NothingChanged does nothing and Changed reports true.

Changes made from Go show at once too, when the module tells the app. A store whose content.Spec has Changed set to env.Changed in Setup, as in Module and Setup, tells it after every committed write that visitors see, also one made from Go, such as an import through Store(), a seed or a background job. For other writes, such as to a table of the module's own, the module calls env.Changed() after the commit. db.AfterCommit(ctx, fn) calls fn at once outside a transaction, and inside one (DB.Tx) after the outermost transaction commits; after a rollback it never calls it. db.AfterWrite(ctx, err, env.Changed) does the same when err is nil and returns err, for the last line of a write method, as the bundled services do. A call before the commit is too early: a page rendered in between is kept with the content before the write. App.Changed() does the same for the site's own code. A change the app is not told about, a change made by another process and what changes with time alone, such as an event that has passed, show once the pages' time in the cache has passed.

The cache leaves alone the requests of the admin, the visitor actions, the media library and the assets, requests with the editors' session cookie or a kept post (frontend.KeptFormCookie), previews and searches with a query. Those two are the only cookies that keep a request from the cache: a request with any other cookie, such as a site's analytics or a theme choice, gets the page the cache keeps for everyone, unless the cookie is registered as personal, as below. The admin's flash messages have a cookie of the admin's path, which site pages never get. The cache never keeps an answer with another status than 200, with Cache-Control: private or no-store, or that sets a cookie. A page that is the visitor's own altogether, such as a registration looked up by its code, says so with Cache-Control: private, no-store. A page that only shows a part differently to a visitor by a cookie of the module or of the site, such as the polls a visitor voted on, registers that cookie in Setup with env.PersonalCookie(name): the cache then keeps the page apart for every value of the cookie, also when the answer varies on the Cookie header, where other cookies, such as a site's analytics, count for nothing. The polls module registers its cookie, wt_poll, this way.

Testing

sitetest starts a whole site on SQLite in a test, in English and Dutch, signed in as administrator, and drives the admin like a browser:

func TestLinks(t *testing.T) {
    s := sitetest.StartWith(t,
        sitetest.Options{Templates: "testdata/templates"},
        links.Module("partners", "Partners"),
    )

    link := s.Submit(s.App.AdminURL("admin.partners.new", url.Values{"locale": {"en"}}), url.Values{
        "Title": {"The Go website"},
        "URL":   {"https://go.dev"},
    })
    s.Publish(link + "?locale=en")
    s.Mount("partners", "Partners", "partners")

    s.Expect("/en/partners", http.StatusOK, `<a href="https://go.dev">The Go website</a>`)
}

s.App.AdminURL(name, args...) builds admin addresses by route name, as env.AdminURL does, so a test does not depend on where the admin is. testdata/templates/links/list.gohtml is the screen for the test; sitetest brings the layout. With Options.StartingPoints, such as []string{"partners"}, the test uses the starting points that App.WriteTemplates generates for those instances instead, and needs no templates of its own. s.Mount returns the editor of the page it made, and s.MountIn(module, translations...) places a module on a page in several languages, each a sitetest.Translation with a locale, title and slug. s.DraftPage(title, draft, slug) gives the page titled title an unpublished English title and slug. sitetest.PNG(t, width, height) makes an image and s.Upload(name, data) adds it to the media library. s.PostFiles(formPage, action, values, files...) sends a form with a file input from its page, each file a sitetest.File, and returns the status and body, for an import. s.Visitor() is a browser that is not signed in, s.Send posts a visitor's form, s.Mail holds the e-mail the site sent and s.Mails(n) waits until it has sent n, for mail sent in the background, and sitetest.HasToast(body, level, text) checks an admin page's messages. Options.NoAccount starts a site without accounts, as a fresh install. Sites in tests have the output cache off, so a page shows a change made from Go at once, also one the app is not told about. Options.OutputCache keeps the cache on, as the site setting says, for a test of the cache, and Options.Configure can set Config.OutputCacheTTL itself. Sites in tests hash passwords at the cheapest cost, so they start quickly.

The dashboard's panels load after the page, so s.Get(s.App.AdminURL("admin.dashboard")) shows only their placeholders. s.Dashboard() returns the dashboard with its panels loaded, and s.Fragment(path, id) the part of a page with that ID, as HTMX asks for it. s.Request(req) sends a request of your own with the browser's cookies and returns the response unread, for a stream.

dbtest.Each(t, func(t *testing.T, database *db.DB) { … }) runs a test on SQLite, and on PostgreSQL and MySQL when WT_TEST_POSTGRES and WT_TEST_MYSQL hold a server's DSN. Apply media.Schema() before the module's schema there, since saving content records the media it uses; ../modules/testimonials/store_test.go shows how.

catalogtest.Complete(t, files, linkInput{}), of package sitetest/catalogtest, fails a test for every text of the section's forms that the admin's catalogues miss in one of the languages the admin comes with (catalogtest.Languages): the admin's own translations/<language>.po with the module's in files on top, as the admin loads them. An empty translation counts as missing, so a label added to a form cannot go untranslated. It skips English (en_US, catalogtest.Source), the language the texts are written in, since a text its catalogue lacks shows as written; it checks Dutch (nl_NL). A module therefore needs a translations/nl_NL.po, and a translations/en_US.po is optional. The bundled modules check their catalogues this way, such as ../modules/lists/catalogue_test.go.

Guides.Title: Another template engine
Guides.Summary: go-webthings renders the public site with Go templates, but another template engine can take over by implementing frontend.Renderer. This guide covers what a renderer receives, what it must do and what the site gives up.
Guides.Body:
The Renderer interface

A renderer turns a page's data into HTML. The interface is in frontend/view.go:

type Renderer interface {
    Render(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, name string, view View) error
    Has(name string) bool
}

The built-in Go templates are a renderer too: frontend.Templates in frontend/templates.go, one per theme.

Config.Renderer

Set Config.Renderer instead of Config.Templates. When both are set, the renderer is used.

app := webthings.New(webthings.Config{
    Name:     "My site",
    Renderer: engine,
    Assets:   os.DirFS("static"),
})

What a renderer receives

Render is called once per page with:

  • name, the template to render, without extension.
  • view, the whole frontend.View: what layout.gohtml gets, with the content template's data in view.Content. The renderer draws both the layout and the content.
  • r, the request. Its context carries the page being rendered, so frontend.Locale(ctx), frontend.Request(ctx) and frontend.Service(ctx, key) work, and so do the template functions (see Template functions).
name view.Content
page frontend.Page
404 frontend.NotFound
search frontend.SearchView
<key>/<name>, such as news/post The module's view, such as publishing.Post
<type>/<name>, such as publishing/post The same, when Has reports no <key>/<name>

Templates describes the View and each kind of content.

What a renderer must do

Has reports whether the site has a template. go-webthings asks it before every render and acts on the answer:

Has is false for Then
A module's <key>/<name> <type>/<name> is rendered instead
The screen to render The visitor gets status 500 with missing_template, and the log names the template
404 Visitors get a plain-text "404 page not found"
search /<locale>/search answers 404

When the site starts, Has also decides which module screens are reported as missing (see Templates).

Render writes the whole page and sets the Content-Type. Leave the status to go-webthings: the not-found page is sent with 404, and a module screen that sets a status with that status, whatever success status the renderer sets. view.Status is that status, such as 404 for 404; zero is 200 OK. An error status from the renderer, 400 or higher, is kept. When Render returns an error, go-webthings logs it and answers with status 500 and go-partial's plain error page (Frontend.Fail): its heading, "Internal Server Error", and its sentence, "Something went wrong. Please try again.", are in the page's language, with the site's translations, and so is its lang; for 404 it sends a plain not-found page instead. Render into a buffer first and write only when it worked, so an error leaves no half page.

With Config.Development the plain page shows the error in place of the sentence, in English; outside development it never shows the error. The detailed error page, with the template and the line, belongs to the built-in Go templates, and so does a theme's 500.gohtml (see Templates). A renderer that answers an error itself, with a detailed page while you develop or with an error page of its own, writes that page and returns an error that wraps render.ErrShown; go-webthings then logs the error and writes nothing more.

Escaping is the renderer's job. Fields of type template.HTML, such as a page's Body, are HTML already; everything else is text.

Template functions

frontend.TemplateFuncs(r.Context()) from frontend/context.go returns every template function: core's, the modules', go-translator's tl, tn, ctl and ctn with the site's translations from Config.Translations, importmap, importmap_nonce, importmap_url, importmap_script and importmap_style when Config.ImportMap or Config.Assets is set, your own from Config.Funcs, and localizer and locale for the page's language. go-partial's HTMX attribute functions, such as submitAttrs, belong to the built-in Go templates and are not among them. Functions that take a context.Context first come with the request's context filled in, as templates call them:

funcs := frontend.TemplateFuncs(r.Context())

date := funcs["date"].(func(time.Time, ...string) string)
posts := funcs["posts"].(func(string, int) []publishing.Post)

An engine that takes a map of Go functions can get the map as it is. Outside Render, TemplateFuncs returns nil.

funcs["feedLinks"], a func() template.HTML, writes the links to the feeds of the page for its head (see Template functions). An engine that writes its own tags gets the same links from app.Frontend.FeedLinks(r, view.Title), each a frontend.FeedLink with Type, Title and URL, Atom first. As with feedLinks, it is empty on pages without feeds and on error pages, where view.Status is 400 or higher, such as a category that does not exist; app.Frontend.FeedURL(r, "atom") is "" there too:

for _, link := range app.Frontend.FeedLinks(r, view.Title) {
    fmt.Fprintf(w, `<link rel="alternate" type="%s" title="%s" href="%s">`,
        html.EscapeString(link.Type), html.EscapeString(link.Title), html.EscapeString(link.URL))
}

Set Config.Translations to the translator frontend.Translations returns, and Config.Funcs, as you would for Go templates: the same translations and functions also serve components, e-mail, the labels of share links and profiles, and the names of months and days.

What the site gives up

Themes, components and e-mail are built on Go templates. With a renderer:

  • The site has no themes. The admin's Theme section is hidden, view.Theme is always default without values, and theme gives "", logged once as a template mistake (see Calls that find nothing).
  • /theme/ serves no files, and asset, assetScript and assetStyle give /theme/default/… addresses that answer 404, logged once as a template mistake; only core's files come from core: webthings.css, focal-points.css and partial-errors.css at /_/. With Config.Development such a call returns the mistake as its error. Serve CSS, JavaScript and images at /assets/ with Config.Assets or Config.ImportMap; both give each file a versioned address (importmap_url) and its tag (importmap_style, importmap_script), and the import map for the head (importmap), which maps go-partial's browser clients too; see Configuration and Themes.
  • Components render the modules' defaults, which a theme cannot replace. They have every template function and the site's translations.
  • E-mail uses the modules' default templates, translated with the site's translations.
  • Frontend.Execute has no templates to render.
  • Config.Development shows only the text of the error Render returns, on go-partial's plain error page, and there is no debug function (see Templates).
  • App.WriteTemplates still writes Go templates. They remain useful as a list of each template's data and fields.
  • Start checks no templates of the renderer (see Checking the templates at start), and core's head region is for Go templates: the renderer writes the tags of <head> itself, with feedLinks, apiLink and structuredData from frontend.TemplateFuncs.
  • App.Translations reads Go templates only: the modules' defaults, and Config.Templates when it is set.
  • HTMX requests get whatever the renderer writes; the built-in renderer sends the content template with the theme's regions, among them the tags of the head region, the theme's regions/head.gohtml or core's, which replace those of the page left in <head>, or a fragment alone (see HTMX).

A skeleton

This renderer draws every template with a Go function, as code generated by another engine would. It compiles against the current interface:

package main

import (
    "bytes"
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "html"
    "io"
    "log"
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "time"

    webthings "github.com/donseba/go-webthings"
    "github.com/donseba/go-webthings/frontend"
    "github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/publishing"
)

// Screen writes the HTML of one template.
type Screen func(w io.Writer, r *http.Request, view frontend.View) error

// Screens renders every template with a Go function. The keys are the
// template names: "page", "404", "search" and "<key>/<name>".
type Screens map[string]Screen

// Has reports whether the site has a template.
func (s Screens) Has(name string) bool {
    _, ok := s[name]

    return ok
}

// Render writes the whole page: the layout around the template.
func (s Screens) Render(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, name string, view frontend.View) error {
    screen, ok := s[name]
    if !ok {
        return fmt.Errorf("no template %q", name)
    }

    // Render into a buffer, so an error leaves no half page.
    var body bytes.Buffer

    if err := screen(&body, r, view); err != nil {
        return err
    }

    w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")

    _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"%s\">\n<title>%s</title>\n%s</html>\n",
        html.EscapeString(view.Locale), html.EscapeString(view.Site.Name), body.Bytes())

    return err
}

func page(w io.Writer, _ *http.Request, view frontend.View) error {
    page, ok := view.Content.(frontend.Page)
    if !ok {
        return fmt.Errorf("page: unexpected data %T", view.Content)
    }

    // Body is HTML already; everything else is escaped.
    _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "<main><h1>%s</h1>%s</main>", html.EscapeString(page.Title), page.Body)

    return err
}

func notFound(w io.Writer, _ *http.Request, view frontend.View) error {
    data, _ := view.Content.(frontend.NotFound)

    _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "<main><p>Not found. <a href=\"%s\">Home</a></p></main>", html.EscapeString(data.HomeURL))

    return err
}

func newsPost(w io.Writer, r *http.Request, view frontend.View) error {
    post, ok := view.Content.(publishing.Post)
    if !ok {
        return fmt.Errorf("news/post: unexpected data %T", view.Content)
    }

    funcs := frontend.TemplateFuncs(r.Context())
    date := funcs["date"].(func(time.Time, ...string) string)

    _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "<article><h1>%s</h1><p>%s</p>%s</article>",
        html.EscapeString(post.Title), html.EscapeString(date(post.Date, "long")), post.Body)

    return err
}

func main() {
    app := webthings.New(webthings.Config{
        Name: "My site",
        Renderer: Screens{
            "page":      page,
            "404":       notFound,
            "news/post": newsPost,
        },
        Assets: os.DirFS("static"),
    })

    if err := app.Use(publishing.Module("news", "News")); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    if err := app.ListenAndServe(context.Background(), ":8080"); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
}
